children.text: Chapter 92
ya āviveśa dvipado yaś catuṣpadas tebhyo agnibhyo hutam astv etat ||
children.translated_text: May this oblation be offered to those fires which have entered the two-footed and the four-footed beings.

children.text: ya indreṇa sarathaṃ yāti devo vaiśvānara uta viśvadāvyaḥ
children.translated_text: To the god who goes in the same chariot with <s>Indra</s>, to <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, and also to <s>Viśvadāvya</s>,

children.text: yaṃ johavīmi pṛtanāsu sāsahiṃ tebhyo agnibhyo hutam astv etat ||
children.translated_text: whom I call upon in battles as the overpowering one: may this oblation be offered to those fires.

children.text: yo devo viśvād yam u kāmam āhur yaṃ dātāraṃ pratigṛhṇantam āhuḥ
children.translated_text: To the god whom they call 'belonging to all,' whom indeed they call desire, whom they call the giver and the receiver,

children.text: yo dhīraḥ śakraḥ paribhūr adābhyas tebhyo agnibhyo hutam astv etat ||
children.translated_text: who is wise, mighty, all-surrounding, and not to be deceived: may this oblation be offered to those fires.

children.text: yaṃ tvā hotāraṃ manasābhi saṃvidus trayodaśa bhauvanāḥ pañca mānavāḥ
children.translated_text: You whom the thirteen <s>Bhauvanas</s> and the five <s>Mānavas</s> have recognized in their mind as the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest,

children.text: varcodhase yaśase sūnṛtāvate tebhyo agnibhyo hutam astv etat ||
children.translated_text: for brilliance, fame, and gracious speech: may this oblation be offered to those fires.

children.text: ukṣānnāya vaśānnāya somapṛṣṭhāya vedhase
children.translated_text: For those whose food is the bull, whose food is the barren cow, whose back is <s>Soma</s>, for the ordainers,

children.text: vaiśvānarajyeṣṭhebhyas tebhyo agnibhyo hutam astv etat ||
children.translated_text: for those whose eldest is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>: may this oblation be offered to those fires.

children.text: divaṃ pṛthivīm anv antarikṣam ye vidyutam anusaṃcaranti
children.translated_text: Those who move along through heaven, earth, and the midspace, who follow the lightning,

children.text: ye dikṣv antar ye vāte antas tebhyo agnibhyo hutam astv etat ||
children.translated_text: those who are within the directions, or who are within the wind: may this oblation be offered to those fires.

children.text: hiraṇyapāṇiṃ savitāram indraṃ bṛhaspatiṃ varuṇaṃ mitram agnim
children.translated_text: We call upon golden-handed <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, and <s>Agni</s>,

children.text: viśvān devān aṅgiraso havāmahe imaṃ kravyādaṃ śamayantv agnim ||
children.translated_text: all the gods and the <s>Aṅgirases</s>; may they quiet this corpse-eating <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: śānto agniḥ kravyācchāntaḥ puruṣareṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Appeased is <s>Agni</s> the corpse-eater; appeased is the one who harms men.

children.text: atho yo viśvadāvyas taṃ kravyādam aśīśamam ||
children.translated_text: And that <s>Viśvadāvya</s>, the corpse-eater, I have caused to be appeased.

children.text: ye parvatāḥ somapṛṣṭhā āpa uttānaśīvarīḥ
children.translated_text: The mountains with <s>Soma</s> on their backs, the waters lying open,

children.text: vātaḥ parjanya ād agnis te kravyādam aśīśaman ||
children.translated_text: the wind, <s>Parjanya</s>, and <s>Agni</s>: let them appease the corpse-eater.

children.text: Chapter 93
hastivarcasaṃ prathatāṃ bṛhad yaśo adityā yat tanvaḥ saṃbabhūva
children.translated_text: May elephant-like brilliance spread out, great fame, that which was born from the body of <s>Aditi</s>.

children.text: tat sarve sam adur mahyam etad viśve devā aditiḥ sajoṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All the gods have together given that to me, the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> with <s>Aditi</s> in accord.

children.text: mitraś ca varuṇaś cendro rudraś ca cetatu
children.translated_text: Let <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Rudra</s> take notice,

children.text: devāso viśvadhāyasas te māñjantu varcasā ||
children.translated_text: and let the all-sustaining gods anoint me with brilliance.

children.text: yena hastī varcasā saṃbabhūva yena rājā manuṣyeṣv apsv antaḥ
children.translated_text: By the brilliance by which the elephant came into being, by which the king is powerful among men and within the waters,

children.text: yena devā devatām agra āyan tena mām adya varcasāgne varcasvinaṃ kṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: by which the gods first went to godhead, by that brilliance, <s>Agni</s>, make me brilliant today.

children.text: yat te varco jātavedo bṛhad bhavaty āhuteḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever great brilliance of yours, <s>Jātavedas</s>, arises from the oblation,

children.text: yāvat sūryasya varca āsurasya ca hastinaḥ
children.translated_text: as much as is the brilliance of the sun and of the mighty elephant,

children.text: tāvan me aśvinā varca ā dhattāṃ puṣkarasrajā ||
children.translated_text: so much brilliance may the two <s>Aśvins</s>, lotus-garlanded, place in me.

children.text: yāvac catasraḥ pradiśaś cakṣur yāvat samaśnute
children.translated_text: As far as the four quarters extend, as far as sight reaches,

children.text: tāvat samaitv indriyaṃ mayi taddhastivarcasam ||
children.translated_text: so far let power come together in me, that elephant-like brilliance.

children.text: hastī mṛgāṇāṃ suṣadām atiṣṭhāvān babhūva hi
children.translated_text: For the elephant has become superior among wild animals and among those well seated.

children.text: tasya bhagena varcasābhi ṣiñcāmi mām aham ||
children.translated_text: With his share and his brilliance I sprinkle myself.

children.text: Chapter 94
yena vehad babhūvitha nāśayāmasi tat tvat
children.translated_text: That by which you became barren, we drive that away from you.

children.text: idaṃ tad anyatra tvad apa dūre ni dadhmasi ||
children.translated_text: This thing we set down elsewhere, far away from you.

children.text: ā te yoniṃ garbha etu pumān bāṇa iveṣudhim
children.translated_text: May a male embryo enter your womb, like an arrow into a quiver.

children.text: ā vīro 'tra jāyatāṃ putras te daśamāsyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: May a hero be born here, your son after ten months.

children.text: pumāṃsaṃ putraṃ janaya taṃ pumān anu jāyatām
children.translated_text: Give birth to a male son; after him let a male be born.

children.text: bhavāsi putrāṇāṃ mātā jātānāṃ janayāś ca yān ||
children.translated_text: May you be the mother of sons already born and of those whom you will bear.

children.text: yāni bhadrāṇi bījāny ṛṣabhā janayanti ca
children.translated_text: With those auspicious seeds which the bulls beget,

children.text: tais tvaṃ putraṃ vindasva sā prasūr dhenukā bhava ||
children.translated_text: with them obtain a son; be a fruitful, milch-cow-like mother.

children.text: kṛṇomi te prājāpatyam ā yoniṃ garbha etu te
children.translated_text: I make for you what belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>; may the embryo enter your womb.

children.text: vindasva tvaṃ putraṃ nāri yas tubhyaṃ śam asaccham u tasmai tvam bhava ||
children.translated_text: Obtain a son, woman; may he be a blessing to you, and you be a blessing to him.

children.text: yāsām dyauḥ pitā pṛthivī mātā samudro mūlaṃ vīrudhāṃ babhūva
children.translated_text: Those divine herbs of which heaven was the father, earth the mother, and the ocean the root of the plants,

children.text: tās tvā putravidyāya daivīḥ prāvantv oṣadhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may they aid you for the gaining of a son.

children.text: Chapter 95
payasvatīr oṣadhayaḥ payasvan māmakaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Milk-rich are the herbs, and milk-rich is this speech of mine.

children.text: atho payasvatīnām ā bhare 'haṃ sahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And of the milk-rich ones I bring here thousands upon thousands.

children.text: vedāhaṃ payasvantaṃ cakāra dhānyam bahu
children.translated_text: I know the milk-rich god, who made much grain,

children.text: saṃbhṛtvā nāma yo devas taṃ vayaṃ havāmahe yoyo ayajvano gṛhe ||
children.translated_text: the one named <s>Saṃbhṛtvan</s>; we call upon him, even in the house of each non-sacrificer.

children.text: imā yāḥ pañca pradiśo mānavīḥ pañca kṛṣṭayaḥ
children.translated_text: These five human directions, the five peoples,

children.text: vṛṣṭe śāpaṃ nadīr iveha sphātiṃ samāvahān ||
children.translated_text: like rivers when rain has fallen, let them bring increase here together.

children.text: ud utsaṃ śatadhāraṃ sahasradhāram akṣitam
children.translated_text: Raise up an unfailing spring with a hundred streams, with a thousand streams.

children.text: evāsmākedaṃ dhānyaṃ sahasradhāram akṣitam ||
children.translated_text: So may this grain of ours be unfailing, with a thousand streams.

children.text: śatahasta samāhara sahasrahasta saṃ kira
children.translated_text: With a hundred hands gather it; with a thousand hands scatter it abroad.

children.text: kṛtasya kāryasya ceha sphātiṃ samāvaha ||
children.translated_text: Bring here increase for what has been done and what is still to be done.

children.text: tisro mātrā gandharvāṇāṃ catasro gṛhapatnyāḥ
children.translated_text: There are three measures of the <s>Gandharvas</s> and four of the mistress of the house.

children.text: tāsāṃ yā sphātimattamā tayā tvābhi mṛśāmasi ||
children.translated_text: With the one among them fullest of increase, with that we touch you.

children.text: upohaś ca samūhaś ca kṣattārau te prajāpate
children.translated_text: <s>Upoha</s> and <s>Samūha</s> are your two attendants, O <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: tāv ihā vahatāṃ sphātiṃ bahuṃ bhūmānam akṣitam ||
children.translated_text: Let those two bring hither increase, much abundance, unfailing.

children.text: Chapter 96
uttudas tvot tudatu mā dhṛthāḥ śayane sve
children.translated_text: Let the rouser rouse you; do not remain lying on your own bed.

children.text: iṣuḥ kāmasya yā bhīmā tayā vidhyāmi tvā hṛdi ||
children.translated_text: With the terrible arrow of <s>Kāma</s> I pierce you in the heart.

children.text: ādhīparṇāṃ kāmaśalyām iṣuṃ saṃkalpakulmalām
children.translated_text: The arrow feathered with longing, barbed with desire, with resolve as its socket,

children.text: tāṃ susaṃnatāṃ kṛtvā kāmo vidhyatu tvā hṛdi ||
children.translated_text: having made that well-bent, let <s>Kāma</s> pierce you in the heart.

children.text: yā plīhānaṃ śoṣayati kāmasyeṣuḥ susaṃnatā
children.translated_text: The well-bent arrow of <s>Kāma</s>, which dries up the spleen,

children.text: prācīnapakṣā vyoṣā tayā vidhyāmi tvā hṛdi ||
children.translated_text: with forward-pointing feathers, burning: with that I pierce you in the heart.

children.text: śucā viddhā vyoṣayā śuṣkāsyābhi sarpa mā
children.translated_text: Pierced with heat, burning, dry-mouthed, crawl toward me,

children.text: mṛdur nimanyuḥ kevalī priyavādiny anuvratā ||
children.translated_text: gentle, free from anger, alone, speaking lovingly, and obedient.

children.text: ājāmi tvājanyā pari mātur atho pituḥ
children.translated_text: I draw you, well-born woman, away from your mother and also from your father,

children.text: yathā mama kratāv aso mama cittam upāyasi ||
children.translated_text: so that you may be within my will and come into my thought.

children.text: vy asyai mitrāvaruṇau hṛdaś cittāny asyatam
children.translated_text: Let <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> cast away from her heart her thoughts.

children.text: athainām akratuṃ kṛtvā mamaiva kṛṇutaṃ vaśe ||
children.translated_text: Then, making her without will, bring her under my control alone.

children.text: Chapter 97
ye 'syāṃ stha prācyāṃ diśi hetayo nāma devās teṣāṃ vo agnir iṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: You who are in this eastern direction, gods named missiles: <s>Agni</s> is your arrows.

children.text: te no mṛḍata te no 'dhi brūta tebhyo vo namas tebhyo vaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Be gracious to us; speak in our favor. To you there is homage; to you, svāhā.

children.text: ye 'syāṃ stha dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśy aviṣyavo nāma devās teṣāṃ vaḥ kāma iṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: Those of you who are in this southern direction, gods named <s>Aviṣyava</s>: your arrows are desire.

children.text: te no mṛḍata te no 'dhi brūta tebhyo vo namas tebhyo vaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Be gracious to us; speak in our favor. To you homage; to you <s>svāhā</s>.

children.text: ye 'syāṃ stha pratīcyāṃ diśi vairājā nāma devās teṣāṃ va āpa iṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: Those of you who are in this western direction, gods named <s>Vairāja</s>: your arrows are the waters.

children.text: te no mṛḍata te no 'dhi brūta tebhyo vo namas tebhyo vaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Be gracious to us; speak in our favor. To you homage; to you <s>svāhā</s>.

children.text: ye 'syāṃ sthodīcyāṃ diśi pravidhyanto nāma devās teṣāṃ vo vāta iṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: Those of you who are in this northern direction, gods named <s>Pravidhyanta</s>: your arrows are the wind.

children.text: te no mṛḍata te no 'dhi brūta tebhyo vo namas tebhyo vaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Be gracious to us; speak in our favor. To you homage; to you <s>svāhā</s>.

children.text: ye 'syāṃ stha dhruvāyāṃ diśi nilimpā nāma devās teṣāṃ va oṣadhīr iṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: Those of you who are in this fixed direction, gods named <s>Nilimpa</s>: your arrows are the plants.

children.text: te no mṛḍata te no 'dhi brūta tebhyo vo namas tebhyo vaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Be gracious to us; speak in our favor. To you homage; to you <s>svāhā</s>.

children.text: ye 'syāṃ sthordhvāyāṃ diśy avasvanto nāma devās teṣāṃ vo bṛhaspatir iṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: Those of you who are in this upward direction, gods named <s>Avasvant</s>: your arrows are <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: te no mṛḍata te no 'dhi brūta tebhyo vo namas tebhyo vaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Be gracious to us; speak in our favor. To you homage; to you <s>svāhā</s>.

children.text: Chapter 98
prācī dig agnir adhipatir asito rakṣitādityā iṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: The eastern direction: <s>Agni</s> is its overlord, <s>Asita</s> its protector, and the <s>Ādityas</s> its arrows.

children.text: tebhyo namo 'dhipatibhyo namo rakṣitṛbhyo nama iṣubhyo nama ebhyo astu
children.translated_text: Homage to those overlords, homage to the protectors, homage to the arrows; homage to these beings.

children.text: yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmas taṃ vo jambhe dadhmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever hates us, and whomever we hate, we place him in your jaws.

children.text: dakṣiṇā dig indro 'dhipatis tiraścirājī rakṣitā pitara iṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: The southern direction: <s>Indra</s> is its overlord, <s>Tiraścirājī</s> its protector, and the Fathers its arrows.

children.text: tebhyo namo 'dhipatibhyo namo rakṣitṛbhyo nama iṣubhyo nama ebhyo astu
children.translated_text: Homage to those overlords, homage to the protectors, homage to the arrows; homage to these beings.

children.text: yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmas taṃ vo jambhe dadhmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever hates us, and whomever we hate, we place him in your jaws.

children.text: pratīcī dig varuṇo 'dhipatiḥ pṛdākū rakṣitānnam iṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: The western direction: <s>Varuṇa</s> is its overlord, <s>Pṛdākū</s> its protector, and food its arrows.

children.text: tebhyo namo 'dhipatibhyo namo rakṣitṛbhyo nama iṣubhyo nama ebhyo astu
children.translated_text: Homage to those overlords, homage to the protectors, homage to the arrows; homage to these beings.

children.text: yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmas taṃ vo jambhe dadhmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever hates us, and whomever we hate, we place him in your jaws.

children.text: udīcī dik somo 'dhipatiḥ svajo rakṣitāśanir iṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: The northern direction: <s>Soma</s> is its overlord, <s>Svaja</s> its protector, and the thunderbolt its arrows.

children.text: tebhyo namo 'dhipatibhyo namo rakṣitṛbhyo nama iṣubhyo nama ebhyo astu
children.translated_text: Homage to those overlords, homage to the protectors, homage to the arrows; homage to these beings.

children.text: yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmas taṃ vo jambhe dadhmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever hates us, and whomever we hate, we place him in your jaws.

children.text: dhruvā dig viṣṇur adhipatiḥ kalmāṣagrīvo rakṣitā vīrudha iṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: The fixed direction: <s>Viṣṇu</s> is its overlord, <s>Kalmāṣagrīva</s> its protector, and the plants its arrows.

children.text: tebhyo namo 'dhipatibhyo namo rakṣitṛbhyo nama iṣubhyo nama ebhyo astu
children.translated_text: Homage to those overlords, homage to the protectors, homage to the arrows; homage to these beings.

children.text: yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayam dviṣmas taṃ vo jambhe dadhmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever hates us, and whomever we hate, we place him in your jaws.

children.text: ūrdhvā dig bṛhaspatir adhipatiḥ śvitro rakṣitā varṣam iṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: The upward direction: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is its overlord, <s>Śvitra</s> its protector, and rain its arrows.

children.text: tebhyo namo 'dhipatibhyo namo rakṣitṛbhyo nama iṣubhyo nama ebhyo astu
children.translated_text: Homage to those overlords, homage to the protectors, homage to the arrows; homage to these beings.

children.text: yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmas taṃ vo jambhe dadhmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever hates us, and whomever we hate, we place him in your jaws.

children.text: Chapter 99
ekaikayaiṣā sṛṣṭyā saṃ babhūva yatra gā asṛjanta bhūtakṛto viśvarūpāḥ
children.translated_text: With each separate creation she came into being, where the makers of beings created cattle of every form.

children.text: yatra vijāyate yaminy apartuḥ sā paśūn kṣiṇāti riphatī ruśatī ||
children.translated_text: Where <s>Yaminī</s> is born out of season, she wastes the cattle away, tearing and shining red.

children.text: eṣā paśūnt saṃ kṣiṇāti kravyād bhūtvā vyadvarī
children.translated_text: This one wastes the cattle away, becoming a flesh-eater and a maimer.

children.text: utaināṃ brahmaṇe dadyāt tathā syonā śivā syāt ||
children.translated_text: But one should give her to a brahman; then she will become favorable and auspicious.

children.text: śivā bhava puruṣebhyo gobhyo aśvebhyaḥ śivā
children.translated_text: Be auspicious for men, auspicious for cows, auspicious for horses.

children.text: śivāsmai sarvasmai kṣetrāya śivā na ihaidhi ||
children.translated_text: Be auspicious for this whole field; come here to us auspiciously.

children.text: iha puṣṭir iha rasa iha sahasrasātamā bhava
children.translated_text: Here be nourishment; here be sap. Here be most productive of a thousandfold gain.

children.text: paśūn yamini poṣaya ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Yaminī</s>, make the cattle prosper.

children.text: yatrā suhārdaḥ sukṛto madanti vihāya rogaṃ tanvaḥ svāyāḥ
children.translated_text: Where friends, men of good deeds, rejoice, having left behind sickness of their own bodies,

children.text: taṃ lokaṃ yaminy abhisaṃbabhūva sā no mā hiṃsīt puruṣān paśūṃś ca ||
children.translated_text: that world <s>Yaminī</s> has reached; may she not harm our men and cattle.

children.text: yatrā suhārdāṃ sukṛtām agnihotrahutām yatra lokaḥ
children.translated_text: Where the world of friends, of men of good deeds, of those who have offered the <s>agnihotra</s> oblation is,

children.text: taṃ lokaṃ yaminy abhisaṃbabhūva sā no mā hiṃsīt puruṣān paśūṃś ca ||
children.translated_text: that world <s>Yaminī</s> has reached; may she not harm our men and cattle.

children.text: Chapter 100
yad rājāno vibhajanta iṣṭāpūrtasya ṣoḍaśam yamasyāmī sabhāsadaḥ
children.translated_text: When the kings, companions and courtiers of <s>Yama</s>, divide a sixteenth part of the works of sacrifice and public benefaction,

children.text: avis tasmāt pra muñcati dattaḥ śitipāt svadhā ||
children.translated_text: a given white-footed sheep releases one from that; <s>svadhā</s>.

children.text: sarvān kāmān pūrayaty ābhavan prabhavan bhavan
children.translated_text: It fulfills all desires, coming into being, arising, existing.

children.text: ākūtipro 'vir dattaḥ śitipānn nopa dasyati ||
children.translated_text: A given white-footed sheep, satisfying intention, does not fail.

children.text: yo dadāti śitipādam aviṃ lokena saṃmitam
children.translated_text: He who gives a white-footed sheep, commensurate with the world,

children.text: sa nākam abhyārohati yatra śulko na kriyate abalena balīyase ||
children.translated_text: ascends to heaven, where no toll is taken by the stronger from the weaker.

children.text: pañcāpūpaṃ śitipādam aviṃ lokena saṃmitam
children.translated_text: A white-footed sheep with five cakes, commensurate with the world:

children.text: pradātopa jīvati pitṝṇāṃ loke 'kṣitam ||
children.translated_text: the giver lives upon it in the world of the Fathers, inexhaustibly.

children.text: pañcāpūpaṃ śitipādam aviṃ lokena saṃmitam
children.translated_text: A white-footed sheep with five cakes, commensurate with the world:

children.text: pradātopa jīvati sūryāmāsayor akṣitam ||
children.translated_text: the giver lives upon it in the world of sun and moon, inexhaustibly.

children.text: ireva nopa dasyati samudra iva payo mahat
children.translated_text: It does not fail, like refreshment, like the great milk in the ocean.

children.text: devau savāsināv iva śitipān nopa dasyati ||
children.translated_text: Like two gods dwelling together, the white-footed one does not fail.

children.text: ka idaṃ kasmā adāt kāmaḥ kāmāyādāt
children.translated_text: Who gave this, and to whom? Desire gave it to desire.

children.text: kāmo dātā kāmaḥ pratigrahītā kāmaḥ samudram ā viveśa
children.translated_text: Desire is the giver; desire is the receiver. Desire has entered into the ocean.

children.text: kāmena tvā prati gṛhṇāmi kāmaitat te ||
children.translated_text: With desire I receive you. O desire, this is yours.

children.text: bhūmiṣ ṭvā prati gṛhṇātv antarikṣam idaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: May the earth receive you; may this great midspace receive you.

children.text: māhaṃ prāṇena mātmanā mā prajayā pratigṛhya vi rādhiṣi ||
children.translated_text: May I not, after receiving, be deprived of breath, of self, or of offspring.

children.text: Chapter 101
sahṛdayaṃ sāṃmanasyam avidveṣaṃ kṛṇomi vaḥ
children.translated_text: I make you of one heart, of one mind, free from hatred.

children.text: anyo anyam abhi haryata vatsaṃ jātam ivāghnyā ||
children.translated_text: Show affection to one another, as the inviolable cow does to her newborn calf.

children.text: anuvrataḥ pituḥ putro mātrā bhavatu saṃmanāḥ
children.translated_text: Let the son be obedient to the father and of one mind with the mother.

children.text: jāyā patye madhumatīṃ vācaṃ vadatu śantivām ||
children.translated_text: Let the wife speak to her husband a honey-sweet, peace-bringing word.

children.text: mā bhrātā bhrātaraṃ dvikṣan mā svasāram uta svasā
children.translated_text: Let brother not hate brother, nor sister hate sister.

children.text: samyañcaḥ savratā bhūtvā vācaṃ vadata bhadrayā ||
children.translated_text: Having become united and sharing one vow, speak words that are auspicious.

children.text: yena devā na viyanti no ca vidviṣate mithaḥ
children.translated_text: By that by which the gods do not go apart, nor hate one another,

children.text: tat kṛṇmo brahma vo gṛhe saṃjñānaṃ puruṣebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: we make that <s>brahman</s> for you in your house, a common understanding among the people.

children.text: jyāyasvantaś cittino mā vi yauṣṭa saṃrādhayantaḥ sadhurāś carantaḥ
children.translated_text: Be rich in elders and thoughtful; do not separate, but be successful, moving together under one yoke.

children.text: anyo anyasmai valgu vadanta eta sadhrīcīnān vaḥ saṃmanasas kṛṇomi ||
children.translated_text: Speaking pleasantly to one another, come here; I make you go together, of one mind.

children.text: samānī prapā saha vo 'nnabhāgaḥ samāne yoktre saha vo yunajmi
children.translated_text: Let your watering place be common, and your share of food together; I yoke you together in the same harness.

children.text: samyañco 'gniṃ saparyatārā nābhim ivābhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: United, serve <s>Agni</s> all around, as spokes around the nave.

children.text: sadhrīcīnān vaḥ saṃmanasas kṛṇomy ekaśnuṣṭīnt saṃvananena sarvān
children.translated_text: I make you go together, of one mind, all of one resolve through the charm of attraction.

children.text: devā ivāmṛtaṃ rakṣamāṇāḥ sāyaṃprātaḥ saumanaso vo astu ||
children.translated_text: Like the gods guarding immortality, may good-mindedness be yours evening and morning.

children.text: Chapter 102
vi devā jarasāvṛtan vi tvam agne arātyā
children.translated_text: The gods have separated from old age; you, <s>Agni</s>, from hostility.

children.text: vy ahaṃ sarveṇa pāpmanā vi yakṣmeṇa sam āyuṣā ||
children.translated_text: I separate myself from every evil, from wasting disease, together with life-span.

children.text: vy ārtyā pavamāno vi śakraḥ pāpakṛtyayā
children.translated_text: <s>Pavamāna</s> separates from distress; <s>Śakra</s> from evil-doing.

children.text: vy ahaṃ sarveṇa pāpmanā vi yakṣmeṇa sam āyuṣā ||
children.translated_text: I separate myself from every evil, from wasting disease, together with life-span.

children.text: vi grāmyāḥ paśava āraṇyair vy āpas tṛṣṇayāsaran
children.translated_text: Domestic animals have gone apart from wild ones; the waters have flowed apart from thirst.

children.text: vy ahaṃ sarveṇa pāpmanā vi yakṣmeṇa sam āyuṣā ||
children.translated_text: I separate myself from every evil, from wasting disease, together with life-span.

children.text: vī me dyāvāpṛthivī ito vi panthāno diśaṃ diśam
children.translated_text: For me heaven and earth are apart from here; the paths are apart in every direction.

children.text: vy ahaṃ sarveṇa pāpmanā vi yakṣmeṇa sam āyuṣā ||
children.translated_text: I separate myself from every evil, from wasting disease, together with life-span.

children.text: tvaṣṭā duhitre vahatuṃ yunaktītīdaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ vi yāti
children.translated_text: <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> yokes the wedding-carriage for his daughter; thus this whole world goes apart.

children.text: vy ahaṃ sarveṇa pāpmanā vi yakṣmeṇa sam āyuṣā ||
children.translated_text: I separate myself from every evil, from wasting disease, together with life-span.

children.text: agniḥ prāṇānt saṃ dadhāti candraḥ prāṇena saṃhitaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> joins together the vital breaths; the moon is joined with breath.

children.text: vy ahaṃ sarveṇa pāpmanā vi yakṣmeṇa sam āyuṣā ||
children.translated_text: I separate myself from every evil, from wasting disease, together with life-span.

children.text: prāṇena viśvatovīryaṃ devāḥ sūryaṃ sam airayan
children.translated_text: By breath the gods set the sun in motion, full of power on every side.

children.text: vy ahaṃ sarveṇa pāpmanā vi yakṣmeṇa sam āyuṣā ||
children.translated_text: I separate myself from every evil, from wasting disease, together with life-span.

children.text: āyuṣmatām āyuṣkṛtāṃ prāṇena jīva mā mṛthāḥ
children.translated_text: With the breath of the long-lived and of those who make long life, live; do not die.

children.text: vy ahaṃ sarveṇa pāpmanā vi yakṣmeṇa sam āyuṣā ||
children.translated_text: I separate myself from every evil, from wasting disease, together with life-span.

children.text: prāṇena prāṇatāṃ prāṇehaiva bhava mā mṛthāḥ
children.translated_text: With breath among those who breathe, be here in breath itself; do not die.

children.text: vy ahaṃ sarveṇa pāpmanā vi yakṣmeṇa sam āyuṣā ||
children.translated_text: I separate myself from every evil, from wasting disease, together with life-span.

children.text: ud āyuṣā sam āyuṣod oṣadhīnāṃ rasena
children.translated_text: Rise up with life-span, together with life-span, up with the sap of the plants.

children.text: vy ahaṃ sarveṇa pāpmanā vi yakṣmeṇa sam āyuṣā ||
children.translated_text: I separate myself from every evil, from wasting disease, together with life-span.

children.text: ā parjanyasya vṛṣṭyod asthāmāmṛtā vayam
children.translated_text: By the rain of <s>Parjanya</s> we have risen up, immortal.

children.text: vy ahaṃ sarveṇa pāpmanā vi yakṣmeṇa sam āyuṣā ||
children.translated_text: I separate myself from every evil, from wasting disease, together with life-span.

children.text: Chapter 103
brahma jajñānaṃ prathamaṃ purastād vi sīmataḥ suruco vena āvaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s>, born first in the east, has shone forth from the boundary, bright and lovely.

children.text: sa budhnyā upamā asya viṣṭhāḥ sataś ca yonim asataś ca vi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He has opened up its lowest and highest stations, the womb of being and of non-being.

children.text: iyaṃ pitryā rāṣṭry etv agre prathamāya januṣe bhuvaneṣṭhāḥ
children.translated_text: Let this ancestral, sovereign one go forward, first for the first birth, established among beings.

children.text: tasmā etaṃ surucaṃ hvāram ahyaṃ gharmaṃ śrīṇantu prathamāya dhāsyave ||
children.translated_text: For him let them heat this bright, slanting gharma for me, for the first one who is to be established.

children.text: pra yo jajñe vidvān asya bandhur viśvā devānāṃ janimā vivakti
children.translated_text: He who was born forth, the wise one, its kinsman, proclaims all the births of the gods.

children.text: brahma brahmaṇa uj jabhāra madhyān nīcair uccaiḥ svadhā abhi pra tasthau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> raised <s>brahman</s> up from the midst of <s>brahman</s>; low and high, by its own power, it took its stand.

children.text: sa hi vidaḥ sa pṛthivyā ṛtasthā mahī kṣemaṃ rodasī askabhāyat
children.translated_text: For he is the knower, the maintainer of truth upon the earth; he propped apart the great secure heaven and earth.

children.text: mahān mahī askabhāyad vi jāto dyāṃ sadma pārthivaṃ ca rajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Great and widely born, he propped up the great one, the heavenly seat and the earthly realm.

children.text: sa budhnyād āṣṭra januṣo 'bhy agram bṛhaspatir devatā tasya samrāṭ
children.translated_text: From the depth, from the lineage, toward the beginning, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is its deity and sovereign.

children.text: ahar yacchukraṃ jyotiṣo janiṣṭātha dyumanto vi vasantu viprāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the bright day was born from light, then let the inspired singers dwell resplendent.

children.text: nūnaṃ tad asya kāvyo hinoti maho devasya pūrvyasya dhāma
children.translated_text: Now his poetic power impels that ancient dwelling of the great god.

children.text: eṣa jajñe bahubhiḥ sākam itthā pūrve ardhe viṣite sasan nu ||
children.translated_text: This one was born thus together with many, seated in the earlier half when it was loosened.

children.text: yo 'tharvāṇaṃ pitaraṃ devabandhuṃ bṛhaspatiṃ namasāva ca gacchāt
children.translated_text: Whoever comes with reverence to father <s>Atharvan</s>, kinsman of the gods, and to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,

children.text: tvaṃ viśveṣāṃ janitā yathāsaḥ kavir devo na dabhāyat svadhāvān ||
children.translated_text: as you are the begetter of all, a seer, a god, not to be deceived, self-powered.

children.text: Chapter 104
ya ātmadā baladā yasya viśva upāsate praśiṣaṃ yasya devāḥ
children.translated_text: He who gives soul, who gives strength, whose command all the gods revere,

children.text: yo 'syeśe dvipado yaś catuṣpadaḥ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
children.translated_text: who rules over this two-footed and four-footed world: to which god shall we offer with oblation?

children.text: yaḥ prāṇato nimiṣato mahitvaiko rājā jagato babhūva
children.translated_text: He who, by his greatness, alone became king of the breathing and blinking world,

children.text: yasya chāyāmṛtaṃ yasya mṛtyuḥ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
children.translated_text: whose shadow is immortality, whose shadow is death: to which god shall we offer with oblation?

children.text: yaṃ krandasī avataś caskabhāne bhiyasāne rodasī ahvayethām
children.translated_text: Whom the two roaring worlds called upon when, trembling, they were upheld from below,

children.text: yasyāsau panthā rajaso vimānaḥ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
children.translated_text: whose path is the measure of the airy realm: to which god shall we offer with oblation?

children.text: yasya dyaur urvī pṛthivī ca mahī yasyāda urv antarikṣam
children.translated_text: Whose is the broad heaven and the great earth, whose is this wide midspace,

children.text: yasyāsau sūro vitato mahitvā kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
children.translated_text: whose is that sun stretched out by greatness: to which god shall we offer with oblation?

children.text: yasya viśve himavanto mahitvā samudre yasya rasām id āhuḥ
children.translated_text: By whose greatness all the snowy mountains exist, and whose essence they call the ocean,

children.text: imāś ca pradiśo yasya bāhū kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
children.translated_text: whose arms are these quarters of space: to which god shall we offer with oblation?

children.text: āpo agre viśvam āvan garbhaṃ dadhānā amṛtā ṛtajñāḥ
children.translated_text: In the beginning the waters protected the whole, bearing the embryo, immortal and knowing the truth.

children.text: yāsu devīṣv adhi deva āsīt kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
children.translated_text: Among those divine waters the god was seated: to which god shall we offer with oblation?

children.text: hiraṇyagarbhaḥ sam avartatāgre bhūtasya jātaḥ patir eka āsīt
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> arose in the beginning; born, he was the one lord of what exists.

children.text: sa dādhāra pṛthivīm uta dyāṃ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
children.translated_text: He supported the earth and also heaven: to which god shall we offer with oblation?

children.text: āpo vatsaṃ janayantīr garbham agre sam airayan
children.translated_text: The waters, generating the calf, set the embryo in motion in the beginning.

children.text: tasyota jāyamānasyolba āsīddhiraṇyayaḥ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
children.translated_text: And for him as he was being born, the caul was golden: to which god shall we offer with oblation?

children.text: Chapter 105
ud itas trayo akraman vyāghraḥ puruṣo vṛkaḥ
children.translated_text: From here three have stepped away: the tiger, the man, and the wolf.

children.text: hirugghi yanti sindhavo hirug devo vanaspatir hiruṅ namantu śatravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the rivers go far away, let the divine tree go far away, let the enemies bow down far away.

children.text: pareṇaitu pathā vṛkaḥ parameṇota taskaraḥ
children.translated_text: Let the wolf go by the farther path, and the thief by the farthest one.

children.text: pareṇa datvatī rajjuḥ pareṇāghāyur arṣatu ||
children.translated_text: Let the toothed noose pass by a farther way; let the ill-wisher go by a farther way.

children.text: akṣyau ca te mukhaṃ ca te vyāghra jambhayāmasi
children.translated_text: Your eyes and your mouth, O tiger, we benumb and make gape.

children.text: āt sarvān viṃśatiṃ nakhān ||
children.translated_text: And then all your twenty claws as well.

children.text: vyāghraṃ datvatāṃ vayaṃ prathamaṃ jambhayāmasi
children.translated_text: We first benumb the tiger among the toothed creatures.

children.text: ād u ṣṭenam atho ahiṃ yātudhānam atho vṛkam ||
children.translated_text: Then the thief, and also the serpent, the sorcerer, and the wolf.

children.text: yo adya stena āyati sa sampiṣṭo apāyati
children.translated_text: The thief who comes today goes away crushed.

children.text: pathām apadhvaṃsenaitv indro vajreṇa hantu tam ||
children.translated_text: Let him go by the ruin of the roads; may <s>Indra</s> strike him with the thunderbolt.

children.text: mūrṇā mṛgasya dantā apiśīrṇā u pṛṣṭayaḥ
children.translated_text: The animal's teeth are broken at the head, and its backs are shattered.

children.text: nimruk te godhā bhavatu nīcāyacchaśayur mṛgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: May your lurking lizard sink down; may the beast lie low, turned downward.

children.text: yat saṃyamo na vi yamo vi yamo yan na saṃyamaḥ
children.translated_text: What is restraint and not release, what is release and not restraint,

children.text: indrajāḥ somajā ātharvaṇam asi vyāghrajambhanam ||
children.translated_text: born of <s>Indra</s>, born of <s>Soma</s>, you are the <s>Atharvan</s> tiger-benumbing charm.

children.text: Chapter 106
yāṃ tvā gandharvo akhanad varuṇāya mṛtabhraje
children.translated_text: You whom a <s>Gandharva</s> dug up for <s>Varuṇa</s>, for the dead-bound one,

children.text: tāṃ tvā vayaṃ khanāmasy oṣadhiṃ śepaharṣaṇīm ||
children.translated_text: that very herb we dig up, the herb that arouses the male member.

children.text: ud uṣā ud u sūrya ud idaṃ māmakaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Up has <s>Uṣas</s> risen, up has <s>Sūrya</s> risen, up has this speech of mine risen.

children.text: ud ejatu prajāpatir vṛṣā śuṣmeṇa vājinā ||
children.translated_text: Let <s>Prajāpati</s> rise up, a bull with force, with vigorous strength.

children.text: yathā sma te virohato 'bhitaptam ivānati
children.translated_text: As, when it grows forth for you, it bends like something heated,

children.text: tatas te śuṣmavattaram iyaṃ kṛṇotv oṣadhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: so may this herb make it still more full of force for you.

children.text: ucchuṣmauṣadhīnāṃ sārā ṛṣabhāṇām
children.translated_text: The heat-raising essence of the herbs, the essence of the bulls,

children.text: saṃ puṃsām indra vṛṣṇyam asmin dhehi tanūvaśin ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Indra</s>, place the virile power of males in this body-governing one.

children.text: apāṃ rasaḥ prathamajo 'tho vanaspatīnām
children.translated_text: The sap of the waters, first-born, and also the sap of the forest trees,

children.text: uta somasya bhrātāsy utārśam asi vṛṣṇyam ||
children.translated_text: and you are the brother of <s>Soma</s>; you are virility and ardor.

children.text: adyāgne adya savitar adya devi sarasvati
children.translated_text: Today, O <s>Agni</s>, today, O <s>Savitṛ</s>, today, O goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: adyāsya brahmaṇaspate dhanur ivā tānayā pasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: today, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>, stretch his member like a bow.

children.text: āhaṃ tanomi te paso adhi jyām iva dhanvani
children.translated_text: I stretch your member over the string as on a bow.

children.text: kramasvarśa iva rohitam anavaglāyatā sadā ||
children.translated_text: Stride like a red stag, always without flagging.

children.text: aśvasyāśvatarasyājasya petvasya ca
children.translated_text: Of the horse, of the mule, of the goat, and of the swift beast,

children.text: atha ṛṣabhasya ye vājās tān asmin dhehi tanūvaśin ||
children.translated_text: and the powers of the bull, place those in him, O body-governing one.

children.text: Chapter 107
sahasraśṛṅgo vṛṣabho yaḥ samudrād udācarat
children.translated_text: The thousand-horned bull that rose up from the ocean,

children.text: tenā sahasyenā vayaṃ ni janānt svāpayāmasi ||
children.translated_text: with that mighty one we make the people sleep.

children.text: na bhūmiṃ vāto ati vāti nāti paśyati kaścana
children.translated_text: The wind does not blow beyond the earth, and no one sees beyond.

children.text: striyaś ca sarvāḥ svāpaya śunaś cendrasakhā caran ||
children.translated_text: Put all the women to sleep, and the dogs too, as you move, friend of <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: proṣṭheśayās talpeśayā nārīr yā vahyaśīvarīḥ
children.translated_text: The women who lie on benches, who lie on beds, the women who go in conveyances and are kindly,

children.text: striyo yāḥ puṇyagandhayas tāḥ sarvāḥ svāpayāmasi ||
children.translated_text: the women who have pleasant fragrance, all those we make sleep.

children.text: ejadejad ajagrabhaṃ cakṣuḥ prāṇam ajagrabham
children.translated_text: Moving and moving, I have seized; I have seized the eye and the breath.

children.text: aṅgāny ajagrabhaṃ sarvā rātrīṇām atiśarvare ||
children.translated_text: I have seized all the limbs, O night beyond nights.

children.text: ya āste yaś carati yaś ca tiṣṭhan vipaśyati
children.translated_text: Whoever sits, whoever walks, and whoever stands and looks out,

children.text: teṣāṃ saṃ dadhmo akṣīṇi yathedaṃ harmyaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: we close their eyes, just as this mansion is closed.

children.text: svaptu mātā svaptu pitā svaptu śvā svaptu viśpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Let the mother sleep, let the father sleep, let the dog sleep, let the clan-lord sleep.

children.text: svapantv asyai jñātayaḥ svaptv ayam abhito janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let her kinsmen sleep; let this whole surrounding people sleep.

children.text: svapna svapnābhikaraṇena sarvaṃ ni svāpayā janam
children.translated_text: O Sleep, with the sleep-making instrument put all people fully to sleep.

children.text: otsūryam anyānt svāpayāvyuṣaṃ jāgṛtād aham indra ivāriṣṭo akṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Put the others to sleep until sunrise; until dawn may I stay awake, unharmed like <s>Indra</s> and undiminished.

children.text: Chapter 108
brāhmaṇo jajñe prathamo daśaśīrṣo daśāsyaḥ
children.translated_text: The Brahman was born first, ten-headed and ten-mouthed.

children.text: sa somaṃ prathamaḥ papau sa cakārārasaṃ viṣam ||
children.translated_text: He first drank the <s>Soma</s>; he made the poison sapless.

children.text: yāvatī dyāvāpṛthivī varimṇā yāvat sapta sindhavo vitaṣṭhire
children.translated_text: As far as heaven and earth extend in breadth, as far as the seven rivers have spread out,

children.text: vācaṃ viṣasya dūṣaṇīṃ tām ito nir avādiṣam ||
children.translated_text: that speech which spoils poison I have spoken out from here.

children.text: suparṇas tvā garutmān viṣa prathamam āvayat
children.translated_text: <s>Suparṇa</s>, <s>Garutmān</s>, first swept you away, O poison.

children.text: nāmīmado nārūrupa utāsmā abhavaḥ pituḥ ||
children.translated_text: You did not bewilder him, you did not injure him, and you became as food for him.

children.text: yas ta āsyat pañcāṅgurir vakrāc cid adhi dhanvanaḥ
children.translated_text: The five-fingered one who shot you, even from the curved bow,

children.text: apaskambhasya śalyān nir avocam ahaṃ viṣam ||
children.translated_text: from the support and from the barbs, I have spoken the poison out.

children.text: śalyād viṣaṃ nir avocam prāñjanād uta parṇadheḥ
children.translated_text: From the barb I have spoken out the poison, and also from the anointing and from the feather-holder.

children.text: apāṣṭhācchṛṅgāt kulmalān nir avocam aham viṣam ||
children.translated_text: From the shaft, the horn, and the tip I have spoken out the poison.

children.text: arasas ta iṣo śalyo 'tho te arasaṃ viṣam
children.translated_text: Sapless is your arrow, your barb, and sapless is your poison.

children.text: utārasasya vṛkṣasya dhanuṣ ṭe arasārasam ||
children.translated_text: And from the sapless tree your bow is utterly without sap.

children.text: ye apīṣan ye adihan ya āsyan ye avāsṛjan
children.translated_text: Those who smeared it, those who rubbed it on, those who shot it, those who released it,

children.text: sarve te vadhrayaḥ kṛtā vadhrir viṣagiriḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all of them have been made impotent; the poison-bearing hill has been made impotent.

children.text: vadhrayas te khanitāro vadhris tvam asy oṣadhe
children.translated_text: Impotent are your diggers, and impotent are you, O herb.

children.text: vadhriḥ sa parvato girir yato jātam idaṃ viṣam ||
children.translated_text: Impotent is that mountain, that hill from which this poison was born.

children.text: Chapter 109
vār idam vārayātai varaṇāvatyām adhi
children.translated_text: This water is for warding off, upon <s>Varaṇāvatī</s>.

children.text: tatrāmṛtasyāsiktaṃ tenā te vāraye viṣam ||
children.translated_text: There the immortal draught was poured; with that I ward off your poison.

children.text: arasaṃ prācyaṃ viṣam arasaṃ yad udīcyam
children.translated_text: Sapless is the eastern poison, sapless whatever poison is northern.

children.text: athedam adharācyaṃ karambheṇa vi kalpate ||
children.translated_text: And this lower poison is broken apart with karambha gruel.

children.text: karambhaṃ kṛtvā tiryaṃ pībaspākam udārathim
children.translated_text: Having made karambha gruel, drink crosswise the unripe belly-going draught.

children.text: kṣudhā kila tvā duṣṭano jakṣivānt sa na rūrupaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hunger, they say, has eaten you, evil-toothed one; it has not injured you.

children.text: vi te madaṃ madāvati śaram iva pātayāmasi
children.translated_text: We make your intoxication, O intoxicated one, fall away like an arrow.

children.text: pra tvā carum iva yeṣantaṃ vacasā sthāpayāmasi ||
children.translated_text: With speech we set you in place, as you wander like a sacrificial vessel.

children.text: pari grāmam ivācitaṃ vacasā sthāpayāmasi
children.translated_text: With speech we set you around like an unassembled village.

children.text: tiṣṭhā vṛkṣa iva sthāmny abhrikhāte na rūrupaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Stand like a tree on firm ground; un-dug from the pit, do not injure.

children.text: pavastais tvā pary akrīṇan dūrśebhir ajinair uta
children.translated_text: They bought you with pavasta goods and also with costly skins.

children.text: prakrīr asi tvam oṣadhe 'bhrikhāte na rūrupaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are bought forth, O herb; un-dug from the pit, do not injure.

children.text: anāptā ye vaḥ prathamā yāni karmāṇi cakrire
children.translated_text: Those first unattained deeds of yours, the deeds that they performed,

children.text: vīrān no atra mā dabhan tad va etat puro dadhe ||
children.translated_text: let them not harm our heroes here; this I set before you.

children.text: Chapter 110
bhūto bhūteṣu paya ā dadhāti sa bhūtānām adhipatir babhūva
children.translated_text: The being places milk among beings; he became the overlord of beings.

children.text: tasya mṛtyuś carati rājasūyaṃ sa rājā anu manyatām idaṃ ||
children.translated_text: Death performs his royal consecration; let that king approve this.

children.text: abhi prehi māpa vena ugraś cettā sapatnahā
children.translated_text: Advance against them; do not withdraw, O fierce discerner, slayer of rivals.

children.text: ā tiṣṭha mitravardhana tubhyam devā adhi bruvan ||
children.translated_text: Stand up, increaser of friends; the gods have spoken in your favor.

children.text: ātiṣṭhantaṃ pari viśve abhūṣañchriyaṃ vasānaś carati svarociḥ
children.translated_text: As he stood up, all adorned him; wearing splendor, he moves with his own radiance.

children.text: mahat tad vṛṣṇo asurasya nāmā viśvarūpo amṛtāni tasthau ||
children.translated_text: Great is that name of the virile <s>Asura</s>; the all-formed one has taken his stand among the immortal things.

children.text: vyāghro adhi vaiyāghre vi kramasva diśo mahīḥ
children.translated_text: Stride out, a tiger, upon the tiger-skin, across the great directions.

children.text: viśas tvā sarvā vāñchantv āpo divyāḥ payasvatīḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let all the clans desire you, and the heavenly waters rich in milk.

children.text: yā āpo divyāḥ payasā madanty antarikṣa uta vā pṛthivyām
children.translated_text: Those heavenly waters that rejoice in milk, whether in the midspace or on the earth,

children.text: tāsāṃ tvā sarvāsām apām abhi ṣiñcāmi varcasā ||
children.translated_text: with the splendor of all those waters I sprinkle you over.

children.text: abhi tvā varcasāsicann āpo divyāḥ payasvatīḥ
children.translated_text: The heavenly waters rich in milk have sprinkled you with splendor.

children.text: yathāso mitravardhanas tathā tvā savitā karat ||
children.translated_text: As you are one who increases friendship, so may <s>Savitā</s> make you.

children.text: enā vyāghraṃ pariṣasvajānāḥ siṃhaṃ hinvanti mahate saubhagāya
children.translated_text: Embracing the tiger with this, they impel the lion toward great good fortune.

children.text: samudraṃ na subhuvas tasthivāṃsaṃ marmṛjyante dvīpinam apsv antaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Like well-placed ones standing in the sea, they cleanse the leopard within the waters.

children.text: Chapter 111
ehi jīvaṃ trāyamāṇaṃ parvatasyāsy akṣyam
children.translated_text: Come here, protecting the living one, the imperishable thing of this mountain.

children.text: viśvebhir devair dattaṃ paridhir jīvanāya kam ||
children.translated_text: Given by all the gods, you are a girdle for the sake of living.

children.text: paripāṇaṃ puruṣāṇāṃ paripāṇaṃ gavāṃ asi
children.translated_text: You are the protection of men, the protection of cows.

children.text: aśvānām arvatām paripāṇāya tasthiṣe ||
children.translated_text: You stand for the protection of horses and swift steeds.

children.text: utāsi paripāṇam yātujambhanam āñjana
children.translated_text: And you are protection, a crusher of sorcery, O <s>āñjana</s> (collyrium).

children.text: utāmṛtasya tvaṃ vetthātho asi jīvabhojanam atho haritabheṣajam ||
children.translated_text: And you know what is immortal; further, you are food for life, and also a yellow-green remedy.

children.text: yasyāñjana prasarpasy aṅgamaṅgam paruṣparuḥ
children.translated_text: When you creep forth, O <s>āñjana</s>, through limb after limb, joint by joint,

children.text: tato yakṣmaṃ vi bādhasa ugro madhyamaśīr iva ||
children.translated_text: from there you drive away wasting disease, fierce like one who devours the middle head.

children.text: nainaṃ prāpnoti śapatho na kṛtyā nābhiśocanam
children.translated_text: No curse reaches him, no sorcery, no burning grief.

children.text: nainaṃ viṣkandham aśnute yas tvā bibharty āñjana ||
children.translated_text: No convulsive seizure attacks the one who wears you, O <s>āñjana</s>.

children.text: asanmantrād duṣvapnyād duṣkṛtācchamalād uta
children.translated_text: From an evil mantra, from a bad dream, from wrongdoing and from defilement,

children.text: durhārdaś cakṣuṣo ghorāt tasmān naḥ pāhy āñjana ||
children.translated_text: from the terrible eye of the ill-hearted, protect us from that, O <s>āñjana</s>.

children.text: idaṃ vidvān āñjana satyaṃ vakṣyāmi nānṛtam
children.translated_text: Knowing this, O <s>āñjana</s>, I shall speak truth, not falsehood:

children.text: saneyam aśvaṃ gām aham ātmānaṃ tava pūruṣa ||
children.translated_text: may I win a horse, a cow, and myself as your man.

children.text: trayo dāsā āñjanasya takmā balāsa ād ahiḥ
children.translated_text: The three slaves of <s>āñjana</s> are fever, balāsa disease, and the serpent.

children.text: varṣiṣṭhaḥ parvatānāṃ trikakun nāma te pitā ||
children.translated_text: The tallest of mountains, named <s>Trikakud</s>, is your father.

children.text: yad āñjanaṃ traikakudam jātaṃ himavatas pari
children.translated_text: The <s>āñjana</s> born around <s>Himavat</s>, the three-peaked one,

children.text: yātūṃś ca sarvāñ jambhayat sarvāś ca yātudhānyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has crushed all sorcerers and all sorceresses.

children.text: yadi vāsi traikakudaṃ yadi yāmunam ucyase
children.translated_text: Whether you are three-peaked, or whether you are called Yamunian,

children.text: ubhe te bhadre nāmnī tābhyāṃ naḥ pāhy āñjana ||
children.translated_text: both your names are auspicious; by them protect us, O <s>āñjana</s>.

children.text: Chapter 112
vātājjāto antarikṣād vidyuto jyotiṣas pari
children.translated_text: Born from wind, from the midspace, from lightning and from light,

children.text: sa no hiraṇyajāḥ śaṅkhaḥ kṛśanaḥ pātv aṃhasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may that gold-born conch shell, the pearl-white one, protect us from distress.

children.text: yo agrato rocanānāṃ samudrād adhi jajñiṣe
children.translated_text: You who were born in front of the shining realms, from the ocean,

children.text: śaṅkhena hatvā rakṣāṃsy attriṇo vi ṣahāmahe ||
children.translated_text: with the conch shell, having struck down the demons and devourers, we overpower them.

children.text: śaṅkhenāmīvām amatiṃ śaṅkhenota sadānvāḥ
children.translated_text: With the conch shell we overpower disease and want, and with the conch shell the ever-following foes.

children.text: śaṅkho no viśvabheṣajaḥ kṛśanaḥ pātv aṃhasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The conch shell is our all-healing remedy; may the pearl-white one protect us from distress.

children.text: divi jātaḥ samudrajaḥ sindhutas pary ābhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Born in heaven, born from the ocean, brought here from the river,

children.text: sa no hiraṇyajāḥ śaṅkha āyuṣprataraṇo maṇiḥ ||
children.translated_text: may that gold-born conch shell, the life-prolonging amulet, protect us.

children.text: samudrājjāto maṇir vṛtrāj jāto divākaraḥ
children.translated_text: Born from the ocean, an amulet born from <s>Vṛtra</s>, maker of day,

children.text: so asmānt sarvataḥ pātu hetyā devāsurebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may it protect us on every side from the missile of gods and asuras.

children.text: hiraṇyānām eko 'si somāt tvam adhi jajñiṣe
children.translated_text: You are one among golden things; you were born from <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: rathe tvam asi darśata iṣudhau rocanas tvaṃ pra ṇa āyūṃṣi tāriṣat ||
children.translated_text: You are visible on the chariot, you shine in the quiver; may it carry our lifetimes forward.

children.text: devānām asthi kṛśanaṃ babhūva tad ātmanvac caraty apsv antaḥ
children.translated_text: The pearl-white one became the bone of the gods; possessing a self, it moves within the waters.

children.text: tat te badhnāmy āyuṣe varcase balāya dīrghāyutvāya śataśāradāya kārśanas tvābhi rakṣatu ||
children.translated_text: I fasten that on you for life, for splendor, for strength, for long life, for a hundred autumns; may the pearl-white one protect you.

children.text: Chapter 113
anaḍvān dādhāra pṛthivīm uta dyām anaḍvān dādhārorv antarikṣam
children.translated_text: The ox has upheld the earth and heaven; the ox has upheld the broad midspace.

children.text: anaḍvān dādhāra pradiśaḥ ṣaḍ urvīr anaḍvān viśvaṃ bhuvanam ā viveśa ||
children.translated_text: The ox has upheld the six broad directions; the ox has entered the whole world.

children.text: anaḍvān indraḥ sa paśubhyo vi caṣṭe trayāñchakro vi mimīte adhvanaḥ
children.translated_text: The ox is <s>Indra</s>; he looks apart for the cattle, and, threefold, <s>Śakra</s> measures out the paths.

children.text: bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyad bhuvanā duhānaḥ sarvā devānām carati vratāni ||
children.translated_text: Milking what has been and what will be, he moves through all the observances of the gods.

children.text: indro jāto manuṣyeṣv antar gharmas taptaś carati śośucānaḥ
children.translated_text: Born as <s>Indra</s> among human beings, the heated <s>gharma</s> walks within, blazing.

children.text: suprajāḥ sant sa udāre na sarṣad yo nāśnīyād anaḍuho vijānan ||
children.translated_text: Rich in offspring, he will not fail in the generous rite, if one who knows does not eat of the ox.

children.text: anaḍvān duhe sukṛtasya loka ainaṃ pyāyayati pavamānaḥ purastāt
children.translated_text: The ox milks the world of the well-doer; <s>Pavamāna</s> makes him swell in front.

children.text: parjanyo dhārā maruta ūdho asya yajñaḥ payo dakṣiṇā doho asya ||
children.translated_text: <s>Parjanya</s> is his streams, the <s>Maruts</s> his udder, sacrifice his milk, the priestly gift his milking.

children.text: yasya neśe yajñapatir na yajño nāsya dāteśe na pratigrahītā
children.translated_text: Neither the lord of sacrifice nor the sacrifice has power over him; neither the giver nor the receiver has power over him.

children.text: yo viśvajid viśvabhṛd viśvakarmā gharmaṃ no brūta yatamaś catuṣpāt ||
children.translated_text: Tell us which four-footed one is the <s>gharma</s>, the all-conquering, all-sustaining, all-making one.

children.text: yena devāḥ svar āruruhur hitvā śarīram amṛtasya nābhim
children.translated_text: By means of whom the gods climbed to heaven, leaving the body for the navel of immortality,

children.text: tena geṣma sukṛtasya lokaṃ gharmasya vratena tapasā yaśasyavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by him, through the observance of the <s>gharma</s>, through heat, may we, possessing fame, go to the world of the well-doer.

children.text: indro rūpeṇāgnir vahena prajāpatiḥ parameṣṭhī virāṭ
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> by form, <s>Agni</s> by carrying, <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Parameṣṭhī</s>, <s>Virāj</s>:

children.text: viśvānare akramata vaiśvānare akramatānaḍuhy akramata
children.translated_text: he stepped into <s>Viśvānara</s>, stepped into <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, stepped into the ox.

children.text: so 'dṛṃhayata so 'dhārayata ||
children.translated_text: He made it firm; he upheld it.

children.text: madhyam etad anaḍuho yatraiṣa vaha āhitaḥ
children.translated_text: This is the middle of the ox, where this carrying power is set.

children.text: etāvad asya prācīnaṃ yāvān pratyaṅ samāhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: So much of him is turned eastward, as much as is gathered toward the west.

children.text: yo vedānaḍuho dohān saptānupadasvataḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the seven milkings of the ox in proper order,

children.text: prajāṃ ca lokaṃ cāpnoti tathā saptaṛṣayo viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: obtains offspring and a world; so the <s>Saptaṛṣis</s> know.

children.text: padbhiḥ sedim avakrāmann irāṃ jaṅghābhir utkhidan
children.translated_text: With his feet he stepped down upon the seat; with his shanks he dug up refreshment.

children.text: śrameṇānaḍvān kīlālaṃ kīnāśaś cābhi gacchataḥ ||
children.translated_text: With labor the ox and the ploughman come to the sweet draught.

children.text: dvādaśa vā etā rātrīr vratyā āhuḥ prajāpateḥ
children.translated_text: These twelve nights, they say, are vowed to <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: tatropa brahma yo veda tad vā anaḍuho vratam ||
children.translated_text: There, whoever knows the <s>brahman</s>, that indeed is the ox's observance.

children.text: duhe sāyaṃ duhe prātar duhe madhyaṃdinaṃ pari
children.translated_text: He milks in the evening, he milks in the morning, he milks around midday.

children.text: dohā ye asya saṃyanti tān vidmānupadasvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The milkings of his that come together, we know them in proper order.

children.text: Chapter 114
rohaṇy asi rohaṇy asthnaś chinnasya rohaṇī
children.translated_text: You are the knitting one, the knitting one, the healer of a broken bone.

children.text: rohayedam arundhati ||
children.translated_text: Make this grow together, O <s>Arundhatī</s>.

children.text: yat te riṣṭaṃ yat te dyuttam asti peṣṭraṃ ta ātmani
children.translated_text: Whatever of yours is injured, whatever of yours is broken, whatever is crushed in your body,

children.text: dhātā tad bhadrayā punaḥ saṃ dadhat paruṣā paruḥ ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Dhātṛ</s> set that together again with what is auspicious, joint to joint.

children.text: saṃ te majjā majjñā bhavatu sam u te paruṣā paruḥ
children.translated_text: Let your marrow be joined with marrow, and let your joint also be joined with joint.

children.text: saṃ te māṃsasya visrastaṃ sam asthy api rohatu ||
children.translated_text: Let what has fallen apart from your flesh come together; let bone also grow together.

children.text: majjā majjñā saṃ dhīyatāṃ carmaṇā carma rohatu
children.translated_text: Let marrow be joined with marrow; let skin grow together with skin.

children.text: asṛk te asthi rohatu māṃsaṃ māṃsena rohatu ||
children.translated_text: Let your blood grow together with bone; let flesh grow together with flesh.

children.text: loma lomnā saṃ kalpayā tvacā saṃ kalpayā tvacam
children.translated_text: I fit hair together with hair; I fit skin together with skin.

children.text: asṛk te asthi rohatu chinnaṃ saṃ dhehy oṣadhe ||
children.translated_text: Let your blood grow together with bone; put together what is cut, O plant.

children.text: sa ut tiṣṭha prehi pra drava rathaḥ sucakraḥ
children.translated_text: So rise up, go forth, run onward, like a chariot with good wheels,

children.text: supaviḥ sunābhiḥ prati tiṣṭhordhvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with good rim and good nave; stand firm, upright.

children.text: yadi kartaṃ patitvā saṃśaśre yadi vāśmā prahṛto jaghāna
children.translated_text: If, having fallen into a pit, he was shattered, or if a hurled stone struck him,

children.text: ṛbhū rathasyevāṅgāni saṃ dadhat paruṣā paruḥ ||
children.translated_text: let the <s>Ṛbhus</s> set him together, joint by joint, like the parts of a chariot.

children.text: Chapter 115
uta devā avahitaṃ devā un nayathā punaḥ
children.translated_text: And what has been laid low, O gods, lift up again, O gods.

children.text: utāgaś cakruṣaṃ devā devā jīvayathā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the one who has committed an offence, O gods, make live again, O gods.

children.text: dvāv imau vātau vāta ā sindhor ā parāvataḥ
children.translated_text: These two winds are winds, one from the ocean and one from the far distance.

children.text: dakṣaṃ te anya āvātu vy anyo vātu yad rapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let one blow strength to you; let the other blow away whatever defect there is.

children.text: ā vāta vāhi bheṣajaṃ vi vāta vāhi yad rapaḥ
children.translated_text: Bring medicine here, O wind; blow away, O wind, whatever defect there is.

children.text: tvaṃ hi viśvabheṣaja devānāṃ dūta īyase ||
children.translated_text: For you go as the all-healing messenger of the gods.

children.text: trāyantām imaṃ devās trāyantāṃ marutāṃ gaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Let the gods protect this man; let the hosts of the <s>Maruts</s> protect him.

children.text: trāyantāṃ viśvā bhūtāni yathāyam arapā asat ||
children.translated_text: Let all beings protect him, so that this man may be free from injury.

children.text: ā tvāgamaṃ śaṃtātibhir atho ariṣṭatātibhiḥ
children.translated_text: I have come to you with blessings and also with states of freedom from harm.

children.text: dakṣaṃ ta ugram ābhāriṣaṃ parā yakṣmaṃ suvāmi te ||
children.translated_text: I have brought you fierce strength; I drive wasting disease away from you.

children.text: ayaṃ me hasto bhagavān ayaṃ me bhagavattaraḥ
children.translated_text: This hand of mine is blessed; this one of mine is still more blessed.

children.text: ayaṃ me viśvabheṣajo 'yaṃ śivābhimarśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This one of mine is all-healing; this one has an auspicious touch.

children.text: hastābhyāṃ daśaśākhābhyāṃ jihvā vācaḥ purogavī
children.translated_text: With the two hands, ten-branched, and with the tongue, the leader of speech,

children.text: anāmayitnubhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ tābhyāṃ tvābhi mṛśāmasi ||
children.translated_text: with those two hands that remove illness, with them we touch you.

children.text: Chapter 116
ajo hy agner ajaniṣṭa śokāt so apaśyajjanitāram agre
children.translated_text: For the goat was born from the flame of <s>Agni</s>; at the beginning he saw his begetter.

children.text: tena devā devatām agrā āyan tena rohān ruruhur medhyāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By him the gods first reached godhood; by him the consecrated ones climbed the ascents.

children.text: kramadhvam agninā nākam ukhyān hasteṣu bibhrataḥ
children.translated_text: Stride onward with fire, bearing the ritual fire-vessels in your hands.

children.text: divas pṛṣṭhaṃ svar gatvā miśrā devebhir ādhvam ||
children.translated_text: Having gone to the back of heaven, to the heavenly light, take your place mingled with the gods.

children.text: pṛṣṭhāt pṛthivyā aham antarikṣam āruham antarikṣād divam āruham
children.translated_text: From the back of the earth I ascended to the midspace; from the midspace I ascended to heaven.

children.text: divo nākasya pṛṣṭhāt svar jyotir agām aham ||
children.translated_text: From the back of heaven's vault I have gone to the light of <s>svar</s>.

children.text: svar yanto nāpekṣanta ā dyāṃ rohanti rodasī
children.translated_text: Going to <s>svar</s> and not looking back, they ascend to heaven and the two world-halves,

children.text: yajñaṃ ye viśvatodhāraṃ suvidvāṃso vitenire ||
children.translated_text: those very wise ones who have extended the sacrifice that supports all sides.

children.text: agne prehi prathamo devatānāṃ cakṣur devānām uta mānuṣānām
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, go forth first among the deities, the eye of gods and of human beings.

children.text: iyakṣamāṇā bhṛgubhiḥ sajoṣāḥ svar yantu yajamānāḥ svasti ||
children.translated_text: Intending sacrifice, in harmony with the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, may the sacrificers go to <s>svar</s> with well-being.

children.text: ajam anajmi payasā ghṛtena divyaṃ suparṇaṃ payasaṃ bṛhantam
children.translated_text: I anoint the goat with milk and ghee, the heavenly, fair-winged, great one rich in milk.

children.text: tena geṣma sukṛtasya lokaṃ svar ārohanto abhi nākam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: By him may we reach the world of the well-doer, ascending to <s>svar</s>, to the highest vault.

children.text: pañcaudanaṃ pañcabhir aṅgulibhir darvyoddhara pañcadhaitam odanam
children.translated_text: Take up the fivefold rice-dish with five fingers; with the ladle take up this fivefold rice-dish.

children.text: prācyāṃ diśi śiro ajasya dhehi dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśi dakṣiṇaṃ dhehi pārśvam ||
children.translated_text: Place the goat's head in the eastern direction; place his right side in the southern direction.

children.text: pratīcyāṃ diśi bhasadam asya dhehy uttarasyāṃ diśy uttaraṃ dhehi pārśvam
children.translated_text: Place his rump in the western direction; place his northern side in the northern direction.

children.text: ūrdhvāyāṃ diśy ajasyānūkaṃ dhehi diśi dhruvāyāṃ dhehi pājasyam antarikṣe madhyato madhyam asya ||
children.translated_text: Place the goat's backbone in the upward direction; in the fixed direction place his belly, and in the midspace, in the middle, his middle part.

children.text: śṛtam ajaṃ śṛtayā prorṇuhi tvacā sarvair aṅgaiḥ saṃbhṛtaṃ viśvarūpam
children.translated_text: Cover the cooked goat with the cooked skin, gathered with all its limbs, multiform.

children.text: sa ut tiṣṭheto abhi nākam uttamaṃ padbhiś caturbhiḥ prati tiṣṭha dikṣu ||
children.translated_text: Let him rise up from here toward the highest vault; with four feet stand firm in the quarters.

children.text: Chapter 117
samutpatantu pradiśo nabhasvatīḥ sam abhrāṇi vātajūtāni yantu
children.translated_text: Let the wind-filled regions fly up together; let the clouds driven by wind come together.

children.text: maharṣabhasya nadato nabhasvato vāśrā āpaḥ pṛthivīṃ tarpayantu ||
children.translated_text: Let the roaring waters of the great bull, borne by the wind, bellowing, satisfy the earth.

children.text: sam īkṣayantu taviṣāḥ sudānavo 'pāṃ rasā oṣadhībhiḥ sacantām
children.translated_text: Let the powerful, generous ones look upon one another; let the juices of the waters join with the plants.

children.text: varṣasya sargā mahayantu bhūmiṃ pṛthag jāyantām oṣadhayo viśvarūpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the releases of rain magnify the earth; let the multiform plants be born separately.

children.text: sam īkṣayasva gāyato nabhāṃsy apām vegāsaḥ pṛthag ud vijantām
children.translated_text: Look together upon the singing skies; let the streams of the waters tremble forth separately.

children.text: varṣasya sargā mahayantu bhūmiṃ pṛthag jāyantām vīrudho viśvarūpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the releases of rain magnify the earth; let the multiform shoots be born separately.

children.text: gaṇās tvopa gāyantu mārutāḥ parjanya ghoṣiṇaḥ pṛthak
children.translated_text: Let the <s>Marut</s> hosts sing near you, O <s>Parjanya</s>, sounding out separately.

children.text: sargā varṣasya varṣato varṣantu pṛthivīm anu ||
children.translated_text: Let the outpourings of rain from the raining one rain down along the earth.

children.text: ud īrayata marutaḥ samudratas tveṣo arko nabha ut pātayātha
children.translated_text: Set them in motion from the ocean, O <s>Maruts</s>; make the brilliant chant fly up to the sky.

children.text: maharṣabhasya nadato nabhasvato vāśrā āpaḥ pṛthivīṃ tarpayantu ||
children.translated_text: Let the roaring waters of the great bull, borne by the wind, bellowing, satisfy the earth.

children.text: abhi kranda stanayārdayodadhiṃ bhūmiṃ parjanya payasā sam aṅdhi
children.translated_text: Cry out, thunder, stir up the ocean; O <s>Parjanya</s>, soak the earth with milk.

children.text: tvayā sṛṣṭaṃ bahulam aitu varṣam āśāraiṣī kṛśagur etv astam ||
children.translated_text: Let abundant rain released by you come; let the lean cow seeking showers go home.

children.text: saṃ vo 'vantu sudānava utsā ajagarā uta
children.translated_text: Let your generous springs help you, and the great serpents too.

children.text: marudbhiḥ pracyutā meghā varṣantu pṛthivīm anu ||
children.translated_text: Let the clouds, set loose by the <s>Maruts</s>, rain down along the earth.

children.text: āśāmāśāṃ vi dyotatāṃ vātā vāntu diśodiśaḥ
children.translated_text: Let lightning flash in every quarter; let the winds blow in every direction.

children.text: marudbhiḥ pracyutā meghāḥ saṃ yantu pṛthivīm anu ||
children.translated_text: Let the clouds, set loose by the <s>Maruts</s>, come together along the earth.

children.text: āpo vidyud abhraṃ varṣaṃ saṃ vo 'vantu sudānava utsā ajagarā uta
children.translated_text: Waters, lightning, cloud, and rain: let your generous springs help you, and the great serpents too.

children.text: marudbhiḥ pracyutā meghāḥ prāvantu pṛthivīm anu ||
children.translated_text: Let the clouds, set loose by the <s>Maruts</s>, pour forth along the earth.

children.text: apām agnis tanūbhiḥ saṃvidāno ya oṣadhīnām adhipā babhūva
children.translated_text: The <s>Agni</s> of the waters, in accord with their bodies, who became lord of the plants,

children.text: sa no varṣaṃ vanutāṃ jātavedāḥ prāṇaṃ prajābhyo amṛtaṃ divas pari ||
children.translated_text: may that <s>Jātavedas</s> win rain for us, life-breath and immortality from heaven for creatures.

children.text: prajāpatiḥ salilād ā samudrād āpa īrayann udadhim ardayāti
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s>, from the waters, from the ocean, setting the waters in motion, stirs up the sea.

children.text: pra pyāyatāṃ vṛṣṇo aśvasya reto 'rvān etena stanayitnunehi ||
children.translated_text: Let the seed of the vigorous horse swell forth; come hither with this thunder.

children.text: apo niṣiñcann asuraḥ pitā naḥ śvasantu gargarā apāṃ varuṇāva nīcīr apaḥ sṛja
children.translated_text: Pouring down the waters, the mighty father is ours; let the gurgling waters breathe, O <s>Varuṇa</s>; release the waters downward.

children.text: vadantu pṛśnibāhavo maṇḍūkā iriṇānu ||
children.translated_text: Let the speckled-armed frogs speak in the dry hollow.

children.text: saṃvatsaraṃ śaśayānā brāhmaṇā vratacāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having lain for a year, like brahmins who keep a vow,

children.text: vācam parjanyajinvitāṃ pra maṇḍūkā avādiṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the frogs have uttered their voice, quickened by <s>Parjanya</s>.

children.text: upapravada maṇḍūki varṣaṃ ā vada tāduri
children.translated_text: Speak near us, O female frog; call for rain, O <s>Tāduri</s>.

children.text: madhye hradasya plavasva vigṛhya caturaḥ padaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Float in the middle of the pool, stretching out your four feet.

children.text: khaṇvakhā khaimakhā madhye taduri
children.translated_text: <s>Khaṇvakhā</s>, <s>Khaimakhā</s>, in the middle, O <s>Tāduri</s>.

children.text: varṣaṃ vanudhvaṃ pitaro marutāṃ mana icchata ||
children.translated_text: Seek rain for yourselves, fathers; desire the mind of the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: mahāntaṃ kośam ud acābhi ṣiñca savidyutaṃ bhavatu vātu vātaḥ
children.translated_text: Raise up the great vessel and sprinkle it over us; let it be with lightning, let the wind blow.

children.text: tanvatāṃ yajñaṃ bahudhā visṛṣṭā ānandinīr oṣadhayo bhavantu ||
children.translated_text: Let them stretch out the sacrifice in many ways, let the released plants become joyful.

children.text: Chapter 118
bṛhann eṣām adhiṣṭhātā antikād iva paśyati
children.translated_text: Their great overseer sees as if from nearby.

children.text: ya stāyan manyate carant sarvaṃ devā idaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever thinks he is stealing as he goes, the gods know all this.

children.text: yas tiṣṭhati carati yaś ca vañcati yo nilāyaṃ carati yaḥ prataṅkam
children.translated_text: Whoever stands, moves, cheats, whoever moves in hiding, whoever lurks secretly,

children.text: dvau saṃniṣadya yan mantrayete rājā tad veda varuṇas tṛtīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whatever two people sitting together whisper, king <s>Varuṇa</s> knows it as the third.

children.text: uteyaṃ bhūmir varuṇasya rājña utāsau dyaur bṛhatī dūreantā
children.translated_text: This earth belongs to king <s>Varuṇa</s>, and that broad heaven whose ends are far away.

children.text: uto samudrau varuṇasya kukṣī utāsminn alpa udake nilīnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The two oceans too are <s>Varuṇa</s>'s bellies, and he is hidden in this little water.

children.text: uta yo dyām atisarpāt parastān na sa mucyātai varuṇasya rājñaḥ
children.translated_text: Even if someone should creep beyond heaven, he would not escape king <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: divaspaśaḥ pra carantīdam asya sahasrākṣā ati paśyanti bhūmim ||
children.translated_text: His watchers from heaven go forth; thousand-eyed, they look across the earth.

children.text: sarvaṃ tad rājā varuṇo vi caṣṭe yad antarā rodasī yat parastāt
children.translated_text: King <s>Varuṇa</s> observes all that is between heaven and earth and what is beyond.

children.text: saṃkhyātā asya nimiṣo janānām akṣān iva śvaghnī ni minoti tāni ||
children.translated_text: The blinkings of men are counted by him; like a dice-player, he sets them down.

children.text: ye te pāśā varuṇa saptasapta tredhā tiṣṭhanti viṣitā ruṣantaḥ
children.translated_text: Those nooses of yours, O <s>Varuṇa</s>, seven by seven, which stand spread out threefold and shining,

children.text: sinantu sarve anṛtaṃ vadantaṃ yaḥ satyavādy ati taṃ sṛjantu ||
children.translated_text: let them bind everyone who speaks falsehood; let them release the one who speaks truth.

children.text: śatena pāśair abhi dhehi varuṇainaṃ mā te mocy anṛtavāṅ nṛcakṣaḥ
children.translated_text: With a hundred nooses bind him, O <s>Varuṇa</s>; let the false-speaking man who sees men not be released by you.

children.text: āstāṃ jālma udaraṃ śraṃśayitvā kośa ivābandhaḥ parikṛtyamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the wretch sit there with his belly loosened, like a bound vessel being cut all around.

children.text: yaḥ samāmyo varuṇo yo vyāmyo yaḥ saṃdeśyo varuṇo yo videśyo
children.translated_text: The <s>Varuṇa</s> who is nearby, the one who is far away, the <s>Varuṇa</s> at home and the one abroad,

children.text: yo daivo varuṇo yaś ca mānuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the divine <s>Varuṇa</s> and the human one:

children.text: tais tvā sarvair abhi ṣyāmi pāśair asāv āmuṣyāyaṇāmuṣyāḥ putra
children.translated_text: with all those nooses I bind you, so-and-so, son of so-and-so, for so-and-so.

children.text: tān u te sarvān anusaṃdiśāmi ||
children.translated_text: All those I assign to you in order.

children.text: Chapter 119
īśāṇāṃ tvā bheṣajānām ujjeṣa ā rabhāmahe
children.translated_text: As lord of remedies, for victory we take hold of you,

children.text: cakre sahasravīryam sarvasmā oṣadhe tvā ||
children.translated_text: the thousand-powered wheel; for every purpose, O plant, we take hold of you.

children.text: satyajitaṃ śapathayāvanīṃ sahamānāṃ punaḥsarām
children.translated_text: Truth-winning, curse-averting, overpowering, returning again,

children.text: sarvāḥ sam ahvy oṣadhīr ito naḥ pārayād iti ||
children.translated_text: I have called all the plants together, saying, 'Let this one carry us across.'

children.text: yā śaśāpa śapanena yāghaṃ mūram ādadhe
children.translated_text: The woman who cursed with a curse, who placed ruin and folly upon us,

children.text: yā rasasya haraṇāya jātam ārebhe tokam attu sā ||
children.translated_text: who set herself to steal the sap and the born child: let that sorcery consume her.

children.text: yāṃ te cakrur āme pātre yāṃ cakrur nīlalohite
children.translated_text: The <s>kṛtyā</s> they made for you in an unbaked vessel, the one they made in blue and red,

children.text: āme māṃse kṛtyāṃ yāṃ cakrus tayā kṛtyākṛto jahi ||
children.translated_text: the <s>kṛtyā</s> they made in raw flesh: with that strike the makers of <s>kṛtyā</s>.

children.text: dauṣvapnyaṃ daurjīvityaṃ rakṣo abhvam arāyyaḥ
children.translated_text: Bad dreams, bad living, a demon, a monstrous evil, hostile poverty,

children.text: durṇāmnīḥ sarvā durvācas tā asman nāśayāmasi ||
children.translated_text: all ill-named and ill-spoken things: we drive them away from us.

children.text: kṣudhāmāraṃ tṛṣṇāmāram agotām anapatyatām
children.translated_text: Death by hunger, death by thirst, lack of cattle, childlessness:

children.text: apāmārga tvayā vayaṃ sarvaṃ tad apa mṛjmahe ||
children.translated_text: with you, O <s>Apāmārga</s>, we wipe all that away.

children.text: tṛṣṇāmāraṃ kṣudhāmāraṃ atho akṣaparājayam
children.translated_text: Death by thirst, death by hunger, and also defeat at dice:

children.text: apāmārga tvayā vayaṃ sarvaṃ tad apa mṛjmahe ||
children.translated_text: with you, O <s>Apāmārga</s>, we wipe all that away.

children.text: apāmārga oṣadhīnāṃ sarvāsām eka id vaśī
children.translated_text: <s>Apāmārga</s> alone is master over all the plants.

children.text: tena te mṛjma āsthitam atha tvam agadaś cara ||
children.translated_text: With it we wipe away what has settled on you; then go about free from disease.

children.text: Chapter 120
samaṃ jyotiḥ sūryeṇāhnā rātrī samāvatī
children.translated_text: The light is equal with the sun, and the night is equal with the day.

children.text: kṛṇomi satyam ūtaye 'rasāḥ santu kṛtvarīḥ ||
children.translated_text: I make truth for aid; let the sorcerous women be without sap.

children.text: yo devāḥ kṛtyāṃ kṛtvā harād aviduṣo gṛham
children.translated_text: Whoever, O gods, has made a <s>kṛtyā</s> and carried it to the house of one who does not know,

children.text: vatso dhārur iva mātaraṃ taṃ pratyag upa padyatām ||
children.translated_text: let it return back to him, like a calf to its mother.

children.text: amā kṛtvā pāpmānaṃ yas tenānyaṃ jighāṃsati
children.translated_text: Whoever, having made evil at home, seeks to harm another with it,

children.text: aśmānas tasyāṃ dagdhāyāṃ bahulāḥ phaṭ karikrati ||
children.translated_text: when it is burned, many stones will crackle 'phaṭ' against him.

children.text: sahasradhāman viśikhān vigrīvāṁ chāyayā tvam
children.translated_text: Thousand-stationed, arrowless, neckless through your shadow,

children.text: prati sma cakruṣe kṛtyāṃ priyāṃ priyāvate hara ||
children.translated_text: carry the <s>kṛtyā</s> back to its maker, the beloved to the beloved one.

children.text: anayāham oṣadhyā sarvāḥ kṛtyā adūduṣam
children.translated_text: With this plant I have spoiled all <s>kṛtyās</s>,

children.text: yāṃ kṣetre cakrur yāṃ goṣu yāṃ vā te puruṣeṣu ||
children.translated_text: the one they made in the field, the one among the cows, or the one among your men.

children.text: yaś cakāra na śaśāka kartuṃ śaśre pādam aṅgurim
