children.translated_text: Whoever seeks to steal our essence, O <s>Agni</s>, our food, or that of our horses, cows, and bodies,

children.text: ripu stena steyakṛd dabhram etu ni ṣa hīyatāṃ tanvā tanā ca ||
children.translated_text: may that enemy, thief, and maker of theft come to little; may he be cast down from his body and his offspring.

children.text: paraḥ so astu tanvā tanā ca tisraḥ pṛthivīr adho astu viśvāḥ
children.translated_text: May he be far away from his body and offspring; may he be beneath all three earths.

children.text: prati śuṣyatu yaśo asya devā yo mā divā dipsati yaś ca naktam ||
children.translated_text: May his fame dry up, O gods, who seeks to harm me by day and by night.

children.text: suvijñānaṃ cikituṣe janāya sac cāsac ca vacasī paspṛdhāte
children.translated_text: For the discerning person it is easy to know: true and false words contend with each other.

children.text: tasyor yat satyaṃ yatarad ṛjīyas tad it somo 'vati hanty asat ||
children.translated_text: Of the two, whichever is true, whichever is straighter, that one <s>Soma</s> protects; he strikes down the false.

children.text: na vā u somo vṛjinaṃ hinoti na kṣatriyam mithuyā dhārayantam
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s> does not prosper crookedness, nor the ruler who upholds falsehood.

children.text: hanti rakṣo hanty āsad vadantam ubhāv indrasya prasitau śayāte ||
children.translated_text: He slays the <s>rakṣas</s>; he slays the one who speaks falsehood; both lie in the fetters of <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: yadi vāham anṛtadevo asmi moghaṃ vā devāṃ apyūhe agne
children.translated_text: If I am a god of falsehood, or if, O <s>Agni</s>, I have vainly driven the gods away,

children.text: kim asmabhyaṃ jātavedo hṛṇīṣe droghavācas te nirṛthaṃ sacantām ||
children.translated_text: why are you angry with us, O <s>Jātavedas</s>? Let the deceitful speakers be joined to your ruin.

children.text: adyā murīya yadi yātudhāno asmi yadi vāyus tatapa puruṣasya
children.translated_text: May I die today if I am a <s>yātudhāna</s>, or if I have scorched the life-breath of a man.

children.text: adhā sa vīrair daśabhir vi yūyā yo mā moghaṃ yātudhānety āha ||
children.translated_text: Then let the man who falsely calls me a <s>yātudhāna</s> be parted from ten heroes.

children.text: yo māyātuṃ yātudhānety āha yo vā rakṣāḥ śicir asmīty āha
children.translated_text: Whoever calls me, who am no sorcerer, a <s>yātudhāna</s>, or whoever, being a <s>rakṣas</s>, says, 'I am pure,'

children.text: indras taṃ hantu mahatā vadhena viśvasya jantor adhamas padīṣṭa ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Indra</s> slay him with a great weapon; may he fall to the lowest place of every creature.

children.text: pra yā jigāti khargaleva naktam apa druhus tanvaṃ1 gūhamānā
children.translated_text: She who goes forth at night like a khargala, the treacherous one hiding her body,

children.text: vavram anantam ava sā padīṣṭia grāvāṇo ghnantu rakṣasa upabdaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: may she fall into the endless pit; may the pressing stones crush the <s>rakṣases</s> with their crashes.

children.text: vi tiṣṭhadhvam maruto vikṣv ichata gṛbhāyata rakṣasaḥ saṃ pinaṣṭan
children.translated_text: Spread apart, O <s>Maruts</s>; search among the peoples; seize the <s>rakṣases</s> and crush them together.

children.text: vayo ye bhūtvā patayanti naktabhir ye vā ripo dadhire deve adhvare ||
children.translated_text: Those who, becoming birds, fly by night, or who, as enemies, have taken their place at the divine sacrifice,

children.text: pra vartaya divo 'śmānam indra somaśitaṃ maghavant saṃ śiśādhi
children.translated_text: roll forth the stone from heaven, O <s>Indra</s>; sharpen the one whetted by <s>Soma</s>, O bountiful one.

children.text: prākto apākto adharād udakto 'bhi jahi rakṣasaḥ parvatena ||
children.translated_text: From the east, from the west, from below, from the north, strike the <s>rakṣases</s> with the mountain.

children.text: eta u tye patayanti śvayātava indraṃ dipsanti dipsavo 'dābhyam
children.translated_text: These dog-following creatures fly forth; the deceivers seek to harm unconquerable <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: śiśīte śakraḥ piśunebhyo vadhaṃ nunaṃ sṛjad aśaniṃ yātumadbhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The mighty one sharpens a weapon for the slanderers; now release the thunderbolt against those possessed of yātu.

children.text: indro yātūnām abhavat parāśaro havirmathīnām abhy āvivāsatām
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> became the destroyer of the yātus; he assailed those who steal the oblation.

children.text: abhīd u śakraḥ paraśur yathā vanaṃ pātreva bhindant sata etu rakṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Mighty <s>Śakra</s>, like an axe against the forest, has come upon them; let the <s>rakṣas</s> be shattered like a vessel.

children.text: ulūkayātuṃ śuśulūkayātuṃ jahi śvayātum uta kokayātum
children.translated_text: Slay the owl-yātu, the little-owl-yātu; slay the dog-yātu and the cuckoo-yātu,

children.text: suparṇayātum uta gṛdhrayātuṃ dṛṣadeva pra mṛṇa rakṣa indra ||
children.translated_text: the eagle-yātu and the vulture-yātu; crush the <s>rakṣas</s> as with a stone, O <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: mā no rakṣo abhi naḍ yātumāvad apochantu mithunā ye kimīdinaḥ
children.translated_text: Let no <s>rakṣas</s>, no yātu-possessed one, assail us; let the paired <s>kimīdins</s> depart.

children.text: pṛthivī naḥ pārthivāt pātv aṃhaso 'ntarikṣaṃ divyāt pātv asmān ||
children.translated_text: Let earth protect us from earthly distress; let the midspace protect us from heavenly distress.

children.text: indra jahi pumāṃsaṃ yātudhānam uta striyaṃ māyayā śāśadānām
children.translated_text: O <s>Indra</s>, slay the male <s>yātudhāna</s> and also the female one who practices with magic.

children.text: vigrīvāso mūradevā ṛdantu mā te dṛśant sūryam uccarantam ||
children.translated_text: Let the neckless, foolish gods howl; let them not see the sun as it rises.

children.text: prati cakṣva vi cakṣvendraś ca soma jāgṛtam
children.translated_text: Look toward us; look all around. Let <s>Indra</s> and <s>Soma</s> stay awake.

children.text: rakṣobhyo vadham asyatam aśaniṃ yātumadbhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hurl the weapon against the <s>rakṣases</s>, the thunderbolt against those possessed of yātu.

children.text: Chapter 438
yā babhravo yāś ca śukrā rohiṇīr uta pṛśnayaḥ
children.translated_text: Those that are tawny and those that are bright, the red ones and also the speckled ones,

children.text: asiknīḥ kṛṣṇā oṣadhīḥ sarvā acchāvadāmasi ||
children.translated_text: the dark, black herbs: all of them we address.

children.text: trāyantām imaṃ puruṣaṃ yakṣmād deveṣitād adhi
children.translated_text: Let them protect this man from <s>yakṣma</s> (consumptive disease), from what has been sent by the gods,

children.text: yāsām dyauḥ pitā pṛthivī mātā samudro mūlaṃ vīrudhāṃ babhūva ||
children.translated_text: those herbs of which heaven became father, earth mother, and the ocean the root.

children.text: āpo agraṃ divyā oṣadhayaḥ
children.translated_text: The waters were foremost, the heavenly herbs.

children.text: tās te yakṣmam enasyam aṅgādaṅgād anīnaśan ||
children.translated_text: Let them make your sinful <s>yakṣma</s> disappear from limb to limb.

children.text: prastṛṇatī stambinīr ekaśuṅgāḥ pratanvatīr oṣadhīr ā vadāmi
children.translated_text: I address the spreading herbs, the upright ones, the single-horned ones, the far-extending ones.

children.text: aṃśumatīḥ kāṇḍinīr yā viśākhā hvayāmi te vīrudho vaiśvadevīr ugrāḥ puruṣajīvanīḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ones rich in shoots, jointed, and branchy, I call for you, the fierce herbs belonging to all the gods, life-giving for a man.

children.text: yad vaḥ sahaḥ sahamānā vīryaṃ yac ca vo balam
children.translated_text: Whatever overcoming power is yours, O overpowering ones, whatever vigor and strength is yours,

children.text: tenemam asmād yakṣmāt puruṣaṃ muñcatauṣadhīr atho kṛṇomi bheṣajam ||
children.translated_text: with that, O herbs, release this man from this <s>yakṣma</s>; and then I make a remedy.

children.text: jīvalāṃ naghāriṣāṃ jīvantīm oṣadhīm aham
children.translated_text: The living, unharming, living herb

children.text: arundhatīm unnayantīṃ puṣpām madhumatīm iha huve 'smā ariṣṭatātaye ||
children.translated_text: that does not obstruct, that raises up, flowered and honey-sweet, I call here for this man's freedom from harm.

children.text: ihā yantu pracetaso medinīr vacaso mama
children.translated_text: Let them come here, the discerning, fat, fertile ones, to the words of my speech,

children.text: yathemaṃ pārayāmasi puruṣaṃ duritād adhi ||
children.translated_text: so that we may carry this man across beyond misfortune.

children.text: agner ghāso apāṃ garbho yā rohanti punarṇavāḥ
children.translated_text: The food of <s>Agni</s>, the embryo of the waters, those that grow up renewed again,

children.text: dhruvāḥ sahasranāmnīr bheṣajīḥ santv ābhṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: let the firm, thousand-named healing plants be brought here.

children.text: avakolbā udakātmāna oṣadhayaḥ
children.translated_text: The herbs that have water as their nature and that are free from covering,

children.text: vyṛṣantu duritaṃ tīkṣṇaśṛṅgyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: let the sharp-horned ones pour away misfortune.

children.text: unmuñcantīr vivaruṇā ugrā yā viṣadūṣaṇīḥ
children.translated_text: Those that unbind, that release from <s>Varuṇa</s>, the fierce ones that spoil poison,

children.text: atho balāsanāśanīḥ kṛtyādūṣaṇīś ca yās tā ihā yantv oṣadhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those that destroy balāsa disease and spoil sorcery: let those herbs come here.

children.text: apakrītāḥ sahīyasīr vīrudho yā abhiṣṭutāḥ
children.translated_text: The bought-away plants, the mightier herbs that have been praised,

children.text: trāyantām asmin grāme gām aśvaṃ puruṣaṃ paśum ||
children.translated_text: let them protect cow, horse, man, and livestock in this village.

children.text: madhuman mūlaṃ madhumad agram āsāṃ madhuman madhyaṃ vīrudhāṃ babhūva
children.translated_text: Honey-sweet is their root, honey-sweet their tip; honey-sweet the middle of the plants has become.

children.text: madhumat parṇaṃ madhumat puṣpam āsāṃ madhoḥ saṃbhaktā amṛtasya bhakṣo ghṛtam annaṃ duhratāṃ gopurogavam ||
children.translated_text: Honey-sweet is their leaf, honey-sweet their flower; sharing in honey, eating of immortality, let them milk out ghee and food, with the cow as their forerunner.

children.text: yāvatīḥ kiyatīś cemāḥ pṛthivyām adhy oṣadhīḥ
children.translated_text: As many and as numerous as these herbs are upon the earth,

children.text: tā mā sahasraparṇyo mṛtyor muñcantv aṃhasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: let those thousand-leaved ones release me from the distress of death.

children.text: vaiyāghro maṇir vīrudhāṃ trāyamāṇo 'bhiśastipāḥ
children.translated_text: The tiger-like amulet of the plants, protecting and warding off curses,

children.text: amīvāḥ sarvā rakṣāṃsy apa hantv adhi dūram asmat ||
children.translated_text: let it strike away all diseases and demons far off from us.

children.text: siṃhasyeva stanathoḥ saṃ vijante 'gner iva vijante ābhṛtābhyaḥ
children.translated_text: They tremble at them as at the roaring of a lion; they tremble at those brought here as at <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: gavāṃ yakṣmaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ vīrudbhir atinutto nāvyā etu srotyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the <s>yakṣma</s> of cattle and of men, driven far away by the plants, go to the navigable streams.

children.text: mumucānā oṣadhayo 'gner vaiśvānarād adhi
children.translated_text: Released from <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>, O herbs,

children.text: bhūmiṃ saṃtanvatīr ita yāsāṃ rājā vanaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: come here, spreading over the earth, you whose king is the forest tree.

children.text: yā rohanty āṅgirasīḥ parvateṣu sameṣu ca
children.translated_text: Those <s>Āṅgirasa</s> herbs that grow on mountains and on level places,

children.text: tā naḥ payasvatīḥ śivā oṣadhīḥ santu śaṃ hṛde ||
children.translated_text: let those milky, auspicious herbs be healing for us and comfort for the heart.

children.text: yāś cāhaṃ veda vīrudho yāś ca paśyāmi cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: The herbs that I know and those that I see with my eye,

children.text: ajñātā jānīmaś ca yā yāsu vidma ca saṃbhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: those unknown and those we know, and whatever store we know among them,

children.text: sarvāḥ samagrā oṣadhīr bodhantu vacaso mama
children.translated_text: let all the herbs together awaken to the words of my speech,

children.text: yathemaṃ pārayāmasi puruṣam duritād adhi ||
children.translated_text: so that we may carry this man across beyond misfortune.

children.text: aśvattho darbho vīrudhāṃ somo rājāmṛtaṃ haviḥ
children.translated_text: The aśvattha, the darbha, and <s>Soma</s>, king of the plants, the immortal oblation,

children.text: vrīhir yavaś ca bheṣajau divasputrāv amartyau ||
children.translated_text: and rice and barley, the two remedies, sons of heaven, undying.

children.text: ujjihīdhve stanayaty abhikrandaty oṣadhīḥ
children.translated_text: Rise up, O herbs, when he thunders and bellows,

children.text: yadā vaḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ parjanyo retasāvati ||
children.translated_text: when <s>Parjanya</s>, whose seed is in the rain-cloud, impregnates you, O speckled-mothered ones.

children.text: tasyāmṛtasyemaṃ balaṃ puruṣaṃ pāyayāmasi
children.translated_text: With the strength of that immortality we make this man drink power,

children.text: atho kṛṇomi bheṣajaṃ yathāsacchatahāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then I make a remedy, so that he may become one who lives a hundred years.

children.text: varāho veda vīrudhaṃ nakulo veda bheṣajīm
children.translated_text: The boar knows the plant; the mongoose knows the healing herb.

children.text: sarpā gandharvā yā vidus tā asmā avase huve ||
children.translated_text: The plants that serpents and <s>Gandharvas</s> know, those I call for help for him.

children.text: yāḥ suparṇā āṅgirasīr divyā yā raghaṭo viduḥ
children.translated_text: Those heavenly <s>Āṅgirasa</s> herbs that the eagles know, those that Raghaṭa knows,

children.text: vayāṃsi haṃsā yā vidur yāś ca sarve patatriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: those that birds and geese know, and those that all winged creatures know,

children.text: mṛgā yā vidur oṣadhīs tā asmā avase huve ||
children.translated_text: the herbs that wild animals know, those I call for help for him.

children.text: yāvatīnām oṣadhīnāṃ gāvaḥ prāśnanty aghnyā yāvatīnām ajāvayaḥ
children.translated_text: As many herbs as the inviolate cows eat, as many as the goats and sheep eat,

children.text: tāvatīs tubhyam oṣadhīḥ śarma yacchantv ābhṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so many herbs, brought here, let them grant shelter to you.

children.text: yāvatīṣu manuṣyā bheṣajaṃ bhiṣajo viduḥ
children.translated_text: As many herbs as physicians among human beings know as medicine,

children.text: tāvatīr viśvabheṣajīr ā bharāmi tvām abhi ||
children.translated_text: so many universal remedies I bring around you.

children.text: puṣpavatīḥ prasūmatīḥ phalinīr aphalā uta
children.translated_text: Those with flowers, those with offspring, those bearing fruit and those without fruit,

children.text: saṃmātara iva duhrām asmā ariṣṭatātaye ||
children.translated_text: like mothers in agreement, let them milk out safety from harm for this man.

children.text: ut tvāhārṣaṃ pañcaśalād atho daśaśalād uta
children.translated_text: I have drawn you up from the fivefold bond and also from the tenfold bond,

children.text: atho yamasya paḍvīśād viśvasmād devakilbiṣāt ||
children.translated_text: and from <s>Yama</s>'s foot-fetter, from every offense against the gods.

children.text: Chapter 439
divas pṛthivyā antarikṣāt samudrād agner vātān madhukaśā hi jajñe
children.translated_text: From heaven, from earth, from the midspace, from the ocean, from <s>Agni</s>, from the wind, the <s>madhukaśā</s> (honey-lash) was born.

children.text: tāṃ cāyitvāmṛtaṃ vasānāṃ hṛdbhiḥ prajāḥ prati nandanti sarvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having perceived her, clothed in immortality, all creatures rejoice toward her with their hearts.

children.text: mahat payo viśvarūpam asyāḥ samudrasya tvota reta āhuḥ
children.translated_text: They say that her great, all-formed milk is the seed of the ocean.

children.text: yata aiti madhukaśā rarāṇā tat prāṇas tad amṛtaṃ niviṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: From where the bounteous <s>madhukaśā</s> comes, there breath, there immortality, is established.

children.text: paśyanty asyāś caritaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pṛthaṅ naro bahudhā mīmāṃsamānāḥ
children.translated_text: Men, seeing her course upon the earth separately, ponder it in many ways.

children.text: agner vātān madhukaśā hi jajñe marutām ugrā naptiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the <s>madhukaśā</s> was born from <s>Agni</s>, from the wind, the fierce granddaughter of the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: mātādityānāṃ duhitā vasūnāṃ prāṇaḥ prajānām amṛtasya nābhiḥ
children.translated_text: Mother of the <s>Ādityas</s>, daughter of the <s>Vasus</s>, life-breath of creatures, navel of immortality,

children.text: hiraṇyavarṇā madhukaśā ghṛtācī mahān bhargaś carati martyeṣu ||
children.translated_text: gold-colored, rich in ghee, the <s>madhukaśā</s>, a great splendor, moves among mortals.

children.text: madhoḥ kaśām ajanayanta devās tasyā garbho abhavad viśvarūpaḥ
children.translated_text: The gods generated the lash of honey; its embryo became all-formed.

children.text: taṃ jātaṃ taruṇaṃ piparti mātā sa jāto viśvā bhuvanā vi caṣṭe ||
children.translated_text: The mother nourishes him, born and young; once born, he looks out upon all beings.

children.text: kas taṃ pra veda ka u taṃ ciketa yo asyā hṛdaḥ kalaśaḥ somadhāno akṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Who knows him fully? Who has perceived him, the unfailing jar in her heart that holds <s>Soma</s>?

children.text: brahmā sumedhāḥ so asmin madeta ||
children.translated_text: The inspired <s>brahman</s> (priest), rich in understanding, may rejoice in him here.

children.text: sa tau pra veda sa u tau ciketa yāv asyāḥ stanau sahasradhārāv akṣitau
children.translated_text: He knows those two, and he has discerned those two breasts of hers, thousand-streamed and inexhaustible;

children.text: ūrjaṃ duhāte anapasphurantau ||
children.translated_text: they milk out nourishment, not faltering.

children.text: hiṅkarikratī bṛhatī vayodhā uccairghoṣābhyeti yā vratam
children.translated_text: Making the hiṅ-sound, broad, giving life, with loud cry, she goes toward the vow;

children.text: trīn gharmān abhi vāvaśānā mimāti māyuṃ payate payobhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: bellowing toward the three heated draughts, she measures out the vital sound and swells with milk.

children.text: yām āpīnām upasīdanty āpaḥ śākvarā vṛṣabhā ye svarājaḥ
children.translated_text: The waters sit near her when she is full, the mighty, self-ruling bulls;

children.text: te varṣanti te varṣayanti tadvide kāmam ūrjam āpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they rain, they cause rain; the waters know that desire and nourishment.

children.text: stanayitnus te vāk prajāpate vṛṣā śuṣmaṃ kṣipasi bhūmyām adhi
children.translated_text: Thunder is your voice, O <s>Prajāpati</s>; as a bull you hurl force upon the earth.

children.text: agner vātān madhukaśā hi jajñe marutām ugrā naptiḥ ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Agni</s> and the winds the honey-whip was born, the fierce granddaughter of the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: yathā somaḥ prātaḥsavane aśvinor bhavati priyaḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Soma</s> is dear in the morning pressing to the two <s>Aśvins</s>,

children.text: evā me aśvinā varca ātmani dhriyatām ||
children.translated_text: so let <s>varcas</s> (radiant vigor) be placed in my own self, O two <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: yathā somo dvitīye savana indrāgnyor bhavati priyaḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Soma</s> is dear in the second pressing to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>,

children.text: evā ma indrāgnī varca ātmani dhriyatām ||
children.translated_text: so let <s>varcas</s> be placed in my own self, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: yathā somas tṛtīye savana ṛbhūṇāṃ bhavati priyaḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Soma</s> is dear in the third pressing to the <s>Ṛbhus</s>,

children.text: evā ma ṛbhavo varca ātmani dhriyatām ||
children.translated_text: so let <s>varcas</s> be placed in my own self, O <s>Ṛbhus</s>.

children.text: madhu janiṣīya madhu vaṃsiṣīya
children.translated_text: May I be born honeyed; may I win honey.

children.text: payasvān agna āgamaṃ taṃ mā saṃ sṛja varcasā ||
children.translated_text: Rich in milk, O <s>Agni</s>, I have come; join me with that, with <s>varcas</s>.

children.text: saṃ māgne varcasā sṛja saṃ prajayā sam āyuṣā
children.translated_text: Join me, O <s>Agni</s>, with <s>varcas</s>, join me with offspring and with lifetime.

children.text: vidyur me asya devā indro vidyāt saha ṛṣibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: May the gods know this of me; may <s>Indra</s> know it together with the seers.

children.text: yathā madhu madhukṛtaḥ saṃbharanti madhāv adhi
children.translated_text: As the honey-makers gather honey upon honey,

children.text: evā me aśvinā varca ātmani dhriyatām ||
children.translated_text: so let <s>varcas</s> be placed in my own self, O two <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: yathā makṣāḥ idaṃ madhu nyañjanti madhāv adhi
children.translated_text: As the flies smear this honey upon honey,

children.text: evā me aśvinā varcas tejo balam ojaś ca dhriyatām ||
children.translated_text: so let <s>varcas</s>, brilliance, strength, and vital force be placed in me, O two <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: yad giriṣu parvateṣu goṣv aśveṣu yan madhu
children.translated_text: Whatever honey is in hills, in mountains, in cows, and in horses,

children.text: surāyāṃ sicyamānāyāṃ yat tatra madhu tan mayi ||
children.translated_text: whatever honey is there in the liquor as it is being poured, let that honey be in me.

children.text: aśvinā sāragheṇa mā madhunāṅktaṃ śubhas patī
children.translated_text: O two <s>Aśvins</s>, lords of beauty, anoint me with the honey of the honey-bee,

children.text: yathā varcasvatīṃ vācam āvadāni janāṁ anu ||
children.translated_text: so that I may speak speech rich in <s>varcas</s> among people.

children.text: stanayitnus te vāk prajāpate vṛṣā śuṣmaṃ kṣipasi bhūmyāṃ divi
children.translated_text: Thunder is your voice, O <s>Prajāpati</s>; as a bull you hurl force upon earth and heaven.

children.text: tāṃ paśava upa jīvanti sarve teno seṣam ūrjaṃ piparti ||
children.translated_text: All cattle live upon it; by it he fills the remnant with nourishment.

children.text: pṛthivī daṇḍo 'ntarikṣaṃ garbho dyauḥ kaśā vidyut prakaśo hiraṇyayo binduḥ ||
children.translated_text: The earth is the staff, the midspace the womb, heaven the whip, lightning the shining golden drop.

children.text: yo vai kaśāyāḥ sapta madhūni veda madhumān bhavati
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the seven honeys of the whip becomes honeyed.

children.text: brāhmaṇaś ca rājā ca dhenuś cānaḍvāṃś ca vrīhiś ca yavaś ca madhu saptamam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the king, the milch cow, the draft ox, rice, barley, and honey as the seventh.

children.text: madhumān bhavati madhumad asyāhāryaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: He becomes honeyed; what is brought to him becomes honeyed.

children.text: madhumato lokān jayati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: He wins honeyed worlds, whoever knows thus.

children.text: yad vīdhre stanayati prajāpatir eva tat prajābhyaḥ prādurbhavati
children.translated_text: When it thunders in the cloud, <s>Prajāpati</s> himself becomes manifest for creatures.

children.text: tasmāt prācīnopavītas tiṣṭhe prajāpate 'nu mā budhyasveti
children.translated_text: Therefore one should stand with the sacred thread over the right shoulder, saying, 'O <s>Prajāpati</s>, notice me.'

children.text: anv enaṃ prajā anu prajāpatir budhyate ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: The creatures notice him, and <s>Prajāpati</s> notices him, whoever knows thus.

children.text: Chapter 440
sapatnahanam ṛṣabhaṃ ghṛtena kāmaṃ śikṣāmi haviṣājyena
children.translated_text: With ghee, with oblation and clarified butter, I instruct <s>Kāma</s>, the bull who slays rivals.

children.text: nīcaiḥ sapatnān mama padaya tvam abhiṣṭuto mahatā vīryeṇa ||
children.translated_text: Cast down my rivals beneath me, you who are praised with great heroic power.

children.text: yan me manaso na priyaṃ cakṣuṣo yan me babhasti nābhinandati
children.translated_text: Whatever is not dear to my mind, whatever devours what belongs to my eye and does not rejoice me,

children.text: tad duṣvapnyaṃ prati muñcāmi sapatne kāmaṃ stutvod ahaṃ bhideyam ||
children.translated_text: that bad dream I release against the rival; having praised <s>Kāma</s>, may I break through upward.

children.text: duṣvapnyaṃ kāma duritaṃ ca kāmāprajastām asvagatām avartim
children.translated_text: Bad dream, O <s>Kāma</s>, evil, O <s>Kāma</s>, childlessness, homelessness, and failure,

children.text: ugra īśānaḥ prati muñca tasmin yo asmabhyam aṃhūraṇā cikitsāt ||
children.translated_text: as the fierce ruler, release these upon the one who seeks to do harm to us.

children.text: nudasva kāma pra ṇudasva kāmāvartiṃ yantu mama ye sapatnāḥ
children.translated_text: Drive them away, O <s>Kāma</s>; drive them forth, O <s>Kāma</s>. Let those rivals of mine go to failure.

children.text: teṣāṃ nuttānām adhamā tamāṃsy agne vāstūni nir daha tvam ||
children.translated_text: When they have been driven away, burn down their lowest dwellings in the darkness, O <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: sā te kāma duhitā dhenur ucyate yām āhur vācaṃ kavayo virājam
children.translated_text: That daughter of yours, O <s>Kāma</s>, is called a milch cow, whom the poets call speech, <s>Virāj</s>.

children.text: tayā sapatnān pari vṛṅgdhi ye mama pary enān prāṇaḥ paśavo jīvanaṃ vṛṇaktu ||
children.translated_text: With her hem in my rivals; let breath, cattle, and life hem them in on every side.

children.text: kāmasyendrasya varuṇasya rājño viṣṇor balena savituḥ savena
children.translated_text: By the strength of <s>Kāma</s>, of <s>Indra</s>, of king <s>Varuṇa</s>, of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and by the impulse of <s>Savitṛ</s>,

children.text: agner hotreṇa pra ṇude sapatnāṁ chambīva nāvam udakeṣu dhīraḥ ||
children.translated_text: by the priesthood of <s>Agni</s>, drive forth the rivals, as a skilled man drives a boat on the waters.

children.text: adhyakṣo vājī mama kāma ugraḥ kṛṇotu mahyam asapatnam eva
children.translated_text: Let <s>Kāma</s>, the overseer, the steed, the fierce one, make this for me alone: freedom from rivals.

children.text: viśve devā mama nāthaṃ bhavantu sarve devā havam ā yantu ma imam ||
children.translated_text: Let all the gods be my protectors; let all the gods come to this call of mine.

children.text: idam ājyaṃ ghṛtavaj juṣāṇāḥ kāmajyeṣṭhā iha mādayadhvam
children.translated_text: Enjoying this clarified butter rich in ghee, you for whom <s>Kāma</s> is chief, rejoice here,

children.text: kṛṇvanto mahyam asapatnam eva ||
children.translated_text: making me without any rival.

children.text: indrāgnī kāma sarathaṃ hi bhūtvā nīcaiḥ sapatnān mama pādayāthaḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, O <s>Kāma</s>, having become companions in one chariot, cast my rivals down beneath me.

children.text: teṣāṃ pannānām adhamā tamāṃsy agne vāstūny anu nirdaha tvam ||
children.translated_text: When they have fallen, burn down their lowest dwellings in the darkness, O <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: jahi tvam kāma mama ye sapatnā andhā tamāṃsy ava pādayainān
children.translated_text: Slay those rivals of mine, O <s>Kāma</s>; cast them down into blind darkness.

children.text: nirindriyā arasāḥ santu sarve mā te jīviṣuḥ katamac canāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let them all be without faculty and without savor; let not one of them live for even a single day.

children.text: avadhīt kāmo mama ye sapatnā uruṃ lokam akaran mahyam edhatum
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s> has struck down those rivals of mine; they have made a broad world for me to prosper in.

children.text: mahyaṃ namantāṃ pradiśaś catasro mahyaṃ ṣaḍ urvīr ghṛtam ā vahantu ||
children.translated_text: Let the four directions bow to me; let the six wide regions bring ghee to me.

children.text: te 'dharāñcaḥ pra plavantāṃ chinnā naur iva bandhanāt
children.translated_text: Let them float downward, like a boat cut loose from its mooring.

children.text: na sāyakapraṇuttānāṃ punar asti nivartanam ||
children.translated_text: For those driven forth by the arrow there is no return again.

children.text: agnir yava indro yavaḥ somo yavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> is barley, <s>Indra</s> is barley, <s>Soma</s> is barley.

children.text: yavayāvāno devā yavayantv enam ||
children.translated_text: Let the gods who drive away with barley drive this man away.

children.text: asarvavīraś caratu praṇutto dveṣyo mitrānāṃ parivargyaḥ svānām
children.translated_text: Let the hated one, driven forth, go about without all his heroes, excluded from friends and from his own people.

children.text: uta pṛthivyām ava syanti vidyuta ugro vo devaḥ pra mṛṇat sapatnān ||
children.translated_text: And on the earth the lightnings shall fall; your fierce god shall crush the rivals.

children.text: cyutā ceyaṃ bṛhaty acyutā ca vidyud bibharti stanayitnūṃś ca sarvān
children.translated_text: This <s>Bṛhatī</s> has been shaken and is unshaken, and lightning bears all the thunders.

children.text: udyann ādityo draviṇena tejasā nīcaiḥ sapatnān nudatāṃ me sahasvān ||
children.translated_text: May the rising <s>Āditya</s>, with wealth and splendor, powerfully drive my rivals downward.

children.text: yat te kāma śarma trivarūtham udbhu brahma varma vitatam anativyādhyaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: O <s>Kāma</s>, whatever threefold shelter of yours has arisen, the <s>brahman</s> (sacred formulation), a shield spread out and made impenetrable,

children.text: tena sapatnān pari vṛṅgdhi ye mama pary enān prāṇaḥ paśavo jīvanaṃ vṛṇaktu ||
children.translated_text: with that hem in the rivals who are mine; let breath, cattle, and life itself choose away from them.

children.text: yena devā asurān prāṇudanta yenendro dasyūn adhamaṃ tamo nināya
children.translated_text: By that with which the gods drove away the <s>Asuras</s>, by which <s>Indra</s> led the <s>Dasyus</s> into the lowest darkness,

children.text: tena tvaṃ kāma mama ye sapatnās tān asmāl lokāt pra ṇudasva dūram ||
children.translated_text: by that, O <s>Kāma</s>, drive those rivals of mine far away from this world.

children.text: yathā devā asurān prāṇudanta yathendro dasyūn adhamaṃ tamo babādhe
children.translated_text: As the gods drove away the <s>Asuras</s>, as <s>Indra</s> struck the <s>Dasyus</s> down into the lowest darkness,

children.text: tathā tvaṃ kāma mama ye sapatnās tān asmāl lokāt pra ṇudasva dūram ||
children.translated_text: so, O <s>Kāma</s>, drive those rivals of mine far away from this world.

children.text: kāmo jajñe prathamo nainaṃ devā āpuḥ pitaro na martyāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s> was born first; neither the gods, nor the Fathers, nor mortals have reached him.

children.text: tatas tvam asi jyāyān viśvahā mahāṃs tasmai te kāma nama it kṛṇomi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore you are greater, always universal and great; to you, O <s>Kāma</s>, I make this homage.

children.text: yāvatī dyāvāpṛthivī varimṇā yāvad āpaḥ siṣyadur yāvad agniḥ
children.translated_text: As far as heaven and earth extend in breadth, as far as the waters have flowed, as far as fire reaches,

children.text: tatas tvam asi jyāyān viśvahā mahāṃs tasmai te kāma nama it kṛṇomi ||
children.translated_text: beyond that you are greater, always universal and great; to you, O <s>Kāma</s>, I make this homage.

children.text: yāvatīr diśaḥ pradiśo viṣūcīr yāvatīr āśā abhicakṣaṇā divaḥ
children.translated_text: As many directions, intermediate directions, and separate quarters as there are, as many visible regions of heaven as there are,

children.text: tatas tvam asi jyāyān viśvahā mahāṃs tasmai te kāma nama it kṛṇomi ||
children.translated_text: beyond that you are greater, always universal and great; to you, O <s>Kāma</s>, I make this homage.

children.text: yāvatīr bhṛṅgā jatvaḥ kurūravo yāvatīr vaghā vṛkṣasarpyo babhūvuḥ
children.translated_text: As many flying insects, gnats, curlew-like birds, as many stinging creatures and tree-serpents as have come into being,

children.text: tatas tvam asi jyāyān viśvahā mahāṃs tasmai te kāma nama it kṛṇomi ||
children.translated_text: beyond that you are greater, always universal and great; to you, O <s>Kāma</s>, I make this homage.

children.text: jyāyān nimiṣato 'si tiṣṭhato jyāyānt samudrād asi kāma manyo
children.translated_text: You are greater than what blinks and what stands still; you are greater than the ocean, O <s>Kāma</s>, O <s>Manyu</s>.

children.text: tatas tvam asi jyāyān viśvahā mahāṃs tasmai te kāma nama it kṛṇomi ||
children.translated_text: Beyond that you are greater, always universal and great; to you, O <s>Kāma</s>, I make this homage.

children.text: na vai vātaś cana kāmam āpnoti nāgniḥ sūryo nota candramāḥ
children.translated_text: Not even the wind reaches <s>Kāma</s>, nor fire, nor the sun, nor the moon.

children.text: tatas tvam asi jyāyān viśvahā mahāṃs tasmai te kāma nama it kṛṇomi ||
children.translated_text: Beyond that you are greater, always universal and great; to you, O <s>Kāma</s>, I make this homage.

children.text: yās te śivās tanvaḥ kāma bhadrā yābhiḥ satyaṃ bhavati yad vṛṇīṣe
children.translated_text: Those auspicious, kindly bodies of yours, O <s>Kāma</s>, through which what you choose becomes true,

children.text: tābhiṣ ṭvam asmāṁ abhisaṃviśasvānyatra pāpīr apa veśayā dhiyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with those enter into us here; set the evil thoughts down elsewhere, away from us.

children.text: Chapter 441
upamitāṃ pratimitām atho parimitām uta
children.translated_text: Measured alongside, measured in correspondence, and also measured all around,

children.text: śālāyā viśvavārāyā naddhāni vi cṛtāmasi ||
children.translated_text: we loosen the fastenings of the all-protecting house.

children.text: yat te naddhaṃ viśvavāre pāśo granthiś ca yaḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever bond of yours is tied, O all-protecting one, and whatever knot has been made,

children.text: bṛhaspatir ivāhaṃ balaṃ vācā vi sraṃsayāmi tat ||
children.translated_text: like <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, I undo that strength with speech.

children.text: ā yayāma saṃ babarha granthīṃś cakāra te dṛḍhān
children.translated_text: He came here; he gathered it together; he made your knots firm.

children.text: parūṃṣi vidvāṁ chastevendreṇa vi cṛtāmasi ||
children.translated_text: Knowing the joints, as a cutter might, we loosen them with <s>Indra</s>'s help.

children.text: vaṃśānāṃ te nahanānāṃ prāṇāhasya tṛṇasya ca
children.translated_text: Of your bamboos, your lashings, of the prāṇāha grass and the thatching grass,

children.text: pakṣāṇāṃ viśvavāre te naddhāni vi cṛtāmasi ||
children.translated_text: of your wings, O all-protecting one, we loosen the fastenings.

children.text: saṃdaṃśānāṃ paladānāṃ pariṣvañjalyasya ca
children.translated_text: Of the clamps, the splints, and what is wrapped around and embraced,

children.text: idaṃ mānasya patnyā naddhāni vi cṛtāmasi ||
children.translated_text: we loosen the fastenings of this house, the wife of man.

children.text: yāni te 'ntaḥ śikyāny ābedhū raṇyāya kam
children.translated_text: Those inner hanging loops of yours, fitted in for use in the forest,

children.text: pra te tāni cṛtāmasi śivā mānasya patni na uddhitā tanve bhava ||
children.translated_text: we loosen them for you; O auspicious wife of man, when raised up, be for our body.

children.text: havirdhānam agniśālaṃ patnīnāṃ sadanaṃ sadaḥ
children.translated_text: You are the havirdhāna shed, the fire-house, the women's dwelling, and the sitting-place;

children.text: sado devānām asi devi śāle ||
children.translated_text: you are the seat of the gods, O divine house.

children.text: akṣum opaśaṃ vitataṃ sahasrākṣaṃ viṣūvati
children.translated_text: The woven covering, spread out, thousand-eyed, facing every way,

children.text: avanaddham abhihitaṃ brahmaṇā vi cṛtāmasi ||
children.translated_text: bound down and laid over, we loosen with <s>brahman</s> (sacred formulation).

children.text: yas tvā śāle pratigṛhṇāti yena cāsi mitā tvam
children.translated_text: Whoever receives you, O house, and by whom you have been measured,

children.text: ubhau mānasya patni tau jīvatāṃ jaradaṣṭī ||
children.translated_text: may both of them, O wife of man, live to old age with teeth intact.

children.text: amutrainam ā gachatād dṛḍhā naddhā pariṣkṛtā
children.translated_text: Let him come here from that place, firmly bound and well adorned,

children.text: yasyās te vicṛtāmasy aṅgamaṅgaṃ paruṣ paruḥ ||
children.translated_text: he whose every limb and every joint of yours we loosen.

children.text: yas tvā śāle nimimāya saṃjabhāra vanaspatīn
children.translated_text: Whoever measured you out, O house, and brought together the forest-trees,

children.text: prajāyai cakre tvā śāle parameṣṭhī prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for offspring <s>Parameṣṭhin Prajāpati</s> made you, O house.

children.text: namas tasmai namo dātre śālāpataye ca kṛṇmaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to him, homage to the giver, and to the lord of the house we make;

children.text: namo 'gnaye pracarate puruṣāya ca te namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: homage to the moving fire, and homage to your man.

children.text: gobhyo aśvebhyo namo yacchālāyāṃ vijāyate
children.translated_text: Homage to the cows and horses, to whatever is born in the house;

children.text: vijāvati prajāvati vi te pāśāṃś cṛtāmasi ||
children.translated_text: rich in birth, rich in offspring, we loosen your bonds.

children.text: agnim antaś chādayasi puruṣān paśubhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: You cover fire within yourself, together with men and cattle;

children.text: vijāvati prajāvati vi te pāśāṃś cṛtāmasi ||
children.translated_text: rich in birth, rich in offspring, we loosen your bonds.

children.text: antarā dyāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca yad vyacas tena śālāṃ prati gṛhṇāmi ta imām
children.translated_text: Whatever expanse lies between heaven and earth, with that I receive this house of yours.

children.text: yad antarikṣaṃ rajaso vimānaṃ tat kṛṇve 'ham udaraṃ śevadhibhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever midspace is the measure of the atmosphere, that I make a belly for treasures;

children.text: tena śālāṃ prati gṛhṇāmi tasmai ||
children.translated_text: with that I receive the house for that purpose.

children.text: ūrjasvatī payasvatī pṛthivyāṃ nimitā mitā
children.translated_text: Full of nourishment, full of milk, set up and measured upon the earth,

children.text: viśvānnaṃ bibhratī śāle mā hiṃsīḥ pratigṛhṇataḥ ||
children.translated_text: bearing all food, O house, do not injure those who receive you.

children.text: tṛṇair āvṛtā paladān vasānā rātrīva śālā jagato niveśanī
children.translated_text: Covered with grasses, clothed in straw, like night, the house is the dwelling-place of the world;

children.text: mitā pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhasi hastinīva padvatī ||
children.translated_text: measured upon the earth you stand, footed like an elephant-cow.

children.text: iṭasya te vi cṛtāmy apinaddham aporṇuvan
children.translated_text: I loosen what is fastened onto your joinery, unwrapping it;

children.text: varuṇena samubjitāṃ mitraḥ prātar vy ubjatu ||
children.translated_text: propped up by <s>Varuṇa</s>, let <s>Mitra</s> prop it open in the morning.

children.text: brahmaṇā śālāṃ nimitāṃ kavibhir nimitāṃ mitām
children.translated_text: The house set up by <s>brahman</s> (sacred formulation), set up and measured by seers,

children.text: indrāgnī rakṣatāṃ śālām amṛtau somyaṃ sadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, immortal, protect the house, the soma-seat.

children.text: kulāye 'dhi kulāyaṃ kośe kośaḥ samubjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Nest upon nest, vessel upon vessel has been set up together;

children.text: tatra marto vi jāyate yasmād viśvaṃ prajāyate ||
children.translated_text: there a mortal is born forth, from which everything is born forth.

children.text: yā dvipakṣā catuṣpakṣā ṣaṭpakṣā yā nimīyate
children.translated_text: The house that is built with two wings, four wings, six wings,

children.text: aṣṭāpakṣāṃ daśapakṣāṃ śālāṃ mānasya patnīm agnir garbha ivā śaye ||
children.translated_text: with eight wings or ten wings, the wife of man: <s>Agni</s> lies within her like an embryo.

children.text: pratīcīṃ tvā pratīcīnaḥ śāle praimy ahiṃsatīm
children.translated_text: Facing west, I, facing west, come forward to you, O house, unharming;

children.text: agnir hy antar āpaś ca ṛtasya prathamā dvāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for <s>Agni</s> is within, and the waters too, the first doors of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order).

children.text: imā āpaḥ pra bharāmy ayakṣmā yakṣmanāśanīḥ
children.translated_text: I bring forward these waters, free from <s>yakṣma</s> (consumptive disease), destroyers of <s>yakṣma</s>.

children.text: gṛhān upa pra sīdāmy amṛtena sahāgninā ||
children.translated_text: I take my seat in the house, together with immortality and with <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: mā naḥ pāśaṃ prati muco gurur bhāro laghur bhava
children.translated_text: Do not release a snare against us; heavy burden, become light.

children.text: vadhūm iva tvā śāle yatrakāmaṃ bharāmasi ||
children.translated_text: Like a bride, O house, we carry you wherever we wish.

children.text: prācyā diśaḥ śālāyā namo mahimne svāhā devebhyaḥ svāhyebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the greatness of the house in the eastern direction; svāhā to the gods and to those worthy of svāhā.

children.text: dakṣiṇāyā diśaḥ śālāyā namo mahimne svāhā devebhyaḥ svāhyebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the greatness of the house in the southern direction; svāhā to the gods and to those worthy of svāhā.

children.text: pratīcyā diśaḥ śālāyā namo mahimne svāhā devebhyaḥ svāhyebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the greatness of the house in the western direction; svāhā to the gods and to those worthy of svāhā.

children.text: udīcyā diśaḥ śālāyā namo mahimne svāhā devebhyaḥ svāhyebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the greatness of the house in the northern direction; svāhā to the gods and to those worthy of svāhā.

children.text: dhruvāyā diśaḥ śālāyā namo mahimne svāhā devebhyaḥ svāhyebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the greatness of the house in the fixed direction; svāhā to the gods and to those worthy of svāhā.

children.text: ūrdhvāyā diśaḥ śālāyā namo mahimne svāhā devebhyaḥ svāhyebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the greatness of the house in the upward direction; svāhā to the gods and to those worthy of svāhā.

children.text: diśo diśaḥ śālāyā namo mahimne svāhā devebhyaḥ svāhyebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the greatness of the house in every direction; svāhā to the gods and to those worthy of svāhā.

children.text: Chapter 442
sāhasras tveṣa ṛṣabhaḥ payasvān viśvā rūpāṇi vakṣaṇāsu bibhrat
children.translated_text: The thousandfold, blazing, milk-rich bull, bearing all forms upon his flanks,

children.text: bhadraṃ dātre yajamānāya śikṣan bārhaspatya usriyas tantum ātān ||
children.translated_text: bestowing good on the giver, the sacrificer, the <s>Bārhaspatya</s> ox has stretched out the thread.

children.text: apāṃ yo agne pratimā babhūva prabhūḥ sarvasmai pṛthivīva devī
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, he who became the counterpart of the waters, lord over all like the divine Earth,

children.text: pitā vatsānāṃ patir aghnyānāṃ sāhasre poṣe api naḥ kṛṇotu ||
children.translated_text: father of calves, lord of inviolate cows, may he set us in thousandfold nourishment.

children.text: pumān antarvānt sthaviraḥ payasvān vasoḥ kabandhaṃ ṛṣabho bibharti
children.translated_text: A male with life within, ancient and milk-rich, the bull bears the vessel of wealth.

children.text: tam indrāya pathibhir devayānair hutam agnir vahatu jātavedāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let <s>Agni Jātavedas</s> carry him, offered to <s>Indra</s>, along the paths that lead to the gods.

children.text: pitā vatsānāṃ patir aghnyānāṃ atho pitā mahatāṃ gargarāṇām
children.translated_text: He is father of calves, lord of inviolate cows, and also father of the great roaring ones.

children.text: vatso jarāyu pratidhuk pīyūṣa āmikṣā ghṛtaṃ tad v asya retaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The calf, the afterbirth, the milk drawn back, the first milk, curds, and ghee: that indeed is his seed.

children.text: devānāṃ bhāga upanāha eṣo 'pāṃ rasa oṣadhīnāṃ ghṛtasya
children.translated_text: This binding is the portion of the gods, the essence of the waters, of the plants, and of ghee.

children.text: somasya bhakṣam avṛṇīta śakro bṛhann adrir abhavad yaccharīram ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> chose the draught of <s>Soma</s>; the great stone became what is his body.

children.text: somena pūrṇaṃ kalaśaṃ bibharṣi tvaṣṭā rūpāṇāṃ janitā paśūnām
children.translated_text: You bear the jar filled with <s>Soma</s>; <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> is the begetter of forms and of cattle.

children.text: śivās te santu prajanva iha yā imā ny asmabhyaṃ svadhite yaccha yā amūḥ ||
children.translated_text: May your offspring here be auspicious; O axe, hand over to us these that are here and those that are yonder.

children.text: ājyaṃ bibharti ghṛtam asya retaḥ sāhasraḥ poṣas tam u yajñam āhuḥ
children.translated_text: He bears the clarified butter; ghee is his seed. They call that thousandfold nourishment the sacrifice itself.

children.text: indrasya rūpam ṛṣabho vasānaḥ so asmān devāḥ śiva aitu dattaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Clothed in the form of <s>Indra</s>, let that bull, given by the gods, come to us auspiciously.

children.text: indrasyaujo varuṇasya bāhū aśvinor aṃsau marutām iyaṃ kakut
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>'s strength, <s>Varuṇa</s>'s arms, the two shoulders of the <s>Aśvins</s>, this hump of the <s>Maruts</s>:

children.text: bṛhaspatiṃ saṃbhṛtam etam āhur ye dhīrāsaḥ kavayo ye manīṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise, the poets, and the thoughtful say that this one has been compounded as <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: daivīr viśaḥ payasvān ā tanoṣi tvām indraṃ tvāṃ sarasvantam āhuḥ
children.translated_text: Rich in milk, you stretch out the divine clans; they call you <s>Indra</s>, they call you <s>Sarasvant</s>.

children.text: sahasraṃ sa ekamukhā dadāti yo brāhmaṇa ṛṣabham ājuhoti ||
children.translated_text: He gives a thousand through that single-mouthed one, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who offers up a bull.

children.text: bṛhaspatiḥ savitā te vayo dadhau tvaṣṭur vāyoḥ pary ātmā ta ābhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and <s>Savitṛ</s> placed vigor in you; your self has been brought from <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: antarikṣe manasā tvā juhomi barhiṣ ṭe dyāvāpṛthivī ubhe stām ||
children.translated_text: In the midspace I offer you with my mind; let both Heaven and Earth be your sacrificial grass.

children.text: ya indra iva deveṣu goṣv eti vivāvadat
children.translated_text: He who, like <s>Indra</s> among the gods, goes bellowing among the cows,

children.text: tasya ṛṣabhasyāṅgāni brahmā saṃ stautu bhadrayā ||
children.translated_text: let the Brahman priest praise the limbs of that bull with auspicious praise.

children.text: pārśve āstām anumatyā bhagasyāstām anūvṛjau
children.translated_text: The two sides belonged to <s>Anumati</s>; the two haunches belonged to <s>Bhaga</s>.

children.text: aṣṭhīvantāv abravīn mitro mamaitau kevalāv iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mitra</s> said, 'These two bony ones are mine alone.'

children.text: bhasad āsīd ādityānāṃ śroṇī āstāṃ bṛhaspateḥ
children.translated_text: The rump belonged to the <s>Ādityas</s>; the two hips belonged to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: pucchaṃ vātasya devasya tena dhūnoty oṣadhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: The tail belonged to the god <s>Vāta</s>; with it he shakes the herbs.

children.text: gudā āsant sinīvālyāḥ sūryāyās tvacam abruvan
children.translated_text: The entrails belonged to <s>Sinīvālī</s>; they declared the skin to belong to <s>Sūryā</s>.

children.text: utthātur abruvan pada ṛṣabhaṃ yad akalpayan ||
children.translated_text: They declared the feet to belong to the one who rises up, when they fashioned the bull.

children.text: kroḍa āsīj jāmiśaṃsasya somasya kalaśo dhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The breast belonged to <s>Jāmiśaṃsa</s>; the held jar belonged to <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: devāḥ saṃgatya yat sarva ṛṣabhaṃ vyakalpayan ||
children.translated_text: This was when all the gods, having come together, apportioned the bull.

children.text: te kuṣṭhikāḥ saramāyai kūrmebhyo adadhuḥ śaphān
children.translated_text: They gave the little swellings to <s>Saramā</s> and the hooves to the tortoises.

children.text: ūbadhyam asya kīṭebhyaḥ śvavartebhyo adhārayan ||
children.translated_text: They assigned his lower belly to the insects and to the śvavartas.

children.text: śṛṅgābhyāṃ rakṣa ṛṣaty avartim hanti cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: With his horns he pierces the <s>rakṣas</s> (demon); with his eye he strikes down distress.

children.text: śṛṇoti bhadraṃ karṇābhyāṃ gavāṃ yaḥ patir aghnyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With his ears he hears what is auspicious, he who is lord of the cows, the inviolate one.

children.text: śatayājaṃ sa yajate nainaṃ dunvanty agnayaḥ
children.translated_text: He sacrifices with a hundredfold sacrifice; the fires do not distress him.

children.text: jinvanti viśve taṃ devā yo brāhmaṇa ṛṣabham ājuhoti ||
children.translated_text: All the gods quicken the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who offers up a bull.

children.text: brāhmaṇebhya ṛṣabhaṃ dattvā varīyaḥ kṛṇute manaḥ
children.translated_text: Having given a bull to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, he makes his mind broader.

children.text: puṣṭiṃ so aghnyānāṃ sve goṣṭhe 'va paśyate ||
children.translated_text: He sees the prosperity of the inviolate cows in his own cattle pen.

children.text: gāvaḥ santu prajāḥ santv atho astu tanūbalam
children.translated_text: Let there be cows; let there be offspring; and let there be strength of body.

children.text: tat sarvam anu manyantāṃ devā ṛṣabhadāyine ||
children.translated_text: May the gods assent to all that for the giver of a bull.

children.text: ayaṃ pipāna indra id rayiṃ dadhātu cetanīm
children.translated_text: May this drinking one, <s>Indra</s> indeed, set in place living wealth.

children.text: ayaṃ dhenuṃ sudughāṃ nityavatsāṃ vaśaṃ duhāṃ vipaścitaṃ paro divaḥ ||
children.translated_text: May this one set in place a cow easy to milk, always with calf, obedient to the milking, wise, beyond heaven.

children.text: piśaṅgarūpo nabhaso vayodhā aindraḥ śuṣmo viśvarūpo na āgan
children.translated_text: Brown in form, strength-giving from the sky, <s>Indra</s>'s force, all-formed, has come to us.

children.text: āyur asmabhyaṃ dadhat prajāṃ ca rāyaś ca poṣair abhi naḥ sacatām ||
children.translated_text: Bestowing life and offspring on us, may he attend us with wealth and prosperities.

children.text: upehopaparcanāsmin goṣṭha upa pṛñca naḥ
children.translated_text: Come here for reverent tending; in this cattle pen, come and fill us.

children.text: upa ṛṣabhasya yad reta upendra tava vīryam ||
children.translated_text: Come with what is the bull's seed, O <s>Upendra</s>, your heroic power.

children.text: etaṃ vo yuvānaṃ prati dadhmo atra tena krīḍantīś carata vaśāṁ anu
children.translated_text: We set this young one here for you; playing with him, move among the cows.

children.text: mā no hāsiṣṭa januṣā subhāgā rāyaś ca poṣair abhi naḥ sacadhvam ||
children.translated_text: Do not abandon us by birth, O fortunate ones; attend us with wealth and prosperities.

children.text: Chapter 443
ā nayaitam ā rabhasva sukṛtāṃ lokam api gachatu prajānan
children.translated_text: Bring this one here; take hold of him. Knowing, let him go to the world of the well-done.

children.text: tīrtvā tamāṃsi bahudhā mahānty ajo nākam ā kramatāṃ tṛtīyam ||
children.translated_text: Having crossed the many great darknesses, let the goat ascend the third heaven.

children.text: indrāya bhāgaṃ pari tvā nayāmy asmin yajñe yajamānāya sūrim
children.translated_text: I lead you around as <s>Indra</s>'s portion, as a liberal patron for the sacrificer in this sacrifice.

children.text: ye no dviṣanty anu tān rabhasvānāgaso yajamānasya vīrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who hate us, attack them; the sacrificer's heroes are without guilt.

children.text: pra pado 'va nenigdhi duścaritaṃ yac cacāra śuddhaiḥ śaphair ā kramatāṃ prajānan
children.translated_text: Wipe clean the feet from whatever misdeed he has committed; with purified hoofs, knowing, let him step forward.

children.text: tīrtvā tamāṃsi bahudhā vipaśyann ajo nākam ā kramatāṃ tṛtīyam ||
children.translated_text: Having crossed the darknesses and seeing in many ways, let the goat mount the third heaven.

children.text: anuchya śyāmena tvacam etāṃ viśastar yathāparv asinā mābhi maṃsthāḥ
children.translated_text: Having followed this skin with the dark blade, O dissector, do not injure it joint by joint with the knife.

children.text: mābhi druhaḥ paruśaḥ kalpayainaṃ tṛtīye nāke adhi vi śrayainam ||
children.translated_text: Do not harm it harshly; prepare this one, and set him down upon the third heaven.

children.text: ṛcā kumbhīm adhy agnau śrayāmy ā siñcodakam ava dhehy enam
children.translated_text: With a verse I set the pot over the fire. Pour in the water; place this one in it.

children.text: paryādhattāgninā śamitāraḥ śṛto gachatu sukṛtāṃ yatra lokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O slaughterers, cover it round with fire; when cooked, let it go where the world of the well-doers is.

children.text: ut krāmātaḥ pari ced ataptas taptāc caror adhi nākaṃ tṛtīyam
children.translated_text: Rise up from here, if you are still uncooked; from the cooked oblation rise to the third heaven.

children.text: agner agnir adhi saṃ babhūvitha jyotiṣmantam abhi lokaṃ jayaitam ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Agni</s> you have become <s>Agni</s>; win this radiant world.

children.text: ajo agnir ajam u jyotir āhur ajaṃ jīvatā brahmaṇe deyam āhuḥ
children.translated_text: The goat is <s>Agni</s>; they call the goat light; they say that the goat is to be given alive to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: ajas tamāṃsy apa hanti dūram asmiṃl loke śraddadhānena dattaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Given with faith in this world, the goat drives the darknesses far away.

children.text: pañcaudanaḥ pañcadhā vi kramatām ākraṃsyamānas trīṇi jyotīṃṣi
children.translated_text: Let the five-rice-dish step forth fivefold, stepping over the three lights.

children.text: ījānānāṃ sukṛtāṃ prehi madhyaṃ tṛtīye nāke adhi vi śrayasva ||
children.translated_text: Go to the midst of the well-doers who have sacrificed; settle upon the third heaven.

children.text: ajā roha sukṛtāṃ yatra lokaḥ śarabho na catto 'ti durgāny eṣaḥ
children.translated_text: O goat, climb to where the world of the well-doers is; like a <s>śarabha</s>, unharmed, you pass beyond difficulties.

children.text: pañcaudano brahmaṇe dīyamānaḥ sa dātāraṃ tṛptyā tarpayāti ||
children.translated_text: The five-rice-dish, when given to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, satisfies the giver with satisfaction.

children.text: ajas trināke tridive tripṛṣṭhe nākasya pṛṣṭhe dadivāṃsaṃ dadhāti
children.translated_text: In the triple heaven, in the triple sky, on the three-backed back of heaven, the goat places the man who has given.

children.text: pañcaudano brahmaṇe dīyamāno viśvarūpā dhenuḥ kāmadughāsy ekā ||
children.translated_text: The five-rice-dish, when given to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, will be your one all-formed cow that yields every desire.

children.text: etad vo jyotiḥ pitaras tṛtīyaṃ pañcaudanaṃ brahmaṇe 'jaṃ dadāti
children.translated_text: This is your third light, O Fathers: he gives the five-rice-dish goat to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: ajas tamāṃsy apa hanti dūram asmiṃl loke śraddadhānena dattaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Given with faith in this world, the goat drives the darknesses far away.

children.text: ījānānāṃ sukṛtāṃ lokam īpsan pañcaudanaṃ brahmaṇe 'jaṃ dadāti
children.translated_text: Seeking the world of the well-doers among those who have sacrificed, he gives the five-rice-dish goat to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: sa vyāptim abhi lokaṃ jayaitaṃ śivo 'smabhyaṃ pratigṛhīto astu ||
children.translated_text: May he win this world of full expanse; received, may he be auspicious for us.

children.text: ajo hy agner ajaniṣṭa śokād vipro viprasya sahaso vipaścit
children.translated_text: For the goat was born from the flame of <s>Agni</s>, a sage from the sage of mighty force, the discerning one.

children.text: iṣṭaṃ pūrtam abhipūrtaṃ vaṣaṭkṛtaṃ tad devā ṛtuśaḥ kalpayantu ||
children.translated_text: May the gods arrange in due seasons that which is sacrificed, fulfilled, abundantly fulfilled, and consecrated with <s>vaṣaṭ</s>.

children.text: amotaṃ vāso dadyāddhiraṇyam api dakṣiṇām
children.translated_text: One should give a garment and gold also as the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.

children.text: tathā lokānt sam āpnoti ye divyā ye ca pārthivāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus he obtains the worlds, those that are heavenly and those that are earthly.

children.text: etās tvājopa yantu dhārāḥ somyā devīr ghṛtapṛṣṭhā madhuścutaḥ
children.translated_text: Let these streams come to you, O goat, Soma-like, divine, with backs of ghee and dripping honey.

children.text: stabhān pṛthivīm uta dyāṃ nākasya pṛṣṭhe 'dhi saptaraśmau ||
children.translated_text: Support the earth and also heaven, upon the back of heaven, upon the seven-rayed one.

children.text: ajo 'sy aja svargo 'si tvayā lokam aṅgirasaḥ prājānan
children.translated_text: You are the goat; O goat, you are heaven. Through you the <s>Aṅgirases</s> came to know the world.

children.text: taṃ lokaṃ puṇyaṃ pra jñeṣam ||
children.translated_text: May I come to know that blessed world.

children.text: yenā sahasraṃ vahasi yenāgne sarvavedasam
children.translated_text: By that with which you carry a thousand, O <s>Agni</s>, by that with which you carry all wealth,

children.text: tenemaṃ yajñaṃ no vaha svar deveṣu gantave ||
children.translated_text: by that carry this sacrifice of ours to heaven, so that it may go among the gods.

children.text: ajaḥ pakvaḥ svarge loke dadhāti pañcaudano nirṛtiṃ bādhamānaḥ
children.translated_text: The cooked goat, the five-rice-dish, driving away <s>Nirṛti</s>, sets one in the heavenly world.

children.text: tena lokānt sūryavato jayema ||
children.translated_text: By it may we win worlds possessed of the sun.

children.text: yaṃ brāhmaṇe nidadhe yaṃ ca vikṣu yā vipruṣa odanānām ajasya
children.translated_text: What I have placed in the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and what among the settlements, whatever drops there are of the goat's rice dishes,

children.text: sarvaṃ tad agne sukṛtasya loke jānītān naḥ saṃgamane pathīnām ||
children.translated_text: all that, O <s>Agni</s>, in the world of the well-doer, may it know the paths for us at the meeting-place of the ways.

children.text: ajo vā idam agne vy akramata tasyora iyam abhavad dyauḥ pṛṣṭham
children.translated_text: The goat, indeed, has stepped out through this, O <s>Agni</s>; this earth became its breast, heaven its back,

children.text: antarikṣaṃ madhyam diśaḥ pārśve samudrau kukṣī ||
children.translated_text: the midspace its middle, the directions its sides, and the oceans its bellies.

children.text: satyaṃ cartaṃ ca cakṣuṣī viśvaṃ satyaṃ śraddhā prāṇo virāṭ śiraḥ
children.translated_text: Truth and <s>ṛta</s> are its eyes; the All, truth, and faith are its breath; <s>Virāj</s> is its head.

children.text: eṣa vā aparimito yajño yad ajaḥ pañcaudanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For this, the five-rice-dish goat, is an immeasurable sacrifice.

children.text: aparimitam eva yajñam āpnoty aparimitaṃ lokam ava runddhe
children.translated_text: He obtains an immeasurable sacrifice and secures an immeasurable world,

children.text: yo 'jaṃ pañcaudanaṃ dakṣiṇājyotiṣaṃ dadāti ||
children.translated_text: who gives the five-rice-dish goat furnished with the light of the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.

children.text: nāsyāsthīni bhindyān na majjño nir dhayet
children.translated_text: One should not break its bones, nor should one draw out the marrow.

children.text: sarvam enaṃ samādāyedamidaṃ pra veśayet ||
children.translated_text: One should gather it all together and place each part in its proper place.

children.text: idamidam evāsya rūpaṃ bhavati tenainaṃ saṃ gamayati
children.translated_text: Each part becomes precisely its own form; by that he brings this one together.

children.text: iṣaṃ maha ūrjam asmai duhe yo 'jaṃ pañcaudanam dakṣiṇājyotiṣaṃ dadāti ||
children.translated_text: It milks food, greatness, and vigor for him who gives the five-rice-dish goat furnished with the light of the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.

children.text: pañca rukmā pañca navāni vastrā pañcāsmai dhenavaḥ kāmadughā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Five gold ornaments, five new garments, and five cows yielding desires become his,

children.text: yo 'jaṃ pañcaudanaṃ dakṣiṇājyotiṣaṃ dadāti ||
children.translated_text: who gives the five-rice-dish goat furnished with the light of the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.

children.text: pañca rukmā jyotir asmai bhavanti varma vāsāṃsi tanve bhavanti
children.translated_text: Five gold ornaments become light for him; the garments become armor for his body.

children.text: svargaṃ lokam aśnute yo 'jaṃ pañcaudanaṃ dakṣiṇājyotiṣam dadāti ||
children.translated_text: He attains the heavenly world, who gives the five-rice-dish goat furnished with the light of the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.

children.text: yā pūrvaṃ patiṃ vittvā 'thānyaṃ vindate 'param
children.translated_text: The woman who, after having found a former husband, then finds another later one,

children.text: pañcaudanaṃ ca tāv ajaṃ dadāto na vi yoṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: if the two give the five-rice-dish goat, they are not separated.

children.text: samānaloko bhavati punarbhuvāparaḥ patiḥ
children.translated_text: The later husband becomes one of the same world with the remarried woman,

children.text: yo 'jaṃ pañcaudanam dakṣiṇājyotiṣaṃ dadāti ||
children.translated_text: who gives the five-rice-dish goat furnished with the light of the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.

children.text: anupūrvavatsāṃ dhenum anaḍvāham upabarhaṇam
children.translated_text: Having given a cow with her calf following, a draft ox, a cushion,

children.text: vāso hiraṇyaṃ dattvā te yanti divam uttamām ||
children.translated_text: a garment, and gold, they go to the highest heaven.

children.text: ātmānaṃ pitaraṃ putraṃ pautraṃ pitāmaham
children.translated_text: Myself, father, son, grandson, and grandfather,

children.text: jāyāṃ janitrīṃ mātaraṃ ye priyās tān upa hvaye ||
children.translated_text: wife, birth-mother, mother, and those who are dear: them I call near.

children.text: yo vai naidāghaṃ nāmartuṃ veda
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the season named <s>Naidāgha</s>,

children.text: eṣa vai naidāgho nāmartur yad ajaḥ pañcaudanaḥ
children.translated_text: this, namely the five-rice-dish goat, is the season named <s>Naidāgha</s>.

children.text: nir evāpriyasya bhrātṛvyasya śriyaṃ dahati bhavaty ātmanā ||
children.translated_text: He burns away the prosperity of the hostile rival and prospers in himself.

children.text: yo vai kurvantaṃ nāmartuṃ veda
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the season named <s>Kurvant</s>,

children.text: kurvatīṃ kurvatīm evāpriyasya bhrātṛvyasya śriyaṃ ā datte
children.translated_text: again and again, as it is being made, he takes to himself the prosperity of the hostile rival.

children.text: eṣa vai kurvan nāmartur yad ajaḥ pañcaudanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This, namely the five-rice-dish goat, is the season named <s>Kurvant</s>.

children.text: yo vai saṃyantaṃ nāmartuṃ veda
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the season named <s>Saṃyant</s>,

children.text: saṃyatīṃ saṃyatīm evāpriyasya bhrātṛvyasya śriyaṃ ā datte
children.translated_text: again and again, as it is being gathered, he takes to himself the prosperity of the hostile rival.

children.text: eṣa vai saṃyan nāmartur yad ajaḥ pañcaudanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This five-rice-dish goat is indeed the <s>ṛtu</s> (season) called <s>Saṃyan</s>.

children.text: yo vai pinvantaṃ nāmartum veda
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the <s>ṛtu</s> called <s>Pinvant</s>,

children.text: pinvatīṃ pinvatīm evāpriyasya bhrātṛvyasya śriyaṃ ā datte
children.translated_text: takes to himself the swelling and ever swelling prosperity of an unfriendly rival.

children.text: eṣa vai pinvan nāmartur yad ajaḥ pañcaudanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This five-rice-dish goat is indeed the <s>ṛtu</s> called <s>Pinvan</s>.

children.text: yo vā udyantaṃ nāmartuṃ veda
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the <s>ṛtu</s> called <s>Udyant</s>,

children.text: udyatīṃ udyatīm evāpriyasya bhrātṛvyasya śriyaṃ ā datte
children.translated_text: takes to himself the rising and ever rising prosperity of an unfriendly rival.

children.text: eṣa vā udyan nāmartur yad ajaḥ pañcaudanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This five-rice-dish goat is indeed the <s>ṛtu</s> called <s>Udyan</s>.

children.text: yo vā abhibhuvaṃ nāmartuṃ veda
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the <s>ṛtu</s> called <s>Abhibhū</s>,

children.text: abhibhavantīm abhibhavantīm evāpriyasya bhrātṛvyasya śriyaṃ ā datte
children.translated_text: takes to himself the overcoming and ever overcoming prosperity of an unfriendly rival.

children.text: eṣa vā abhibhūr nāmartur yad ajaḥ pañcaudanaḥ
children.translated_text: This five-rice-dish goat is indeed the <s>ṛtu</s> called <s>Abhibhū</s>.

children.text: ajaṃ ca pacata pañca caudanān
children.translated_text: Cook the goat and the five rice dishes.

children.text: sarvā diśaḥ saṃmanasaḥ sadhrīcīḥ sāntardeśāḥ prati gṛhṇantu ta etam ||
children.translated_text: May all the directions, of one mind and converging, together with the intermediate regions, receive this from you.

children.text: tās te rakṣantu tava tubhyam etaṃ tābhya ājyaṃ havir idaṃ juhomi ||
children.translated_text: May they protect this for you, belonging to you; to them I offer this oblation, this ghee.

children.text: Chapter 444
yo vidyād brahma pratyakṣaṃ parūṃṣi yasya saṃbhārā ṛco yasyānūkyam ||
children.translated_text: Whoever would know <s>brahman</s> directly, whose limbs are the requisites and whose accompanying recitation is the <s>ṛc</s>-verses,

children.text: sāmāni yasya lomāni yajur hṛdayam ucyate paristaraṇam iddhaviḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose hairs are the <s>sāman</s>-chants, whose heart is called the <s>yajus</s>, and whose enclosing-strewing is the kindled oblation.

children.text: yad vā atithipatir atithīn pratipaśyati devayajanaṃ prekṣate ||
children.translated_text: When the host looks toward the guests, he looks upon the place of divine sacrifice.

children.text: yad abhivadati dīkṣām upaiti yad udakaṃ yācaty apaḥ pra ṇayati ||
children.translated_text: When he addresses them, he enters consecration; when he asks for water, he leads forward the waters.

children.text: yā eva yajña āpaḥ praṇīyante tā eva tāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those very waters which are led forward in the sacrifice are just those.

children.text: yat tarpaṇam āharanti ya evāgnīṣomīyaḥ paśur badhyate sa eva saḥ ||
children.translated_text: When they bring refreshment, that is the <s>Agniṣomīya</s> animal that is bound.

children.text: yad āvasathān kalpayanti sadohavirdhānāny eva tat kalpayanti ||
children.translated_text: When they arrange lodgings, they arrange the <s>sadas</s> and the oblation-sheds.

children.text: yad upastṛṇanti barhir eva tat ||
children.translated_text: When they spread something underneath, that is the <s>barhis</s> grass.

children.text: yad upariśayanam āharanti svargam eva tena lokam ava runddhe ||
children.translated_text: When they bring an upper bedding, by that he secures the heavenly world.

children.text: yat kaśipūpabarhaṇam āharanti paridhaya eva te ||
children.translated_text: When they bring a cushion and a pillow, those are the enclosing-sticks.

children.text: yad āñjanābhyañjanam āharanty ājyam eva tat ||
children.translated_text: When they bring collyrium and anointing oil, that is ghee.

children.text: yat purā pariveṣāt svādam āharanti puroḍāśāv eva tau ||
children.translated_text: When, before serving, they bring something tasty, those two are the <s>puroḍāśa</s> cakes.

children.text: yad aśanakṛtaṃ hvayanti haviṣkṛtam eva taddhvayanti ||
children.translated_text: When they call the food-maker, they call the maker of the oblation.

children.text: ye vrīhayo yavā nirupyante 'ṃśava eva te ||
children.translated_text: The rice grains and barley grains that are set apart are the soma shoots.

children.text: yāny ulūkhalamusalāni grāvāṇa eva te ||
children.translated_text: The mortars and pestles are the pressing-stones.

children.text: śūrpaṃ pavitraṃ tuṣā ṛjīṣābhiṣavaṇīr āpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The winnowing basket is the purifier; the husks are the pressed residue; the waters are the pressing waters.

children.text: srug darvir nekṣaṇam āyavanaṃ droṇakalaśāḥ kumbhyo vāyavyāni pātrāṇīyam eva kṛṣṇājinam ||
children.translated_text: The ladle, the spoon, the inspection vessel, the mixing vessel, the <s>droṇa</s>-cup, the jars, the <s>Vāyavya</s> vessels, and this black antelope skin are their ritual counterparts.

children.text: yajamānabrāhmaṇaṃ vā etad atithipatiḥ kurute yad āhāryāṇi prekṣata idaṃ bhūyā3 idā3m iti ||
children.translated_text: When the host looks at the things to be brought, saying, 'May this become more; this one,' he makes this into the patron's <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: yad āha bhūya ud dhareti prāṇam eva tena varṣīyāṃsaṃ kurute ||
children.translated_text: When he says, 'Bring out more,' by that he makes the breath greater.

children.text: upa harati havīṃṣy ā sādayati ||
children.translated_text: He brings the offerings near; he sets down the oblations.

children.text: teṣām āsannānām atithir ātman juhoti ||
children.translated_text: When they have been set nearby, the guest offers them into himself.

children.text: srucā hastena prāṇe yūpe srukkāreṇa vaṣaṭkāreṇa ||
children.translated_text: With the hand as ladle, on the breath as sacrificial post, with the ladle-call and with the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-call.

children.text: ete vai priyāś cāpriyāś cartvijaḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ gamayanti yad atithayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These guests are indeed the dear and the not-dear priests; they lead one to the heavenly world.

children.text: sa ya evaṃ vidvān na dviṣann aśnīyān na dviṣato 'nnam aśnīyān na mīmāṃsitasya na mīmāṃsamānasya ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one who knows thus should not eat while hating, nor should he eat the food of one who hates, nor of one who has not been considered, nor of one who is considering.

children.text: sarvo vā eṣa jagdhapāpmā yasyānnam aśnanti ||
children.translated_text: All the evil has been eaten away from the man whose food they eat.

children.text: sarvo vā eṣo 'jagdhapāpmā yasyānnam nāśnanti ||
children.translated_text: All the evil remains uneaten in the man whose food they do not eat.

children.text: sarvadā vā eṣa yuktagrāvārdrapavitro vitatādhvara āhṛtayajñakratur ya upaharati ||
children.translated_text: The one who offers hospitality is always with pressing-stones yoked, with wet purifier, with sacrifice extended, with the sacrificial rite brought in.

children.text: prājāpatyo vā etasya yajño vitato ya upaharati ||
children.translated_text: The sacrifice of the one who offers hospitality is indeed sacred to <s>Prajāpati</s> and spread out.

children.text: prajāpater vā eṣa vikramān anuvikramate ya upaharati ||
children.translated_text: The one who offers hospitality follows after the strides of <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: yo 'tithīnāṃ sa āhavanīyo yo veśmani sa gārhapatyo yasmin pacanti sa dakṣiṇāgniḥ ||
children.translated_text: The fire among the guests is the <s>Āhavanīya</s>; the one in the house is the <s>Gārhapatya</s>; the one on which they cook is the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>.

children.text: iṣṭaṃ ca vā eṣa pūrtaṃ ca gṛhāṇām aśnāti yaḥ pūrvo 'tither aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever eats before the guest eats the <s>iṣṭa</s> and the <s>pūrta</s> of the households.

children.text: payaś ca vā eṣa rasaṃ ca gṛhāṇām aśnāti yaḥ pūrvo 'tither aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever eats before the guest eats the milk and the sap of the households.

children.text: ūrjāṃ ca vā eṣa sphātiṃ ca gṛhāṇām aśnāti yaḥ pūrvo 'tither aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever eats before the guest eats the nourishment and increase of the households.

children.text: prajāṃ vā eṣa paśūṃś ca gṛhāṇām aśnāti yaḥ pūrvo 'tither aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever eats before the guest eats the offspring and cattle of the households.

children.text: kīrtiṃ vā eṣa yaśaś ca gṛhāṇām aśnāti yaḥ pūrvo 'tither aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever eats before the guest eats the fame and glory of the households.

children.text: śriyaṃ vā eṣa saṃvidaṃ ca gṛhāṇām aśnāti yaḥ pūrvo 'tither aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever eats before the guest eats the prosperity and shared understanding of the households.

children.text: eṣa vā atithir yacchrotriyas tasmāt pūrvo nāśnīyāt ||
children.translated_text: The guest is indeed the learned <s>śrotriya</s>; therefore one should not eat before him.

children.text: aśitāvaty atithāv aśnīyād yajñasya sātmatvāya yajñasyāvichedāya tad vratam ||
children.translated_text: One should eat when the guest has eaten, for the sacrifice's having its own self and for the sacrifice's not being interrupted; that is the vow.

children.text: etad vā u svādīyo yad adhigavaṃ kṣīraṃ vā māṃsaṃ vā tad eva nāśnīyāt ||
children.translated_text: This indeed is the tastier thing, what comes from the cow, whether milk or meat; he should not eat that very thing.

children.text: sa ya evaṃ vidvān kṣīram upasicyopaharati
children.translated_text: If one, knowing thus, sprinkles milk over it and offers it,

children.text: yāvad agniṣṭomeneṣṭvā susamṛddhenāvarunddhe tāvad enenāva runddhe ||
children.translated_text: as much as he secures after sacrificing with a well-accomplished <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>, so much he secures by this.

children.text: sa ya evaṃ vidvānt sarpir upasicyopaharati
children.translated_text: If one, knowing thus, sprinkles ghee over it and offers it,

children.text: yāvad atirātreṇeṣṭvā susamṛddhenāvarunddhe tāvad enenāva runddhe ||
children.translated_text: as much as he secures after sacrificing with a well-accomplished <s>Atirātra</s>, so much he secures by this.

children.text: sa ya evaṃ vidvān madhūpasicyopaharati
children.translated_text: If one, knowing thus, sprinkles honey over it and offers it,

children.text: yāvat sattrasadyeneṣṭvā susamṛddhenāvarunddhe tāvad enenāva runddhe ||
children.translated_text: as much as he secures after sacrificing with a well-accomplished <s>sattrasadya</s>, so much he secures by this.

children.text: sa ya evaṃ vidvān māṃsam upasicyopaharati
children.translated_text: If one, knowing thus, sprinkles meat over it and offers it,

children.text: yāvad dvādaśāheneṣṭvā susamṛddhenāvarunddhe tāvad enenāva runddhe ||
children.translated_text: as much as he secures after sacrificing with a well-accomplished <s>Dvādaśāha</s>, so much he secures by this.

children.text: sa ya evaṃ vidvān udakam upasicyopaharati
children.translated_text: If one, knowing thus, sprinkles water over it and offers it,

children.text: prajānāṃ prajananāya gacchati pratiṣṭhāṃ priyaḥ prajānāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān upasicyopaharati ||
children.translated_text: He goes for the begetting of offspring; he attains firm standing and becomes dear to creatures, whoever, knowing thus, sprinkles and brings the offering.

children.text: tasmā uṣā hiṅ kṛṇoti savitā pra stauti
children.translated_text: For him <s>Uṣas</s> makes the hiṅ; <s>Savitṛ</s> performs the prastāva.

children.text: bṛhaspatir ūrjayod gāyati tvaṣṭā puṣṭyā prati harati viśve devā nidhanam
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> sings forth with strength; <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> responds with nourishment; the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> are the nidhana (finale).

children.text: nidhanaṃ bhūtyāḥ prajāyāḥ paśūnāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: There is a nidhana (resting-place) of prosperity, offspring, and cattle for the one who knows thus.

children.text: tasmā udyant sūryo hiṅ kṛṇoti saṃgavaḥ pra stauti
children.translated_text: For him the rising sun makes the hiṅ; the forenoon performs the prastāva.

children.text: madhyandina ud gāyaty aparāhṇaḥ prati haraty astaṃ yan nidhanam
children.translated_text: Midday sings forth; afternoon responds; what goes to setting is the nidhana.

children.text: nidhanaṃ bhūtyāḥ prajāyāḥ paśūnāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: There is a nidhana (resting-place) of prosperity, offspring, and cattle for the one who knows thus.

children.text: tasmā abhro bhavan hiṅ kṛṇoti stanayan pra stauti
children.translated_text: For him, becoming a cloud, it makes the hiṅ; thundering, it performs the prastāva.

children.text: vidyotamānaḥ prati harati varṣann ud gāyaty udgṛhṇan nidhanam
children.translated_text: Flashing, it responds; raining, it sings forth; drawing upward, it is the nidhana.

children.text: nidhanaṃ bhūtyāḥ prajāyāḥ paśūnāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
children.translated_text: There is a nidhana (resting-place) of prosperity, offspring, and cattle for the one who knows thus.

children.text: atithīn prati paśyati hiṅ kṛṇoty abhi vadati pra stauty udakam yācaty ud gāyati
children.translated_text: He looks toward the guests: he makes the hiṅ; he addresses them: he performs the prastāva; he asks for water: he sings forth.

children.text: upa harati prati haraty ucchiṣṭaṃ nidhanam
children.translated_text: He brings food: he responds; the leftover is the nidhana.

children.text: nidhanaṃ bhūtyāḥ prajāyāḥ paśūnāṃ bhavati ya evam veda ||
children.translated_text: There is a nidhana (resting-place) of prosperity, offspring, and cattle for the one who knows thus.

children.text: yat kṣattāraṃ hvayaty ā śrāvayaty eva tat ||
children.translated_text: When he calls the carver, that is precisely making him hear.

children.text: yat pratiśṛṇoti pratyāśrāvayaty eva tat ||
children.translated_text: When he answers, that is precisely answering back to what has been heard.

children.text: yat pariveṣṭāraḥ pātrahastāḥ pūrve cāpare ca prapadyante camasādhvaryava eva te ||
children.translated_text: When the servers, bowls in hand, both the earlier and the later, approach, they are just the cup-priests.

children.text: teṣāṃ na kaścanāhotā ||
children.translated_text: None of them is without a Hotṛ-priest.

children.text: yad vā atithipatir atithīn pariviṣya gṛhān upodaity avabhṛtham eva tad upāvaiti ||
children.translated_text: When the host, after serving the guests, comes near the houses, he comes near just the avabhṛtha (ritual bath).
