children.translated_text: Joys, delights, gladnesses, and whatever rejoicings and pleasures there are,

children.text: ucchiṣṭāj jajñire sarve divi devā diviśritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the gods abiding in heaven were born from the <s>ucchiṣṭa</s>.

children.text: devāḥ pitaro manuṣyā gandharvāpsarasaś ca ye
children.translated_text: The gods, the Fathers, human beings, and whatever Gandharvas and Apsarases there are,

children.text: ucchiṣṭāj jajñire sarve divi devā diviśritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the gods abiding in heaven were born from the <s>ucchiṣṭa</s>.

children.text: Chapter 466
yan manyur jāyām āvahat saṃkalpasya gṛhād adhi
children.translated_text: When <s>Manyu</s> took a wife from the house of <s>Saṃkalpa</s>,

children.text: ka āsaṃ janyāḥ ke varāḥ ka u jyeṣṭhavaro 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: who were the bridal companions, who were the suitors, and who was the eldest suitor?

children.text: tapaś caivāstāṃ karma cāntar mahaty arṇave
children.translated_text: Tapas and action were there within the great ocean.

children.text: ta āsaṃ janyās te varā brahma jyeṣṭhavaro 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: They were the bridal companions and the suitors; <s>Brahman</s> was the eldest suitor.

children.text: daśa sākam ajāyanta devā devebhyaḥ purā
children.translated_text: Ten gods were born together, before the gods.

children.text: yo vai tān vidyāt pratyakṣaṃ sa vā adya mahad vadet ||
children.translated_text: Whoever should know them face to face, he indeed could speak a great thing today.

children.text: prāṇāpānau cakṣuḥ śrotram akṣitiś ca kṣitiś ca yā
children.translated_text: Breath and downward breath, sight and hearing, and whatever is imperishable and perishable,

children.text: vyānodānau vāṅ manas te vā ākūtim āvahan ||
children.translated_text: diffused breath, upward breath, speech, and mind: they brought intention.

children.text: ajātā āsann ṛtavo 'tho dhātā bṛhaspatiḥ
children.translated_text: The seasons were unborn then, and so were <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: indrāgnī aśvinā tarhi kaṃ te jyeṣṭham upāsata ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, and the Aśvins then: whom did they worship as eldest?

children.text: tapaś caivāstāṃ karma cāntar mahaty arṇave
children.translated_text: Tapas and action were there within the great ocean.

children.text: tapo ha jajñe karmaṇas tat te jyeṣṭham upāsata ||
children.translated_text: Tapas indeed was born from action; that they worshiped as eldest.

children.text: yeta āsīd bhūmiḥ pūrvā yām addhātaya id viduḥ
children.translated_text: This was the former earth, which the establishers know clearly.

children.text: yo vai tāṃ vidyān nāmathā sa manyeta purāṇavit ||
children.translated_text: Whoever should know it by name would think himself a knower of ancient lore.

children.text: kuta indraḥ kutaḥ somaḥ kuto agnir ajāyata
children.translated_text: Whence was <s>Indra</s> born, whence <s>Soma</s>, whence <s>Agni</s>?

children.text: kutas tvaṣṭā samabhavat kuto dhātājāyata ||
children.translated_text: Whence did <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> come into being, whence was <s>Dhātṛ</s> born?

children.text: indrād indraḥ somāt somo agner agnir ajāyata
children.translated_text: From <s>Indra</s> <s>Indra</s> was born, from <s>Soma</s> <s>Soma</s>, from <s>Agni</s> <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: tvaṣṭā ha jajñe tvaṣṭur dhātur dhātājāyata ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> was born from <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, and <s>Dhātṛ</s> from <s>Dhātṛ</s>.

children.text: ye ta āsan daśa jātā devā devebhyaḥ purā
children.translated_text: Those ten gods who were born before the gods,

children.text: putrebhyo lokaṃ dattvā kasmiṃs te loka āsate ||
children.translated_text: after giving a world to their sons, in what world do they sit?

children.text: yadā keśān asthi snāva māṃsaṃ majjānam ābharat
children.translated_text: When he brought together hair, bone, sinew, flesh, and marrow,

children.text: śarīraṃ kṛtvā pādavat kaṃ lokam anuprāviśat ||
children.translated_text: having made the body furnished with feet, into what world did he enter?

children.text: kutaḥ keśān kutaḥ snāva kuto asthīny ābharat
children.translated_text: Whence did he bring hair, whence sinew, whence bones?

children.text: aṅgā parvāṇi majjānaṃ ko māṃsaṃ kuta ābharat ||
children.translated_text: Who brought the limbs, joints, marrow, and flesh, and whence?

children.text: saṃsico nāma te devā ye saṃbhārānt samabharan
children.translated_text: Those gods are named Saṃsicas, who gathered the component parts together.

children.text: sarvaṃ saṃsicya martyaṃ devāḥ puruṣam āviśan ||
children.translated_text: Having poured everything together into the mortal, the gods entered the person.

children.text: ūrū pādāv aṣṭhīvantau śiro hastāv atho mukham
children.translated_text: The thighs, the feet with bones, the head, the hands, and then the mouth,

children.text: pṛṣṭīr barjahye pārśve kas tat samadadhād ṛṣiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the back, ribs, and sides: what seer joined all that together?

children.text: śiro hastāv atho mukhaṃ jihvāṃ grīvāś ca kīkasāḥ
children.translated_text: The head, the hands, then the mouth, the tongue, the necks, and the vertebrae,

children.text: tvacā prāvṛtya sarvaṃ tat saṃdhā samadadhān mahī ||
children.translated_text: covering all that with skin, the great joining power put the joints together.

children.text: yat taccharīram aśayat saṃdhayā saṃhitaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: When that body lay there, great and bound together by joints,

children.text: yenedam adya rocate ko asmin varṇam ābharat ||
children.translated_text: by which this one shines today, who brought color into it?

children.text: sarve devā upāśikṣan tad ajānād vadhūḥ satī
children.translated_text: All the gods learned it; the bride, being true, knew it.

children.text: īśā vaśasya yā jāyā sāsmin varṇam ābharat ||
children.translated_text: She who is the wife, mistress of control, brought color into it.

children.text: yadā tvaṣṭā vyatṛṇat pitā tvaṣṭur ya uttaraḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> cut it apart, the father, he who is beyond <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>,

children.text: gṛhaṃ kṛtvā martyaṃ devāḥ puruṣam āviśan ||
children.translated_text: having made the mortal house, the gods entered the person.

children.text: svapno vai tandrīr nirṛtiḥ pāpmāno nāma devatāḥ
children.translated_text: Sleep, languor, <s>Nirṛti</s>, and evils are deities by name.

children.text: jarā khālatyaṃ pālityaṃ śarīram anuprāviśan ||
children.translated_text: Old age, baldness, and gray hair entered the body.

children.text: steyaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ vṛjinaṃ satyaṃ yajño yaśo bṛhat
children.translated_text: Theft, wrongdoing, crookedness, truth, sacrifice, and great fame,

children.text: balaṃ ca kṣatram ojaś ca śarīram anuprāviśan ||
children.translated_text: strength, dominion, and force entered the body.

children.text: bhūtiś ca vā abhūtiś ca rātayo 'rātayaś ca yāḥ
children.translated_text: Prosperity and non-prosperity, gifts and refusals of gifts,

children.text: kṣudhaś ca sarvās tṛṣṇāś ca śarīram anuprāviśan ||
children.translated_text: all hungers and thirsts entered the body.

children.text: nindāś ca vā anindāś ca yac ca hanteti neti ca
children.translated_text: Blames and non-blames, and whatever says, 'Strike!' and 'Do not!',

children.text: śarīraṃ śraddhā dakṣiṇāśraddhā cānuprāviśan ||
children.translated_text: faith, sacrificial gift, and lack of faith entered the body.

children.text: vidyāś ca vā avidyāś ca yac cānyad upadeśyam
children.translated_text: Knowledge and ignorance indeed, and whatever else is to be taught,

children.text: śarīraṃ brahma prāviśad ṛcaḥ sāmātho yajuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>brahman</s> entered the body: the <s>Ṛc</s>, the <s>Sāman</s>, and then the <s>Yajus</s>.

children.text: ānandā modāḥ pramudo 'bhīmodamudaś ca ye
children.translated_text: Joys, delights, great rejoicings, and whatever exultations and gladnesses there are,

children.text: haso nariṣṭā nṛttāni śarīram anuprāviśan ||
children.translated_text: laughter, good fortune, and dances entered into the body.

children.text: ālāpāś ca pralāpāś cābhīlāpalapaś ca ye
children.translated_text: Talks, babblings, and all the addresses and utterances that there are,

children.text: śarīraṃ sarve prāviśann āyujaḥ prayujo yujaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all entered the body, joined, yoked, and closely connected.

children.text: prāṇāpānau cakṣuḥ śrotram akṣitiś ca kṣitiś ca yā
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, sight and hearing, and what is undecaying and what decays,

children.text: vyānodānau vāṅ manaḥ śarīreṇa ta īyante ||
children.translated_text: <s>vyāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, speech, and mind: these are set in motion by the body.

children.text: āśiṣaś ca praśiṣaś ca saṃśiṣo viśiṣaś ca yāḥ
children.translated_text: Blessings, commands, instructions, and the various distinctions that there are,

children.text: cittāni sarve saṃkalpāḥ śarīram anuprāviśan ||
children.translated_text: all thoughts and intentions entered into the body.

children.text: āsreyīś ca vāsteyīś ca tvaraṇāḥ kṛpaṇāś ca yāḥ
children.translated_text: The resorting powers, the dwelling powers, the impulses, and the wretched powers that there are,

children.text: guhyāḥ śukrā sthūlā apas tā bībhatsāv asādayan ||
children.translated_text: the hidden, bright, and gross waters: they set down the loathsome one.

children.text: asthi kṛtvā samidhaṃ tad aṣṭāpo asādayan
children.translated_text: Having made bone the fuel-stick, those eight waters set it down;

children.text: retaḥ kṛtvājyaṃ devāḥ puruṣam āviśan ||
children.translated_text: having made seed the ghee, the gods entered the person.

children.text: yā āpo yāś ca devatā yā virāḍ brahmaṇā saha
children.translated_text: The waters that there are, the deities that there are, and <s>Virāj</s> together with <s>brahman</s>,

children.text: śarīraṃ brahma prāviśaccharīre 'dhi prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>brahman</s> entered the body, and <s>Prajāpati</s> was set over the body.

children.text: sūryaś cakṣur vātaḥ prāṇaṃ puruṣasya vibhejire
children.translated_text: The sun as the eye and the wind as the breath divided themselves for the person;

children.text: athāsyetaram ātmānaṃ devāḥ prāyacchann agnaye ||
children.translated_text: then the gods handed over his other self to <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: tasmād vai vidvān puruṣam idaṃ brahmeti manyate
children.translated_text: Therefore the knowing person regards this person as <s>brahman</s>,

children.text: sarvā hyasmin devatā gāvo goṣṭha ivāsate ||
children.translated_text: for all the deities dwell in him, like cows in a cowshed.

children.text: prathamena pramāreṇa tredhā viṣvaṅ vigacchati
children.translated_text: By the first measure he goes apart threefold in different directions;

children.text: ada ekena gacchaty ada ekena gacchatīhaikena niṣevate ||
children.translated_text: by one he goes there, by one he goes there, and with one he stays here.

children.text: apsu stīmāsu vṛddhāsu śarīram antarā hitam
children.translated_text: Within the still, swollen waters the body is placed inside;

children.text: tasmiṃ chavo 'dhy antarā tasmācchavo 'dhyucyate ||
children.translated_text: in it the corpse lies inside; therefore it is called a corpse.

children.text: Chapter 467
ye bāhavo yā iṣavo dhanvanāṃ vīryāṇi ca
children.translated_text: The arms, the arrows, and the powers of bows,

children.text: asīn paraśūn āyudhaṃ cittākūtaṃ ca yaddhṛdi
children.translated_text: the swords, axes, the weapon, and the intention that is in the heart,

children.text: sarvaṃ tad arbude tvam amitrebhyo dṛśe kurūdārāṃś ca pradarśaya ||
children.translated_text: all that, O <s>Arbuda</s>, make visible to the enemies, and display their entrails.

children.text: ut tiṣṭhata saṃ nahyadhvaṃ mitrā devajanā yūyam
children.translated_text: Rise up; gird yourselves together, you friends, you divine people.

children.text: saṃdṛṣṭā guptā vaḥ santu yā no mitrāṇy arbude ||
children.translated_text: May those allies of yours that are seen and guarded be ours, O <s>Arbuda</s>.

children.text: uttiṣṭhatam ārabhetām ādānasaṃdānābhyām
children.translated_text: Rise, you two; take hold with seizure and binding;

children.text: amitrāṇāṃ senā abhi dhattam arbude ||
children.translated_text: set yourselves against the armies of the enemies, O <s>Arbuda</s>.

children.text: arbudir nāma yo deva īśānaś ca nyarbudiḥ
children.translated_text: The god whose name is <s>Arbudi</s>, and <s>Nyarbudi</s> the lord,

children.text: yābhyām antarikṣam āvṛtam iyaṃ ca pṛthivī mahī
children.translated_text: by whom the midspace is covered, and this great earth,

children.text: tābhyām indramedibhyām ahaṃ jitam anvemi senayā ||
children.translated_text: with those two allies of <s>Indra</s> I follow what has been conquered with the army.

children.text: uttiṣṭha tvaṃ devajanārbude senayā saha
children.translated_text: Rise up, you divine being <s>Arbuda</s>, together with the army;

children.text: bhañjann amitrāṇāṃ senāṃ bhogebhiḥ parivāraya ||
children.translated_text: breaking the army of the enemies, surround it with your coils.

children.text: sapta jātān nyarbuda udārāṇāṃ samīkṣayan
children.translated_text: <s>Nyarbuda</s>, observing the seven kinds born from the entrails,

children.text: tebhiṣ ṭvam ājye hute sarvair uttiṣṭha senayā ||
children.translated_text: with all of them, when the ghee has been offered, rise up with the army.

children.text: pratighnānāśrumukhī kṛdhukarṇī ca krośatu
children.translated_text: Let the counter-striking, tear-faced one, and the smoke-eared one, cry out;

children.text: vikeśī puruṣe hate radite arbude tava ||
children.translated_text: let the disheveled one cry when a man is slain, in your roaring, O <s>Arbuda</s>.

children.text: saṃkarṣantī karūkaraṃ manasā putram icchantī
children.translated_text: Dragging along the karūkara, desiring a son in her mind,

children.text: patiṃ bhrātaram āt svān radite arbude tava ||
children.translated_text: a husband, a brother, and her own kin, let her cry in your roaring, O <s>Arbuda</s>.

children.text: aliklavā jāṣkamadā gṛdhrāḥ śyenāḥ patatriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Let aliklavas, jāṣkamadas, vultures, falcons, and winged creatures,

children.text: dhvāṅkṣāḥ śakunayas tṛpyantv amitreṣu samīkṣayan radite arbude tava ||
children.translated_text: crows and birds be sated among the enemies, looking on, in your roaring, O <s>Arbuda</s>.

children.text: atho sarvaṃ śvāpadaṃ makṣikā tṛpyatu krimiḥ
children.translated_text: And let every wild beast, the fly, and the worm be sated

children.text: pauruṣeye 'dhi kuṇape radite arbude tava ||
children.translated_text: upon the human corpse, in your roaring, O <s>Arbuda</s>.

children.text: ā gṛhṇītaṃ saṃ bṛhataṃ prāṇāpānān nyarbude
children.translated_text: Seize and expand the <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> breaths, O <s>Nyarbuda</s>;

children.text: nivāśā ghoṣāḥ saṃyantv amitreṣu samīkṣayan radite arbude tava ||
children.translated_text: let cries and shouts come together among the enemies, looking on, in your roaring, O <s>Arbuda</s>.

children.text: udvepaya saṃ vijantāṃ bhiyāmitrānt saṃsṛja
children.translated_text: Make them tremble; let the enemies shake; join them with fear;

children.text: urugrāhair bāhvaṅkair vidhyāmitrān nyarbude ||
children.translated_text: with wide grasps and arm-hooks pierce the enemies, O <s>Nyarbuda</s>.

children.text: muhyantv eṣāṃ bāhavaś cittākūtaṃ ca yaddhṛdi
children.translated_text: Let their arms be bewildered, and the intention that is in the heart;

children.text: maiṣām uccheṣi kiṃcana radite arbude tava ||
children.translated_text: let nothing at all of theirs remain, in your roaring, O <s>Arbuda</s>.

children.text: pratighnānāḥ saṃdhāvantūraḥ paṭaurāv āghnānāḥ
children.translated_text: Let the counter-striking women run together, striking their breasts with clamor,

children.text: aghāriṇīr vikeśyo rudatyaḥ puruṣe hate radite arbude tava ||
children.translated_text: the wretched, disheveled women weeping when a man is slain, in your roaring, O <s>Arbuda</s>.

children.text: śvanvatīr apsaraso rūpakā utārbude
children.translated_text: The dog-accompanied <s>Apsarases</s>, and the little forms too, O <s>Arbuda</s>,

children.text: antaḥpātre rerihatīṃ riśāṃ durṇihitaiṣiṇīm
children.translated_text: the one licking inside the bowl, the harmful one seeking what is badly hidden:

children.text: sarvās tā arbude tvam amitrebhyo dṛśe kurūdārāṃś ca pradarśaya ||
children.translated_text: all those, O <s>Arbuda</s>, make visible to the enemies, and display their entrails.

children.text: khaḍūre 'dhicaṅkramāṃ kharvikāṃ kharvavāsinīm
children.translated_text: The one that strides on the khaḍūra, the dwarf woman, the dwarf-dwelling one,

children.text: ya udārā antarhitā gandharvāpsarasaś ca ye
children.translated_text: and whatever entrails are hidden, and whatever <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s> there are,

children.text: sarpā itarajanā rakṣāṃsi ||
children.translated_text: serpents, other peoples, and <s>Rakṣases</s>,

children.text: caturdaṃṣṭrāñchyāvadataḥ kumbhamuṣkāṁ asṛṅmukhān
children.translated_text: four-tusked, gray-toothed, pot-scrotumed, blood-faced beings,

children.text: svabhyasā ye codbhyasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those with their own lairs and those with water-lairs:

children.text: udvepaya tvam arbude 'mitrāṇām amūḥ sicaḥ
children.translated_text: make those snares of the enemies tremble, O <s>Arbuda</s>;

children.text: jayaṃś ca jiṣṇuś cāmitrāṁ jayatām indramedinau ||
children.translated_text: and let the victorious, triumphant two allies of <s>Indra</s> conquer the enemies.

children.text: prablīno mṛditaḥ śayāṃ hato 'mitro nyarbude
children.translated_text: Let the enemy lie prostrate, crushed and slain, O <s>Nyarbuda</s>;

children.text: agnijihvā dhūmaśikhā jayantīr yantu senayā ||
children.translated_text: let those with fire-tongues and smoke-crests go victorious with the army.

children.text: tayārbude praṇuttānām indro hantu varaṃ varam
children.translated_text: With that army, O <s>Arbuda</s>, let <s>Indra</s> strike down the best of the best among those driven forth;

children.text: amitrāṇāṃ śacīpatir māmīṣāṃ moci kaścana ||
children.translated_text: let the lord of power strike the enemies; let not one of them be released.

children.text: utkasantu hṛdayāny ūrdhvaḥ prāṇa udīṣatu
children.translated_text: Let their hearts be dug out; let their breath go upward;

children.text: śauṣkāsyam anuvartatām amitrān mota mitriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: let dryness of mouth follow the enemies, but not the allies.

children.text: ye ca dhīrā ye cādhīrāḥ parāñco badhirāś ca ye
children.translated_text: Those who are brave and those who are not brave, those turned away and those who are deaf,

children.text: tamasā ye ca tūparā atho bastābhivāsinaḥ
children.translated_text: those who are blinded by darkness, and also those clothed in goat-skins,

children.text: sarvāṃs tāṁ arbude tvam amitrebhyo dṛśe kurūdārāṃś ca pradarśaya ||
children.translated_text: all those, O <s>Arbuda</s>, make visible to the enemies, and display their entrails.

children.text: arbudiś ca triṣandhiś cāmitrān no vi vidhyatām
children.translated_text: Let <s>Arbudi</s> and <s>Triṣandhi</s> pierce our enemies apart,

children.text: yathaiṣām indra vṛtrahan hanāma śacīpate 'mitrāṇāṃ sahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so that, O <s>Indra</s> <s>Vṛtrahan</s>, O <s>Śacīpati</s>, we may slay enemies by the thousands.

children.text: vanaspatīn vānaspatyān oṣadhīr uta vīrudhaḥ
children.translated_text: The forest trees, the products of forest trees, the healing herbs, and also the creeping plants

children.text: gandharvāpsarasaḥ sarpān devān puṇyajanān pitṝn
children.translated_text: The <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Apsarases</s>, serpents, gods, <s>Puṇyajanas</s>, and <s>Pitṛs</s>,

children.text: sarvāṃs tāṁ arbude tvam amitrebhyo dṛśe kurūdārāṃś ca pradarśaya ||
children.translated_text: all of them, O <s>Arbuda</s>, make visible to the enemies, and reveal the powerful ones.

children.text: īśāṃ vo maruto deva ādityo brahmaṇaspatiḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Maruts</s>, the god <s>Āditya</s>, and <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> are your lords.

children.text: īśāṃ va indraś cāgniś ca dhātā mitraḥ prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, <s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, and <s>Prajāpati</s> are your lords.

children.text: īśāṃ va ṛṣayaś cakrur amitreṣu samīkṣayan radite arbude tava ||
children.translated_text: The seers have established your lordship, O <s>Arbuda</s>, while looking upon the enemies.

children.text: teṣāṃ sarveṣām īśānā uttiṣṭhata saṃnahyadhvam
children.translated_text: As lords over all of them, arise; arm yourselves.

children.text: mitrā devajanā yūyam imaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ saṃjitya yathālokaṃ vitiṣṭhadhvam ||
children.translated_text: You, friendly divine peoples, having conquered this battle, take your places each in your proper world.

children.text: Chapter 468
uttiṣṭhata saṃnahyadhvam udārāḥ ketubhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Arise, arm yourselves, O exalted ones, together with your banners.

children.text: sarpā itarajanā rakṣāṃsy amitrān anudhāvata ||
children.translated_text: Serpents, other peoples, and <s>Rakṣases</s>, pursue the enemies.

children.text: īśāṃ vo veda rājyaṃ triṣandhe aruṇaiḥ ketubhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: I know your lordship and kingship, O <s>Triṣandhi</s>, together with the ruddy banners.

children.text: ye antarikṣe ye divi pṛthivyāṃ ye ca mānavāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who are in the midspace, those in heaven, those on earth, and those who are human,

children.text: triṣandhes te cetasi durṇāmāna upāsatām ||
children.translated_text: let the ill-named ones attend upon them in the thought of <s>Triṣandhi</s>.

children.text: ayomukhāḥ sūcīmukhā atho vikaṅkatīmukhāḥ
children.translated_text: Iron-mouthed, needle-mouthed, and thorn-mouthed ones,

children.text: kravyādo vātaraṃhasa ā sajantv amitrān vajreṇa triṣandhinā ||
children.translated_text: flesh-eaters, swift as wind, let them fasten upon the enemies with <s>Triṣandhi</s>'s thunderbolt.

children.text: antar dhehi jātaveda āditya kuṇapaṃ bahu
children.translated_text: Place within them, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, O <s>Āditya</s>, abundant carrion.

children.text: triṣandher iyaṃ senā suhitāstu me vaśe ||
children.translated_text: May this army of <s>Triṣandhi</s>, well set in place, be under my control.

children.text: ut tiṣṭha tvaṃ devajanārbude senayā saha
children.translated_text: Rise up, O divine-born <s>Arbuda</s>, together with your army.

children.text: ayaṃ balir va āhutas triṣandher āhutiḥ priyā ||
children.translated_text: This offering has been offered to you; it is the dear oblation of <s>Triṣandhi</s>.

children.text: śitipadī saṃdyatu śaravyeyaṃ catuṣpadī
children.translated_text: Let the white-footed, arrow-like four-footed one bind them together.

children.text: kṛtye 'mitrebhyo bhava triṣandheḥ saha senayā ||
children.translated_text: O spell, be directed against the enemies, together with the army of <s>Triṣandhi</s>.

children.text: dhūmākṣī saṃpatatu kṛdhukarṇī ca krośatu
children.translated_text: Let the smoke-eyed one fly forth; let the rough-eared one cry out.

children.text: triṣandheḥ senayā jite aruṇāḥ santu ketavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When victory has been won by the army of <s>Triṣandhi</s>, let the banners be ruddy.

children.text: avāyantāṃ pakṣiṇo ye vayāṃsy antarikṣe divi ye caranti
children.translated_text: Let the birds fly down, the winged creatures that move in the midspace and in heaven.

children.text: śvāpado makṣikāḥ saṃrabhantām āmādo gṛdhrāḥ kuṇape radantām ||
children.translated_text: Let wild beasts and flies be stirred up; let raw-flesh eaters and vultures gnaw at the carrion.

children.text: yām indreṇa saṃdhāṃ samadhatthā brahmaṇā ca bṛhaspate
children.translated_text: The alliance that you established with <s>Indra</s> and with <s>brahman</s>, O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,

children.text: tayāham indrasaṃdhayā sarvān devān iha huva ito jayata māmutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by that alliance with <s>Indra</s> I call all the gods here: win for me from here and from there.

children.text: bṛhaspatir āṅgirasa ṛṣayo brahmasaṃśitāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> the <s>Āṅgirasa</s>, and the seers sharpened by <s>brahman</s>,

children.text: asurakṣayaṇaṃ vadhaṃ triṣandhiṃ divy āśrayan ||
children.translated_text: took refuge in heaven in <s>Triṣandhi</s>, the Asura-destroying blow and slaughter.

children.text: yenāsau gupta āditya ubhāv indraś ca tiṣṭhataḥ
children.translated_text: By which that <s>Āditya</s> stands guarded, and both he and <s>Indra</s> stand firm,

children.text: triṣandhiṃ devā abhajantaujase ca balāya ca ||
children.translated_text: the gods apportioned <s>Triṣandhi</s> for vigor and for strength.

children.text: sarvāṃl lokānt samajayan devā āhutyānayā
children.translated_text: The gods conquered all the worlds by this oblation.

children.text: bṛhaspatir āṅgiraso vajraṃ yam asiñcatāsurakṣayaṇaṃ vadham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> poured out the thunderbolt, the Asura-destroying blow.

children.text: bṛhaspatir āṅgiraso vajraṃ yam asiñcatāsurakṣayaṇaṃ vadham
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> poured out the thunderbolt, the Asura-destroying blow.

children.text: tenāham amūṃ senāṃ nilimpāmi bṛhaspate 'mitrān hanmy ojasā ||
children.translated_text: With it I smear over that army, O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; with force I strike down the enemies.

children.text: sarve devā atyāyanti ye aśnanti vaṣaṭkṛtam
children.translated_text: Let all the gods advance, those who consume what is offered with the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call.

children.text: imāṃ juṣadhvam āhutim ito jayata māmutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Enjoy this oblation; win for me from here and from there.

children.text: sarve devā atyāyantu triṣandher āhutiḥ priyā
children.translated_text: Let all the gods advance; the oblation of <s>Triṣandhi</s> is dear.

children.text: saṃdhāṃ mahatīṃ rakṣata yayāgre asurā jitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Protect the great alliance by which the Asuras were conquered in the beginning.

children.text: vāyur amitrāṇām iṣvagrāṇy āñcatu
children.translated_text: Let <s>Vāyu</s> bend aside the arrow-points of the enemies.

children.text: indra eṣāṃ bāhūn pratibhanaktu mā śakan pratidhām iṣum
children.translated_text: Let <s>Indra</s> break their arms; let them not be able to set the arrow to the string.

children.text: āditya eṣām astraṃ vināśayatu candramā yutām agatasya panthām ||
children.translated_text: Let <s>Āditya</s> destroy their weapon; let the moon divert the path of what has not yet come.

children.text: yadi preyur devapurā brahma varmāṇi cakrire
children.translated_text: If they have gone forth to the gods' strongholds and have made armors of <s>brahman</s>,

children.text: tanūpānaṃ paripāṇaṃ kṛṇvānā yad upocire sarvaṃ tad arasaṃ kṛdhi ||
children.translated_text: whatever body-guarding and surrounding protection they have uttered, make all of that sapless.

children.text: kravyādānuvartayan mṛtyunā ca purohitam
children.translated_text: Setting flesh-eaters in pursuit, with Death as the priest in front,

children.text: triṣandhe prehi senayā jayāmitrān prapadyasva ||
children.translated_text: go forth, O <s>Triṣandhi</s>, with your army; conquer the enemies and fall upon them.

children.text: triṣandhe tamasā tvam amitrān parivāraya
children.translated_text: O <s>Triṣandhi</s>, surround the enemies with darkness.

children.text: pṛṣadājyapraṇuttānāṃ māmīṣāṃ moci kaścana ||
children.translated_text: Let none of these, driven on by speckled ghee, be released.

children.text: śitipadī saṃpatatv amitrāṇām amūḥ sicaḥ
children.translated_text: Let the white-footed one fly upon those snares of the enemies.

children.text: muhyantv adyāmūḥ senā amitrāṇāṃ nyarbude ||
children.translated_text: Let those armies of the enemies be bewildered today, O <s>Nyarbuda</s>.

children.text: mūḍhā amitrā nyarbude jahy eṣāṃ varaṃ varam
children.translated_text: The enemies are bewildered, O <s>Nyarbuda</s>; strike down their best man, each one.

children.text: anayā jahi senayā ||
children.translated_text: Strike them down with this army.

children.text: yaś ca kavacī yaś cākavaco 'mitro yaś cājmani
children.translated_text: May the enemy who has armor, the one without armor, and the one on the battlefield,

children.text: jyāpāśaiḥ kavacapāśair ajmanābhihataḥ śayām ||
children.translated_text: lie struck down on the battlefield by bowstring snares and armor snares.

children.text: ye varmiṇo ye 'varmāṇo amitrā ye ca varmiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Those enemies who are armored, those unarmored, and those who wear armor,

children.text: sarvāṃs tāṁ arbude hatāṁ chvāno 'dantu bhūmyām ||
children.translated_text: all those slain, O <s>Arbuda</s>, let dogs eat on the ground.

children.text: ye rathino ye arathā asādā ye ca sādinaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who have chariots, those without chariots, those not mounted, and those mounted,

children.text: sarvān adantu tān hatān gṛdhrāḥ śyenāḥ patatriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: let vultures, hawks, and winged birds eat all those slain.

children.text: sahasrakuṇapā śetām āmitrī senā samare vadhānām
children.translated_text: Let the enemy army lie in battle as a thousand corpses among the slain,

children.text: vividdhā kakajākṛtā ||
children.translated_text: pierced through, made into food for crows.

children.text: marmāvidhaṃ roruvataṃ suparṇair adantu duścitaṃ mṛditaṃ śayānam
children.translated_text: Let the birds eat the one struck in the vitals, howling, evil-minded, crushed, lying there,

children.text: ya imāṃ pratīcīm āhutim amitro no yuyutsati ||
children.translated_text: the enemy of ours who wishes to fight against this oblation facing him.

children.text: yāṃ devā anutiṣṭhanti yasyā nāsti virādhanam
children.translated_text: That which the gods attend upon, for which there is no failure,

children.text: tayendro hantu vṛtrahā vajreṇa triṣandhinā ||
children.translated_text: with that let <s>Indra</s>, slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, strike with the thunderbolt of <s>Triṣandhi</s>.

children.text: Chapter 469
satyaṃ bṛhad ṛtam ugraṃ dīkṣā tapo brahma yajñaḥ pṛthivīṃ dhārayanti
children.translated_text: Truth, the great, the cosmic order, fierce consecration, tapas, <s>brahman</s>, and sacrifice uphold the earth.

children.text: sā no bhūtasya bhavyasya patny uruṃ lokaṃ pṛthivī naḥ kṛṇotu ||
children.translated_text: May she, mistress of what has been and what will be, the earth, make a broad world for us.

children.text: asaṃbādhaṃ madhyato mānavānāṃ yasyā udvataḥ pravataḥ samaṃ bahu
children.translated_text: Unconstricted in the middle among human beings, whose heights, slopes, and level places are many,

children.text: nānāvīryā oṣadhīr yā bibharti pṛthivī naḥ prathatāṃ rādhyatāṃ naḥ ||
children.translated_text: who bears plants of many powers: may the earth spread wide for us and prosper for us.

children.text: yasyāṃ samudra uta sindhur āpo yasyām annaṃ kṛṣṭayaḥ saṃbabhūvuḥ
children.translated_text: In whom are the ocean, the river, and the waters, in whom food and peoples have come into being,

children.text: yasyām idaṃ jinvati prāṇad ejat sā no bhūmiḥ pūrvapeye dadhātu ||
children.translated_text: in whom this breathing and moving life quickens: may that earth establish us at the first drinking.

children.text: yasyāś catasraḥ pradiśaḥ pṛthivyā yasyām annam kṛṣṭayaḥ saṃbabhūvuḥ
children.translated_text: Whose four quarters are the directions of the earth, in whom food and peoples have come into being.

children.text: yā bibharti bahudhā prāṇad ejat sā no bhūmir goṣv apy anne dadhātu ||
children.translated_text: She who bears breathing, moving life in many forms: may that Earth place us among cattle and in food.

children.text: yasyāṃ pūrve pūrvajanā vicakrire yasyāṃ devā asurān abhyavartayan
children.translated_text: On whom the former forefathers performed their deeds, on whom the gods overcame the <s>Asuras</s>,

children.text: gavām aśvānāṃ vayasaś ca viṣṭhā bhagaṃ varcaḥ pṛthivī no dadhātu ||
children.translated_text: the abode of cows, horses, and birds: may Earth bestow fortune and splendor on us.

children.text: viśvaṃbharā vasudhānī pratiṣṭhā hiraṇyavakṣā jagato niveśanī
children.translated_text: All-bearing, treasure-holding, foundation, golden-breasted, dwelling-place of the world,

children.text: vaiśvānaraṃ bibhratī bhūmir agnim indraṛṣabhā draviṇe no dadhātu ||
children.translated_text: Earth, bearing <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>, with <s>Indra</s> as her bull, may she place us in wealth.

children.text: yāṃ rakṣanty asvapnā viśvadānīṃ devā bhūmiṃ pṛthivīm apramādam
children.translated_text: The sleepless gods guard unerring Earth, all-giving,

children.text: sā no madhu priyaṃ duhām atho ukṣatu varcasā ||
children.translated_text: may that Earth milk for us sweet beloved honey, and may she also sprinkle us with splendor.

children.text: yārṇave 'dhi salilam agra āsīt yāṃ māyābhir anvacaran manīṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: She who at first was upon the ocean, upon the water, whom the wise followed with their powers of <s>māyā</s> (creative power),

children.text: yasyā hṛdayaṃ parame vyomant satyenāvṛtam amṛtaṃ pṛthivyāḥ
children.translated_text: whose heart, the immortal heart of Earth, is in the highest heaven, covered with truth,

children.text: sā no bhūmis tviṣiṃ balaṃ rāṣṭre dadhātūttame ||
children.translated_text: may that Earth place brilliance and strength in our highest kingdom.

children.text: yasyām āpaḥ paricarāḥ samānīr ahorātre apramādaṃ kṣaranti
children.translated_text: On whom the waters, common wanderers, flow day and night without negligence,

children.text: sā no bhūmir bhūridhārā payo duhām atho ukṣatu varcasā ||
children.translated_text: may that Earth, rich in streams, milk milk for us, and may she also sprinkle us with splendor.

children.text: yām aśvināv amimātāṃ viṣṇur yasyāṃ vicakrame
children.translated_text: Earth whom the <s>Aśvins</s> measured out, on whom <s>Viṣṇu</s> strode,

children.text: indro yāṃ cakra ātmane 'namitrāṃ śacīpatiḥ
children.translated_text: whom <s>Indra</s>, lord of power, made free from enemies for himself,

children.text: sā no bhūmir visṛjatāṃ mātā putrāya me payaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may that Earth, the mother, release milk for me, her son.

children.text: girayas te parvatā himavanto 'raṇyaṃ te pṛthivi syonam astu
children.translated_text: Your hills, your mountains, your snowy heights, and your forest, O Earth, may they be kindly.

children.text: babhruṃ kṛṣṇāṃ rohiṇīṃ viśvarūpāṃ dhruvāṃ bhūmiṃ pṛthivīm indraguptām
children.translated_text: Brown, black, red, many-formed, firm Earth, protected by <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: ajīto 'hato akṣato 'dhyaṣṭhām pṛthivīm aham ||
children.translated_text: unconquered, unstruck, unwounded: I have taken my stand upon Earth.

children.text: yat te madhyaṃ pṛthivi yac ca nabhyaṃ yās ta ūrjas tanvaḥ saṃbabhūvuḥ
children.translated_text: What is your middle, O Earth, and what is your navel, and what strengthening bodies of yours have come together,

children.text: tāsu no dhehy abhi naḥ pavasva mātā bhūmiḥ putro ahaṃ pṛthivyāḥ parjanyaḥ pitā sa u naḥ pipartu ||
children.translated_text: place us within those; purify yourself toward us. Earth is mother, I am the son of Earth; <s>Parjanya</s> is father, may he nourish us.

children.text: yasyāṃ vediṃ parigṛhṇanti bhūmyāṃ yasyāṃ yajñaṃ tanvate viśvakarmāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: On which earth they enclose the altar, on which the all-working ones extend the sacrifice,

children.text: yasyāṃ mīyante svaravaḥ pṛthivyām ūrdhvāḥ śukrā āhutyāḥ purastāt
children.translated_text: on which the sacrificial posts are measured out on earth, upright and bright, before the oblations,

children.text: sā no bhūmir vardhayad vardhamānā ||
children.translated_text: may that Earth, growing, make us grow.

children.text: yo no dveṣat pṛthivi yaḥ pṛtanyād yo 'bhidāsān manasā yo vadhena
children.translated_text: Whoever hates us, O Earth, whoever fights us, whoever attacks us with mind or with weapon,

children.text: taṃ no bhūme randhaya pūrvakṛtvari ||
children.translated_text: him, O Earth, make subject to us, you who act from of old.

children.text: tvaj jātās tvayi caranti martyās tvaṃ bibharṣi dvipadas tvaṃ catuṣpadaḥ
children.translated_text: Born from you, mortals move upon you; you bear the two-footed, you bear the four-footed.

children.text: taveme pṛthivi pañca mānavā yebhyo jyotir amṛtaṃ martyebhya udyant sūryo raśmibhir ātanoti ||
children.translated_text: Yours are these five races of men, O Earth, for whom the rising sun spreads out immortal light with his rays, for mortals.

children.text: tā naḥ prajāḥ saṃ duhratāṃ samagrā vāco madhu pṛthivi dhehi mahyam ||
children.translated_text: May those peoples milk together for us, united; O Earth, place the honey of speech in me.

children.text: viśvasvaṃ mātaram oṣadhīnāṃ dhruvāṃ bhūmiṃ pṛthivīṃ dharmaṇā dhṛtām
children.translated_text: Universal mother of the plants, the firm Earth, held by <s>dharma</s> (cosmic order),

children.text: śivāṃ syonām anu carema viśvahā ||
children.translated_text: may we walk upon her every day, auspicious and kindly.

children.text: mahat sadhasthaṃ mahatī babhūvitha mahān vega ejathur vepathuṣ ṭe
children.translated_text: You have become a great seat, a great one; great is your surge, your trembling and your shaking.

children.text: mahāṃs tvendro rakṣaty apramādam
children.translated_text: Great <s>Indra</s> guards you without negligence.

children.text: sā no bhūme prarocaya hiraṇyasyeva saṃdṛśi mā no dvikṣata kaścana ||
children.translated_text: O Earth, make us shine forth, as in the sight of gold; let no one hate us.

children.text: agnir bhūmyām oṣadhīṣv agnim āpo bibhraty agnir aśmasu
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> is in earth and in plants; the waters bear <s>Agni</s>; <s>Agni</s> is in stones.

children.text: agnir antaḥ puruṣeṣu goṣv aśveṣv agnayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> is within human beings; among cows and horses there are fires.

children.text: agnir diva ātapaty agner devasyorv antarikṣam
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> shines from heaven; the broad midspace belongs to <s>Agni</s> the god.

children.text: agniṃ martāsa indhate havyavāhaṃ ghṛtapriyam ||
children.translated_text: Mortals kindle <s>Agni</s>, the oblation-carrier, lover of ghee.

children.text: agnivāsāḥ pṛthivy asitajñūs tviṣīmantaṃ saṃśitaṃ mā kṛṇotu ||
children.translated_text: May Earth, clothed in <s>Agni</s>, dark-kneed, make me brilliant, sharp, and well-honed.

children.text: bhūmyāṃ devebhyo dadati yajñaṃ havyam araṃkṛtam
children.translated_text: On earth they give to the gods the sacrifice, the prepared oblation.

children.text: bhūmyāṃ manuṣyā jīvanti svadhayānnena martyāḥ
children.translated_text: On earth human beings live, mortals, by sustenance and food.

children.text: sā no bhūmiḥ prāṇam āyur dadhātu jaradaṣṭiṃ mā pṛthivī kṛṇotu ||
children.translated_text: May that Earth place breath and life-span in us; may Earth make me one who reaches old age.

children.text: yas te gandhaḥ pṛthivi saṃbabhūva yaṃ bibhraty oṣadhayo yam āpaḥ
children.translated_text: The fragrance of yours, O Earth, that has arisen, which the plants bear, which the waters bear,

children.text: yaṃ gandharvā apsarasaś ca bhejire tena mā surabhiṃ kṛṇu mā no dvikṣata kaścana ||
children.translated_text: which the <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s> have shared: with that make me fragrant; let no one hate us.

children.text: yas te gandhaḥ puṣkaram āviveśa yaṃ saṃjabhruḥ sūryāyā vivāhe
children.translated_text: The fragrance of yours that entered the lotus, which the immortals gathered at the wedding of <s>Sūryā</s>,

children.text: amartyāḥ pṛthivi gandham agre tena mā surabhiṃ kṛṇu mā no dvikṣata kaścana ||
children.translated_text: that first fragrance, O Earth: with that make me fragrant; let no one hate us.

children.text: yas te gandhaḥ puruṣeṣu strīṣu puṃsu bhago ruciḥ
children.translated_text: The fragrance of yours among men and women, among males, fortune and delight,

children.text: yo aśveṣu vīreṣu yo mṛgeṣūta hastiṣu
children.translated_text: which is in horses and heroes, which is in wild animals and also in elephants,

children.text: kanyāyāṃ varco yad bhūme tenāsmāṁ api saṃsṛja mā no dvikṣata kaścana ||
children.translated_text: the splendor that is in a maiden, O Earth: with that also mingle us; let no one hate us.

children.text: śilā bhūmir aśmā pāṃsuḥ sā bhūmiḥ saṃdhṛtā dhṛtā
children.translated_text: Rock is earth, stone is earth, dust is that earth, held together and upheld.

children.text: tasyai hiraṇyavakṣase pṛthivyā akaraṃ namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: To her, to golden-breasted Earth, I have made reverence.

children.text: yasyāṃ vṛkṣā vānaspatyā dhruvās tiṣṭhanti viśvahā
children.translated_text: On whom trees, the lords of the forest, stand firm every day,

children.text: pṛthivīṃ viśvadhāyasaṃ dhṛtām acchāvadāmasi ||
children.translated_text: we speak toward Earth, the all-nourishing, upheld one.

children.text: udīrāṇā utāsīnās tiṣṭhantaḥ prakrāmantaḥ
children.translated_text: Rising up, and sitting down, standing, and stepping forward,

children.text: padbhyāṃ dakṣiṇasavyābhyāṃ mā vyathiṣmahi bhūmyām ||
children.translated_text: with right and left feet, may we not stumble upon earth.

children.text: vimṛgvarīṃ pṛthivīm āvadāmi kṣamāṃ bhūmiṃ brahmaṇā vāvṛdhānām
children.translated_text: I speak to discerning Earth, patient Earth, increased by <s>brahman</s> (sacred utterance),

children.text: ūrjaṃ puṣṭaṃ bibhratīm annabhāgaṃ ghṛtaṃ tvābhiniṣīdema bhūme ||
children.translated_text: bearing vigor, nourishment, and a share of food; with ghee may we sit down upon you, O Earth.

children.text: śuddhā na āpas tanve kṣarantu yo naḥ syedur apriye taṃ nidadhmaḥ
children.translated_text: May pure waters flow for our body; whoever would be hateful to us, him we set down in an unpleasant place.

children.text: pavitreṇa pṛthivi motpunāmi ||
children.translated_text: With a purifier, O Earth, I purify myself upon you.

children.text: yās te prācīḥ pradiśo yā udīcīr yās te bhūme adharād yāś ca paścāt
children.translated_text: Your eastern regions, your northern ones, O Earth, your lower regions and your western ones,

children.text: syonās tā mahyaṃ carate bhavantu mā nipaptaṃ bhuvane śiśriyāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may they be kindly for me as I move; may I not fall down while dwelling in the world.

children.text: mā naḥ paścān mā purastān nudiṣṭhā mottarād adharād uta
children.translated_text: Do not thrust us from behind, nor from the front, nor from the north or from below, and...

children.text: svasti bhūme no bhava mā vidan paripanthino varīyo yāvayā vadham ||
children.translated_text: O Earth, be gracious to us; may waylayers not find us. Drive deadly harm far away.

children.text: yāvat te 'bhi vipaśyāmi bhūme sūryeṇa medinā
children.translated_text: As long as I look out over you, O Earth, by means of the sun's light,

children.text: tāvan me cakṣur mā meṣṭottarāmuttarāṃ samām ||
children.translated_text: so long may my sight not fail me, through each succeeding year.

children.text: yac chayānaḥ paryāvarte dakṣiṇaṃ savyam abhi bhūme pārśvam uttānās tvā pratīcīṃ yat pṛṣṭībhir adhiśemahe
children.translated_text: When, lying down, I turn to the right side or the left, O Earth, and when, lying on our backs, we rest upon you with our ribs,

children.text: mā hiṃsīs tatra no bhūme sarvasya pratiśīvari ||
children.translated_text: do not injure us there, O Earth, you on whom everything lies down.

children.text: yat te bhūme vikhanāmi kṣipraṃ tad apirohatu
children.translated_text: Whatever of you I dig up, O Earth, let that quickly grow over again.

children.text: mā te marma vimṛgvari mā te hṛdayam arpipam ||
children.translated_text: Do not let me strike your vital place, O searching one; do not let me pierce your heart.

children.text: grīṣmas te bhūme varṣāṇi śaraddhemantaḥ śiśiro vasantaḥ
children.translated_text: Summer, O Earth, the rains, autumn, winter, the cool season, and spring are yours;

children.text: ṛtavas te vihitā hāyanīr ahorātre pṛthivi no duhātām ||
children.translated_text: your appointed seasons and your years, day and night, O Earth, may they milk abundance for us.

children.text: yāpa sarpaṃ vijamānā vimṛgvarī yasyām āsann agnayo ye apsv antaḥ
children.translated_text: She who drives away the serpent, shaking it off, searching it out, on whom were the fires that are within the waters,

children.text: parā dasyūn dadatī devapīyūn indraṃ vṛṇānā pṛthivī na vṛtram śakrāya dadhre vṛṣabhāya vṛṣṇe ||
children.translated_text: she who gives hostile god-haters far away, choosing <s>Indra</s>, who like no <s>Vṛtra</s> was established for mighty <s>Śakra</s>, the virile bull.

children.text: yasyāṃ sadohavirdhāne yūpo yasyāṃ nimīyate
children.translated_text: On her the sacrificial seat, the havirdhāna shed, and the post are set up;

children.text: brahmāṇo yasyām arcanty ṛgbhiḥ sāmnā yajurvidaḥ yujyante yasyām ṛtvijaḥ somam indrāya pātave ||
children.translated_text: on her the brahmans, knowers of the <s>Ṛc</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Yajus</s>, worship; on her the priests are yoked to press <s>Soma</s> for <s>Indra</s> to drink.

children.text: yasyāṃ pūrve bhūtakṛta ṛṣayo gā udānṛcchuḥ
children.translated_text: On her the former seers, makers of beings, chanted forth the cows;

children.text: sapta satreṇa vedhaso yajñena tapasā saha ||
children.translated_text: the seven inspired ones did so by their sattra session, together with sacrifice and austerity.

children.text: sā no bhūmir ādiśatu yad dhanaṃ kāmayāmahe
children.translated_text: May that Earth assign to us the wealth that we desire;

children.text: bhago anuprayuṅktām indra etu purogavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Bhaga</s> set it in motion for us; may <s>Indra</s> come as our leader in front.

children.text: yasyāṃ gāyanti nṛtyanti bhūmyāṃ martyā vyailabāḥ
children.translated_text: On Earth, where mortals sing and dance in many ways,

children.text: yudhyante yasyām ākrando yasyām vadati dundubhiḥ
children.translated_text: where they fight, where battle-cry is raised, where the war-drum speaks,

children.text: sā no bhūmiḥ praṇudatāṃ sapatnān asapatnaṃ mā pṛthivī kṛṇotu ||
children.translated_text: may that Earth drive away our rivals; may Earth make me without a rival.

children.text: yasyām annaṃ vrīhiyavau yasyā imāḥ pañca kṛṣṭayaḥ
children.translated_text: On her are food, rice and barley; on her are these five peoples.

children.text: bhūmyai parjanyapatnyai namo 'stu varṣamedase ||
children.translated_text: Homage be to Earth, wife of <s>Parjanya</s>, whose wisdom is rain.

children.text: yasyāḥ puro devakṛtāḥ kṣetre yasyā vikurvate
children.translated_text: Whose cities are fashioned by the gods, whose fields are worked in many ways,

children.text: prajāpatiḥ pṛthivīṃ viśvagarbhām āśāmāśāṃ raṇyāṃ naḥ kṛṇotu ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Prajāpati</s> make Earth, womb of all, delightful for us in every quarter.

children.text: nidhiṃ bibhratī bahudhā guhā vasu maṇiṃ hiraṇyaṃ pṛthivī dadātu me
children.translated_text: Bearing treasure in many hidden places, wealth, jewel, and gold, may Earth give them to me.

children.text: vasūni no vasudā rāsamānā devī dadhātu sumanasyamānā ||
children.translated_text: May the goddess, wealth-giving and kindly disposed, bestowing riches upon us, establish good-mindedness.

children.text: janaṃ bibhratī bahudhā vivācasaṃ nānādharmāṇaṃ pṛthivī yathaukasam
children.translated_text: Earth bears people of many kinds, speaking various tongues, with diverse customs, each according to its dwelling-place.

children.text: sahasraṃ dhārā draviṇasya me duhāṃ dhruveva dhenur anapasphurantī ||
children.translated_text: May she milk for me a thousand streams of wealth, like an unfailing, steady cow.

children.text: yas te sarpo vṛścikas tṛṣṭadaṃśmā hemantajabdho bhṛmalo guhā śaye
children.translated_text: Whatever serpent of yours, whatever scorpion, sharp-biting creature, winter-torpid worm, or burrowing beast lies hidden,

children.text: krimir jinvat pṛthivi yadyad ejati prāvṛṣi tan naḥ sarpan mopasṛpad yac chivaṃ tena no mṛḍa ||
children.translated_text: whatever crawling thing, O Earth, whatever moves in the rains, let that not creep upon us; with what is auspicious, be gracious to us.

children.text: ye te panthāno bahavo janāyanā rathasya vartmānasaś ca yātave
children.translated_text: Those many paths of yours, travelled by people, and the tracks for the chariot's course,

children.text: yaiḥ saṃcaranty ubhaye bhadrapāpās taṃ panthānaṃ jayemānamitram ataskaraṃ yac chivaṃ tena no mṛḍa ||
children.translated_text: on which both the good and the bad move about, may we master that path, free from enemies and thieves; with what is auspicious, be gracious to us.

children.text: malvaṃ bibhratī gurubhṛd bhadrapāpasya nidhanaṃ titikṣuḥ
children.translated_text: Bearing the lowly and bearing the heavy, enduring the destruction of good and evil,

children.text: varāheṇa pṛthivī saṃvidānā sūkarāya vijihīte mṛgāya ||
children.translated_text: Earth, in accord with the boar, opens herself for the boar, the wild beast.

children.text: ye ta āraṇyāḥ paśavo mṛgā vane hitāḥ siṃhā vyāghrāḥ puruṣādaś caranti
children.translated_text: Those forest animals of yours, beasts set in the forest, lions, tigers, and man-eaters that roam,

children.text: ulaṃ vṛkaṃ pṛthivi ducchunām ita ṛkṣīkāṃ rakṣo apabādhayāsmat ||
children.translated_text: the wolf, the fierce creature, O Earth, the ill-omened one, the female bear, and the demon: drive them away from us.

children.text: ye gandharvā apsaraso ye cārāyāḥ kimīdinaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Gandharvas</s>, the <s>Apsarases</s>, and the wandering kimīdin demons,

children.text: piśācānt sarvā rakṣāṃsi tān asmad bhūme yāvaya ||
children.translated_text: the piśācas and all rākṣasas: drive them away from us, O Earth.

children.text: yāṃ dvipādaḥ pakṣiṇaḥ saṃpatanti haṃsāḥ suparṇāḥ śakunā vayāṃsi
children.translated_text: Onto whom the two-footed flying creatures alight, swans, eagles, birds, and winged things,

children.text: yasyāṃ vāto mātariśveyate rajāṃsi kṛṇvaṃś cyāvayaṃś ca vṛkṣān
children.translated_text: on whom the wind, <s>Mātariśvan</s>, blows, making dust and shaking trees,

children.text: vātasya pravām upavām anuvāty arciḥ ||
children.translated_text: the flame follows the wind's forward and backward blowing.

children.text: yasyāṃ kṛṣṇam aruṇaṃ ca saṃhite ahorātre vihite bhūmyām adhi
children.translated_text: On Earth, where black and red, day and night, are joined and appointed,

children.text: varṣeṇa bhūmiḥ pṛthivī vṛtāvṛtā sā no dadhātu bhadrayā priye dhāmani dhāmani ||
children.translated_text: Earth is wrapped and wrapped again by rain; may she place us in an auspicious, beloved station, in every station.

children.text: dyauś ca ma idaṃ pṛthivī cāntarikṣaṃ ca me vyacaḥ
children.translated_text: Heaven, Earth, and the midspace have given me this expanse;

children.text: agniḥ sūrya āpo medhāṃ viśve devāś ca saṃdaduḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, the Sun, the waters, wisdom, and all the gods have bestowed it together.

children.text: aham asmi sahamāna uttaro nāma bhūmyām
children.translated_text: I am the enduring one, named the higher one upon Earth;

children.text: abhīṣāḍ asmi viśvāṣāḍ āśāmāśāṃ viṣāsahiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am overcoming, all-overcoming, conquering every quarter.

children.text: ado yad devi prathamānā purastād devair uktā vyasarpo mahitvam
children.translated_text: When, O goddess, first at the beginning, proclaimed by the gods, you spread forth your greatness,

children.text: ā tvā subhūtam aviśat tadānīm akalpayathāḥ pradiśaś catasraḥ ||
children.translated_text: then good being entered into you, and you set in order the four directions.

children.text: ye grāmā yad araṇyaṃ yāḥ sabhā adhi bhūmyām
children.translated_text: The villages, the forest, and the assemblies that are upon Earth,

children.text: ye saṃgrāmāḥ samitayas teṣu cāru vadema te ||
children.translated_text: the battles and gatherings: in them may we speak what is pleasing to you.

children.text: aśva iva rajo dudhuve vi tān janān ya ākṣiyan pṛthivīṃ yād ajāyata
children.translated_text: Like a horse she shook off dust from those people who dwelt upon Earth when she was born,

children.text: mandrāgretvarī bhuvanasya gopā vanaspatīnāṃ gṛbhir oṣadhīnām ||
children.translated_text: she who goes foremost with a pleasant sound, guardian of the world, amid the houses of trees and plants.

children.text: yad vadāmi madhumat tad vadāmi yad īkṣe tad vananti mā
children.translated_text: What I speak, may I speak honey-sweet; what I look upon, may they love me for it.

children.text: tviṣīmān asmi jūtimān avānyān hanmi dodhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am full of brilliance, full of impulse; I strike down others who hate us.

children.text: śantivā surabhiḥ syonā kīlālodhnī payasvatī
children.translated_text: Peaceful, fragrant, kindly, rich in pools, rich in milk,

children.text: bhūmir adhibravītu me pṛthivī payasā saha ||
children.translated_text: may Earth, together with milk, speak favorably for me.

children.text: yām anvaicchaddhaviṣā viśvakarmāntar arṇave rajasi praviṣṭām
children.translated_text: She whom <s>Viśvakarman</s> sought with oblation, entering the billowy oceanic realm,

children.text: bhujiṣyaṃ pātraṃ nihitaṃ guhā yad āvir bhoge abhavan mātṛmadbhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the free vessel set in secret, which became manifest for enjoyment to the mothers.

children.text: tvam asy āvapanī janānām aditiḥ kāmadughā paprathānā
children.translated_text: You are the pouring-place of people, <s>Aditi</s>, wish-milking, spreading wide.

children.text: yat ta ūnaṃ tat ta āpūrayāti prajāpatiḥ prathamajā ṛtasya ||
children.translated_text: Whatever of you is deficient, may <s>Prajāpati</s>, firstborn of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order), fill that up for you.

children.text: upasthās te anamīvā ayakṣmā asmabhyaṃ santu pṛthivi prasūtāḥ
children.translated_text: May your resting-places, born from you, O <s>Pṛthivī</s>, be free from sickness and free from <s>yakṣma</s> (wasting disease) for us.

children.text: dīrghaṃ na āyuḥ pratibudhyamānā vayaṃ tubhyaṃ balihṛtaḥ syāma ||
children.translated_text: As we awaken, may our life be long; may we be bearers of tribute to you.

children.text: bhūme mātar nidhehi mā bhadrayā supratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhūmi</s>, mother, set me down firmly in what is auspicious.

children.text: saṃvidānā divā kave śriyāṃ mā dhehi bhūtyām ||
children.translated_text: In concord with Heaven, O sage, place me in splendor and prosperity.

children.text: Chapter 470
naḍam āroha na te atra loka idaṃ sīsaṃ bhāgadheyaṃ ta ehi
children.translated_text: Mount the reed; there is no place for you here. This lead is your allotted share; come to it.

children.text: yo goṣu yakṣmaḥ puruṣeṣu yakṣmas tena tvaṃ sākam adharāṅ parehi ||
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>yakṣma</s> is in cattle and whatever <s>yakṣma</s> is in men, go away downward together with that.

children.text: aghaśaṃsaduḥśaṃsābhyāṃ kareṇānukareṇa ca
children.translated_text: By evil-speaking and ill-speaking, by the deed and the copied deed,

children.text: yakṣmaṃ ca sarvaṃ teneto mṛtyuṃ ca nirajāmasi ||
children.translated_text: by that we drive out from here all <s>yakṣma</s> and death as well.

children.text: nir ito mṛtyuṃ nirṛtiṃ nir arātim ajāmasi
children.translated_text: We drive out death from here, drive out destruction, drive out hostility.

children.text: yo no dveṣṭi tam addhy agne akravyād yam u dviṣmas tam u te prasuvāmasi ||
children.translated_text: The one who hates us, consume him, O <s>Agni Akravyād</s>; and the one whom we hate, him we deliver over to you.

children.text: yady agniḥ kravyād yadi vā vyāghra imaṃ goṣṭhaṃ praviveśānyokāḥ
children.translated_text: If a flesh-eating fire, or if a tiger from another dwelling, has entered this cattle-stall,

children.text: taṃ māṣājyaṃ kṛtvā prahiṇomi dūraṃ sa gacchatv apsuṣado 'py agnīn ||
children.translated_text: having made a bean-and-ghee offering for him, I send him far away; let him go to the fires that sit in the waters.

children.text: yat tvā kruddhāḥ pracakrur manyunā puruṣe mṛte
children.translated_text: What angry men, in their wrath, made of you when a man was dead,

children.text: sukalpam agne tat tvayā punas tvoddīpayāmasi ||
children.translated_text: may that be well ordered by you, O <s>Agni</s>; we kindle you up again.

children.text: punas tvādityā rudrā vasavaḥ punar brahmā vasunītir agne
children.translated_text: Again the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, and the <s>Vasus</s>, again <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Vasunīti</s>, O <s>Agni</s>,

children.text: punas tvā brahmaṇaspatir ādhād dīrghāyutvāya śataśāradāya ||
children.translated_text: again <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> has set you in place for long life, for a hundred autumns.

children.text: yo agniḥ kravyāt praviveśa no gṛham imaṃ paśyann itaraṃ jātavedasam
children.translated_text: The <s>Agni</s> who is a <s>kravyād</s> (flesh-eater) has entered our house, looking upon this other <s>Jātavedas</s>.

children.text: taṃ harāmi pitṛyajñāya dūraṃ sa gharmam indhāṃ parame sadhasthe ||
children.translated_text: I carry him far away for the ancestor-sacrifice; let him kindle the hot oblation in the highest seat.

children.text: kravyādam agniṃ prahiṇomi dūram yamarājño gacchatu ripravāhaḥ
children.translated_text: I send the <s>kravyād</s> fire far away; let the bearer of defilement go to the kingdom of <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: ihāyam itaro jātavedā devo devebhyo havyaṃ vahatu prajānan ||
children.translated_text: Here let this other <s>Jātavedas</s>, the god, knowingly carry the oblation to the gods.

children.text: kravyādam agnim iṣito harāmi janān dṛṃhantaṃ vajreṇa mṛtyum
children.translated_text: Impelled, I carry away the <s>kravyād</s> fire, death that fastens men with a thunderbolt.

children.text: ni taṃ śāsmi gārhapatyena vidvān pitṝṇāṃ loke 'pi bhāgo astu ||
children.translated_text: Knowing, I restrain him with the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire); let there be a share also in the world of the Fathers.

children.text: kravyādam agniṃ śaśamānam ukthyaṃ prahiṇomi pathibhiḥ pitṛyāṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: I send the <s>kravyād</s> fire, praised with recitation, along the paths that go to the Fathers.

children.text: mā devayānaiḥ punar āgā atraivaidhi pitṛṣu jāgṛhi tvam ||
children.translated_text: Do not come back by the paths that go to the gods; remain right there, and keep watch among the Fathers.

children.text: samindhate saṃkasukaṃ svastaye śuddhā bhavantaḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāḥ
children.translated_text: They kindle <s>Saṃkasuka</s> for well-being, becoming clean, bright, and purifying.

children.text: jahāti ripram aty ena eti samiddho agniḥ supunā punāti ||
children.translated_text: He leaves defilement behind and passes beyond it; kindled, <s>Agni</s>, a good purifier, purifies.

children.text: devo agniḥ saṃkasuko divas pṛṣṭhāny āruhat
children.translated_text: The god <s>Agni Saṃkasuka</s> has climbed the backs of heaven.

children.text: mucyamāno nir enaso 'mog asmāṁ aśastyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Being released from sin, release us from ill repute.

children.text: asmin vayaṃ saṃkasuke agnau riprāṇi mṛjmahe
children.translated_text: In this <s>Saṃkasuka</s> fire we wipe off our defilements.

children.text: abhūma yajñiyāḥ śuddhāḥ pra ṇa āyūṃṣi tāriṣat ||
children.translated_text: We have become fit for sacrifice and pure; may he carry our lifetimes onward.

children.text: saṃkasuko vikasuko nirṛtho yaś ca nisvaraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃkasuka</s>, <s>Vikasuka</s>, <s>Nirṛtha</s>, and the voiceless one,

children.text: te te yakṣmaṃ savedaso dūrād dūram anīnaśan ||
children.translated_text: those, sharing one knowledge, have driven your <s>yakṣma</s> farther and farther away.

children.text: yo no aśveṣu vīreṣu yo no goṣv ajāviṣu
children.translated_text: Whatever is among our horses and heroes, whatever among our cattle, goats, and sheep,

children.text: kravyādaṃ nirṇudāmasi yo agnir janayopanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: we drive out the <s>kravyād</s> fire that comes near the people.

children.text: anyebhyas tvā puruṣebhyo gobhyo aśvebhyas tvā
children.translated_text: From other men we drive you, from cattle we drive you, from horses we drive you.

children.text: niḥ kravyādaṃ nudāmasi yo agnir jīvitayopanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We thrust out the <s>kravyād</s>, the fire that comes near the living.

children.text: yasmin devā amṛjata yasmin manuṣyā uta
children.translated_text: In that in which the gods wiped themselves clean, and in which men did so too,

children.text: tasmin ghṛtastāvo mṛṣṭvā tvam agne divaṃ ruha ||
children.translated_text: in that, smeared with ghee, having wiped yourself clean, O <s>Agni</s>, climb to heaven.

children.text: samiddho agna āhuta sa no mābhyapakramīḥ
children.translated_text: Kindled and invoked, O <s>Agni</s>, do not go away from us.

children.text: atraiva dīdihi dyavi jyok ca sūryaṃ dṛśe ||
children.translated_text: Shine right here and in heaven, so that we may long see the sun.

children.text: sīse mṛḍḍhvaṃ naḍe mṛḍḍhvam agnau saṃkasuke ca yat
children.translated_text: Cleanse yourselves on the lead; cleanse yourselves on the reed, and on what is in the <s>Saṃkasuka</s> fire,

children.text: atho avyāṃ rāmāyāṃ śīrṣaktim upabarhaṇe ||
children.translated_text: and also on the wool of the dark ewe, on the head-pad and the pillow.

children.text: sīse malaṃ sādayitvā śīrṣaktim upabarhaṇe
children.translated_text: Having set the impurity in the lead and the head-affliction in the pillow,

children.text: avyām asiknyāṃ mṛṣṭvā śuddhā bhavata yajñiyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: having wiped yourselves clean on the wool of the black ewe, become pure and fit for sacrifice.

children.text: paraṃ mṛtyo anu parehi panthāṃ yas ta eṣa itaro devayānāt
children.translated_text: Go away beyond, O <s>Mṛtyu</s>, along that path of yours which is other than the path of the gods.

children.text: cakṣuṣmate śṛṇvate te bravīmīheme vīrā bahavo bhavantu ||
children.translated_text: To you, who see and hear, I say this: let these heroes here become many.

children.text: ime jīvā vi mṛtair āvavṛtrann abhūd bhadrā devahutir no adya
children.translated_text: These living ones have turned away from the dead; today our invocation of the gods has become auspicious.

children.text: prāñco agāma nṛtaye hasāya suvīrāso vidatham ā vadema ||
children.translated_text: Facing forward, we have gone to dancing and laughter; rich in good heroes, may we speak in the assembly.

children.text: imaṃ jīvebhyaḥ paridhiṃ dadhāmi maiṣāṃ nu gād aparo artham etam
children.translated_text: I set this boundary for the living; let none of these now go to that further goal.

children.text: śataṃ jīvantaḥ śaradaḥ purūcīs tiro mṛtyuṃ dadhatām parvatena ||
children.translated_text: Living a hundred abundant autumns, let them place death beyond a mountain.

children.text: ārohatāyur jarasaṃ vṛṇānā anupūrvaṃ yatamānā yati stha
children.translated_text: Ascend to life, choosing old age, striving in order, as many as you are.

children.text: tān vas tvaṣṭā sujanimā sajoṣāḥ sarvam āyur nayatu jīvanāya ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, of good birth and in harmony, lead all your lifetime toward living.

children.text: yathāhāny anupūrvaṃ bhavanti yathartava ṛtubhir yanti sākam
children.translated_text: As days arise one after another, as seasons go together with seasons,

children.text: yathā na pūrvam aparo jahāty evā dhātar āyūṃṣi kalpayaiṣām ||
children.translated_text: as the later does not abandon the former, so, O <s>Dhātṛ</s>, arrange lifetimes for these people.

children.text: aśmanvatī rīyate saṃrabhadhvaṃ vīrayadhvaṃ pra taratā sakhāyaḥ
children.translated_text: A stony stream is flowing; gather yourselves, be heroic, cross over, friends.

children.text: atrā jahīta ye asan durevā anamīvān ut taremābhi vājān ||
children.translated_text: Here leave behind those who were ill-disposed; may we cross beyond, free from sickness, toward the prizes.

children.text: uttiṣṭhatā prataratā sakhāyo 'śmanvatī nadī syandata iyam
children.translated_text: Stand up and cross over, friends; this stony river is flowing.

children.text: atrā jahīta ye asann aśivāḥ śivānt syonān ut taremābhi vājān ||
children.translated_text: Here leave behind those who were inauspicious; may we cross beyond toward auspicious, pleasant prizes.

children.text: vaiśvadevīṃ varcasā ārabhadhvaṃ śuddhā bhavantaḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāḥ
children.translated_text: Take hold of the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> with radiance, becoming clean, bright, and purifying.

children.text: atikrāmanto duritā padāni śataṃ himāḥ sarvavīrā madema ||
children.translated_text: Stepping over the footprints of evil, may we rejoice for a hundred winters, all our heroes with us.

children.text: udīcīnaiḥ pathibhir vāyumadbhir atikrāmanto 'varān parebhiḥ
children.translated_text: By northward, windy paths, crossing beyond the lower ones with the higher,

children.text: triḥ sapta kṛtvarṣayaḥ paretā mṛtyuṃ pratyauhan padayopanena ||
children.translated_text: the seers, having departed three times seven times, drove back death by warding off his footstep.

children.text: mṛtyoḥ padaṃ yopayanta eta drāghīya āyuḥ prataraṃ dadhānāḥ
children.translated_text: Avoiding the footprint of death, these men take on a longer and further-reaching life.

children.text: āsīnā mṛtyuṃ nudatā sadhasthe 'tha jīvāso vidatham āvadema ||
children.translated_text: Sitting in the common seat, drive death away; then, alive, may we speak in the assembly.

children.text: imā nārīr avidhavāḥ supatnīr āñjanena sarpiṣā saṃspṛśantām
children.translated_text: Let these women, not widowed, with good husbands, touch themselves with ointment and ghee;

children.text: anaśravo anamīvāḥ suratnā ārohantu janayo yonim agre ||
children.translated_text: tearless, free from disease, rich in good jewels, let the wives first ascend the womb-place.

children.text: vyākaromi haviṣāham etau tau brahmaṇā vy ahaṃ kalpayāmi
children.translated_text: With oblation I separate these two; with <s>brahman</s> I set them apart.

children.text: svadhāṃ pitṛbhyo ajarāṃ kṛṇomi dīrgheṇāyuṣā sam imānt sṛjāmi ||
children.translated_text: I make unfailing <s>svadhā</s> (ancestral offering) for the <s>Pitṛs</s>; I join these together with long life.

children.text: yo no agniḥ pitaro hṛtsv antar āviveśāmṛto martyeṣu
children.translated_text: That <s>Agni</s> of ours, O <s>Pitṛs</s>, who, immortal, entered within the hearts of mortals,

children.text: mayy ahaṃ taṃ parigṛhṇāmi devaṃ mā so asmān dvikṣata mā vayaṃ tam ||
children.translated_text: I take that god into myself; may he not hate us, nor may we hate him.

children.text: apāvṛtya gārhapatyāt kravyādā preta dakṣiṇā
children.translated_text: Having turned away from the gārhapatya fire, O flesh-eater, go forth to the right;

children.text: priyaṃ pitṛbhya ātmane brahmabhyaḥ kṛṇutā priyam ||
children.translated_text: make what is dear for the <s>Pitṛs</s>, for yourself, and for the sacred formulas; make what is dear.

children.text: dvibhāgadhanam ādāya prakṣiṇāty avartyā
children.translated_text: Having taken the wealth divided into two shares, he circles about without returning;

children.text: agniḥ putrasya jyeṣṭhasya yaḥ kravyād anirāhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, the fire of the eldest son, is the flesh-eater that has not been set aside.

children.text: yat kṛṣate yad vanute yac ca vasnena vindate
children.translated_text: Whatever a mortal plows, whatever he wins, and whatever he obtains by price,

children.text: sarvaṃ martyasya tan nāsti kravyāc ced anirāhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all that does not belong to him if the flesh-eater has not been set aside.

children.text: ayajñiyo hatavarcā bhavati nainena havir attave
children.translated_text: He becomes unfit for sacrifice and deprived of brilliance; the oblation is not to be eaten by him.

children.text: chinatti kṛṣyā gor dhanād yaṃ kravyād anuvartate ||
children.translated_text: The flesh-eater that follows him cuts him off from agriculture, cattle, and wealth.

children.text: muhur gṛdhyaiḥ pravadaty ārtim martyo nītya
children.translated_text: Again and again the mortal speaks to the vultures, having been led to distress,

children.text: kravyād yān agnir antikād anuvidvān vitāvati ||
children.translated_text: when <s>Agni</s>, as flesh-eater, from nearby, knowingly runs after those men.

children.text: grāhyā gṛhāḥ saṃsṛjyante striyā yan mriyate patiḥ
children.translated_text: The houses become liable to seizure when a woman's husband dies;

children.text: brahmaiva vidvān eṣyo yaḥ kravyādaṃ nirādadhat ||
children.translated_text: the true knower of the <s>brahman</s> is the one who should come, who has set aside the flesh-eater.

children.text: yad ripraṃ śamalaṃ cakṛma yac ca duṣkṛtam
children.translated_text: Whatever stain or defilement we have committed, and whatever evil deed,

children.text: āpo mā tasmācchumbhantvagneḥ saṃkasukāc ca yat ||
children.translated_text: may the waters cleanse me from that, and from what belongs to the clinging fire.

children.text: tā adharād udīcīr āvavṛtran prajānatīḥ pathibhir devayānaiḥ
children.translated_text: Those knowing waters have turned from below toward the north, along the god-going paths;

children.text: parvatasya vṛṣabhasyādhi pṛṣṭhe navāś caranti saritaḥ purāṇīḥ ||
children.translated_text: on the back of the mountain's bull the new and ancient rivers move.

children.text: agne akravyān niḥ kravyādaṃ nudā devayajanaṃ vaha ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s> who are not flesh-eating, drive out the flesh-eater; carry the god-sacrificing rite.

children.text: imaṃ kravyād āviveśāyaṃ kravyādam anvagāt
children.translated_text: This flesh-eater entered in; this one has followed after the flesh-eater.

children.text: vyāghrau kṛtvā nānānaṃ taṃ harāmi śivāparam ||
children.translated_text: Having made the two tigers separate, I carry him away to the auspicious farther side.

children.text: antardhir devānāṃ paridhir manuṣyāṇām agnir gārhapatya ubhayān antarā śritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> the gārhapatya, the concealment of the gods and the enclosure of men, has settled between both.

children.text: jīvānām āyuḥ pratira tvam agne pitṝṇāṃ lokam api gacchantu ye mṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the prolonger of the living men's life; let those who have died go also to the world of the <s>Pitṛs</s>.

children.text: sugārhapatyo vitapann arātim uṣāmuṣāṃ śreyasīṃ dhehy asmai ||
children.translated_text: As a good gārhapatya, burning away hostility, place a better dawn after dawn for this man.

children.text: sarvān agne sahamānaḥ sapatnān aiṣām ūrjaṃ rayim asmāsu dhehi ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, overpowering all rivals, place their vigor and wealth among us.

children.text: imam indraṃ vahniṃ paprim anvārabhadhvaṃ sa vo nirvakṣad duritād avadyāt
children.translated_text: Take hold of this <s>Indra</s>, the bearer, the filling one; he will lead you out from trouble and blame.

children.text: tenāpahata śarum āpatantaṃ tena rudrasya paripātāstām ||
children.translated_text: With him strike away the falling arrow; with him may the protections of <s>Rudra</s> stand around you.

children.text: anaḍvāhaṃ plavam anvārabhadhvaṃ sa vo nirvakṣad duritād avadyāt
children.translated_text: Take hold of the ox as a boat; it will lead you out from trouble and blame.

children.text: ārohata savitur nāvam etāṃ ṣaḍbhir urvībhir amatiṃ tarema ||
children.translated_text: Mount this boat of <s>Savitṛ</s>; with the six broad spaces may we cross beyond want of thought.

children.text: ahorātre anveṣi bibhrat kṣemyas tiṣṭhan prataraṇaḥ suvīraḥ
children.translated_text: Following day and night, bearing security, standing firm as a crossing, rich in heroes,

children.text: anāturānt sumanasas talpa bibhraj jyog eva naḥ puruṣagandhir edhi ||
children.translated_text: free from sickness, kindly in mind, bearing a couch, be long fragrant with human presence for us.

children.text: te devebhya āvṛścante pāpaṃ jīvanti sarvadā
children.translated_text: They are cut off from the gods and live in evil at all times,

children.text: kravyād yān agnir antikād aśva ivānuvapate naḍam ||
children.translated_text: when <s>Agni</s>, as flesh-eater, from nearby scatters them like a horse scattering reeds.

children.text: ye 'śraddhā dhanakāmyā kravyādā samāsate
children.translated_text: Those who, faithless and desiring wealth, sit together with the flesh-eating fires,

children.text: te vā anyeṣāṃ kumbhīṃ paryādadhati sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: they indeed keep setting another's pot around themselves at all times.

children.text: preva pipatiṣati manasā muhur āvartate punaḥ
children.translated_text: With his mind he almost falls forward; again and again he turns back once more,

children.text: kravyād yān agnir antikād anuvidvān vitāvati ||
children.translated_text: when <s>Agni</s>, as flesh-eater, from nearby, knowingly runs after those men.

children.text: aviḥ kṛṣṇā bhāgadheyaṃ paśūnāṃ sīsaṃ kravyād api candraṃ ta āhuḥ
children.translated_text: A black ewe is the assigned share among animals; lead, and even bright metal, they call yours, O flesh-eater.

children.text: māṣāḥ piṣṭā bhāgadheyaṃ te havyam araṇyānyā gahvaraṃ sacasva ||
children.translated_text: Ground beans are your assigned share, your oblation; attach yourself to the wilderness, to the thicket.

children.text: iṣīkāṃ jaratīm iṣṭvā tilpiñjaṃ daṇḍanaṃ naḍam
children.translated_text: Having sacrificed an aged reed, tilpiñja grass, a staff, and reed,

children.text: tam indra idhmam kṛtvā yamasyāgniṃ nirādadhau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, making that the fuel, set aside <s>Yama</s>'s fire.

children.text: pratyañcam arkaṃ pratyarpayitvā pravidvān panthāṃ vi hy āviveśa
children.translated_text: Having turned the sunward chant back in the opposite direction, the wise one entered upon the path;

children.text: parāmīṣām asūn dideśa dīrgheṇāyuṣā sam imānt sṛjāmi ||
children.translated_text: he directed their life-breaths away; I join these together with long life.

children.text: Chapter 471
pumān puṃso 'dhitiṣṭha carmehi tatra hvayasva yatamā priyā te
children.translated_text: Man, stand upon the man's hide; come here and call there to what is dearest to you.

children.text: yāvantāv agre prathamaṃ sameyathus tad vāṃ vayo yamarājye samānam ||
children.translated_text: As far as you two first came together at the beginning, so may the span of life be the same for you two in <s>Yama</s>'s kingdom.

children.text: tāvad vāṃ cakṣus tati vīryāṇi tāvat tejas tatidhā vājināni
children.translated_text: So far may your sight extend, so far your powers, so far your brilliance, and so many your vigorous strengths.

children.text: agniḥ śarīraṃ sacate yadaidho 'dhā pakvān mithunā saṃbhavāthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Agni</s> as fuel joins the body, then, cooked, you two shall arise as a pair.

children.text: sam asmiṃlloke sam u devayāne saṃ smā sametaṃ yamarājyeṣu
children.translated_text: Together in this world, together also on the god-going path, may you two be assembled together in the kingdoms of <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: pūtau pavitrair upa taddhvayethāṃ yadyad reto adhi vāṃ saṃbabhūva ||
children.translated_text: Purified by purifiers, call upon that which of your seed has been produced between you two.

children.text: āpas putrāso abhisaṃviśadhvam imaṃ jīvaṃ jīvadhanyāḥ sametya
children.translated_text: Waters, sons, enter together; meeting this living one, rich in living sustenance,

children.text: tāsāṃ bhajadhvam amṛtaṃ yam āhur odanaṃ pacati vāṃ janitrī ||
children.translated_text: share in their immortal thing, which they call the cooked rice that your mother cooks for you two.

children.text: yaṃ vāṃ pitā pacati yaṃ ca mātā riprān nirmuktyai śamalāc ca vācaḥ
children.translated_text: That which your father cooks for you two, and which your mother cooks, for release from stains, defilement, and speech,

children.text: sa odanaḥ śatadhāraḥ svarga ubhe vyāpa nabhasī mahitvā ||
children.translated_text: that cooked rice, having a hundred streams, in heaven, has filled both heavens by its greatness.

children.text: ubhe nabhasī ubhayāṃś ca lokān ye yajvanām abhijitāḥ svargāḥ
children.translated_text: Both heavens, and both kinds of worlds, the heavenly realms won by sacrificers,

children.text: teṣāṃ jyotiṣmān madhumān yo agre tasmin putrair jarasi saṃśrayethām ||
children.translated_text: the luminous, honeyed one that is foremost among them: in that may you two take refuge with sons in old age.

children.text: prācīṃ prācīṃ pradiśam ārabhethām etaṃ lokaṃ śraddadhānāḥ sacante
children.translated_text: Take hold of the eastern direction, farther and farther east; those who have faith attend upon this world.

children.text: yad vāṃ pakvaṃ pariviṣṭam agnau tasya guptaye daṃpatī saṃśrayethām ||
children.translated_text: For the guarding of what has been cooked for you two and set around in the fire, may you two, husband and wife, take refuge in it.

children.text: dakṣiṇāṃ diśam abhi nakṣamāṇau paryāvartethām abhi pātram etat
children.translated_text: Turning toward the southern direction, marking it out, may you two turn around toward this vessel.

children.text: tasmin vāṃ yamaḥ pitṛbhiḥ saṃvidānaḥ pakvāya śarma bahulaṃ niyacchāt ||
children.translated_text: In that, may <s>Yama</s>, in agreement with the <s>Pitṛs</s>, assign abundant shelter for the cooked offering to you two.

children.text: pratīcī diśām iyam id varaṃ yasyāṃ somo adhipā mṛḍitā ca
children.translated_text: This western quarter is indeed the best of the directions, in which <s>Soma</s> is overlord and gracious.

children.text: tasyāṃ śrayethāṃ sukṛtaḥ sacethām adhā pakvān mithunā saṃbhavāthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In that quarter may you two take refuge; may you two join with what has been well done; then may you two come together as a pair among the cooked offerings.

children.text: uttaraṃ rāṣṭraṃ prajayottarāvad diśām udīcī kṛṇavan no agram
children.translated_text: May the northern realm, rich in progeny and superior, make the northern direction our foremost one among the directions.

children.text: pāṅktaṃ chandaḥ puruṣo babhūva viśvair viśvāṅgaiḥ saha sambhavema ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Pankti</s> metre became the Person; may we come into being with all, together with all our limbs.

children.text: dhruveyaṃ virāṇ namo astv asyai śivā putrebhya uta mahyam astu
children.translated_text: This fixed <s>Virāj</s>: homage be to her; may she be auspicious for the sons and also for me.

children.text: sā no devy adite viśvavāra irya iva gopā abhirakṣa pakvam ||
children.translated_text: May that goddess <s>Aditi</s>, choice-worthy for all, protect our cooked offering like a herdsman guarding the flock.

children.text: piteva putrān abhisaṃsvajasva naḥ śivā no vātā iha vāntu bhūmau
children.translated_text: Embrace us as a father embraces his sons; may auspicious winds blow for us here upon the earth.

children.text: yam odanaṃ pacato devate iha taṃ nas tapa uta satyaṃ ca vettu ||
children.translated_text: The <s>odana</s> (cooked rice offering) which the two deities cook here: may austerity and truth recognize it for us.
